## 50 Best Manhwa of All Time — Korean Comics That Changed Everything


*Reading time: ~14 min | Category: Rankings | Tags: best manhwa, top manhwa list, Korean webtoons, manhwa recommendations*

---

### Introduction

If you're still treating manhwa as "manga but Korean," you're missing the point entirely. In the last decade, Korean manhwa — particularly in the webtoon format — has built its own distinct visual language, its own storytelling conventions, and its own phenomenally dedicated global readership. Some of the most-read comics on the planet right now are Korean.

What makes manhwa special? A few things. The vertical scroll format, perfected for smartphones, changes the pacing of how stories are told. The color art is almost universally stunning — Korean artists have developed a house style that prioritizes lush, expressive coloring over the ink-heavy monochrome of traditional manga. And the genres manhwa has dominated — isekai regression, villainess romance, dungeon fantasy, murim martial arts — are ones that Japanese manga only partly covered.

This list ranks the 50 best manhwa ever made. It includes both print manhwa and webtoons. It skews toward completed or long-running series with proven staying power. And it's unapologetically opinionated.

---

### What Sets Great Manhwa Apart?

Criteria for this list:

- **Narrative construction** — Manhwa has a reputation for slow starts and payoff-heavy mid-sections. The best ones nail their hooks early and keep building.
- **Art and color design** — Manhwa's strongest asset. We ranked works that use color expressively, not just decoratively.
- **Genre execution** — Did it actually do something new with its genre, or was it a competent retread?
- **Character work** — Protagonists and antagonists who feel real and evolve meaningfully.
- **Reader retention** — Did people keep coming back chapter after chapter?

---

### 50–41: Starting Strong

**50. The God of High School** — Yongje Park's tournament fighter is exactly what the cover promises: high-octane martial arts with escalating stakes. The mythological elements in later arcs are divisive, but the early tournament chapters are elite action content.
[Read The God of High School](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-god-of-high-school)

**49. Noblesse** — The granddaddy of manhwa action. A noble vampire awakens in modern Korea after 820 years and navigates high school while secretly being one of the most powerful beings alive. The slow-burn power reveals are deeply satisfying.
[Read Noblesse](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/noblesse)

**48. Ability** — An underrated manhwa about a young man who inherits supernatural abilities. The character development is stronger than most of its genre peers, and the action choreography is clean and readable.
[Read Ability](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/ability)

**47. Eleceed** — A cat who is secretly a powerful esper, a boy with super reflexes, and a found-family of awakened fighters. Jaehyun and Kayden's dynamic is one of the most charming in action manhwa.
[Read Eleceed](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/eleceed)

**46. Nano Machine** — Cultivation meets nanotechnology. A descendant of the Heavenly Demon receives a nano machine from the future and begins his climb through the murim world. Supremely satisfying power fantasy with good pacing.
[Read Nano Machine](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/nano-machine)

**45. A Returner's Magic Should Be Special** — Desir Herrman survives a Shadow Labyrinth and returns to the past to change everything. The magic academy setting, the strategic battles, and the emotional weight of knowing what's coming — this one consistently delivers.
[Read A Returner's Magic Should Be Special](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/a-returners-magic-should-be-special)

**44. The Beginning After the End** — Arthur Leywin, a reincarnated king, grows up in a fantasy world with all his past-life skills intact. The coming-of-age structure is handled unusually well for the genre, and the world-building is among the best in manhwa.
[Read The Beginning After the End](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-beginning-after-the-end)

**43. My Hero Academia (manhwa spiritual successors)** — Rather than one title, this slot goes to **Wind Breaker** by Jo Yongseok, a delinquent action manhwa with MHA-level heart and a unique cycling backdrop.
[Read Wind Breaker](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/wind-breaker)

**42. Teenage Mercenary (Mercenary Enrollment)** — Ijin Yu returns to civilian life after years as a child mercenary abroad. His protective instincts, his difficulty with normal social situations, and the action sequences that erupt whenever someone threatens his family — this manhwa earns every emotional beat.
[Read Teenage Mercenary](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/teenage-mercenary)

**41. True Beauty** — Yaongyi's romance webtoon about a girl who becomes popular through makeup mastery is a social media phenomenon for good reason. The art is gorgeous, the love triangle is genuinely agonizing, and it handles social anxiety and beauty standards with surprising sincerity.
[Read True Beauty](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/true-beauty)

---

### 40–31: The Proven Performers

**40. I Love Yoo** — Quimchee's slice-of-life romance webtoon is a slow build with extraordinary character depth. The relationships feel authentic in a way that many webtoon romances don't quite achieve.
[Read I Love Yoo](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/i-love-yoo)

**39. Lookism** — Park Taejon's webtoon about a bullied teenager who wakes up able to switch between his original body and a handsome one tackles appearance, class, violence, and identity with remarkable complexity. It spawned an entire universe of spinoffs.
[Read Lookism](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/lookism)

**38. UnOrdinary** — A world where everyone has supernatural abilities except John. Except John isn't what he seems. uru-chan's webtoon is a slow burn that eventually detonates into one of the most emotionally charged sequences in webtoon history.
[Read UnOrdinary](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/unordinary)

**37. The Remarried Empress** — Political scheming, a cold but competent empress, and a story about what happens after a bad marriage is ended. One of the defining titles in the empress/nobility romance subgenre.
[Read The Remarried Empress](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-remarried-empress)

**36. I'm the Villain's Daughter but I Wanna Be Normal** — The villainess genre gets a comedic subversion here. The protagonist knows she's in an otome game and wants no part of the original plot. Light, fun, but smarter than it looks.
[Read I'm the Villain's Daughter](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/im-the-villains-daughter)

**35. Lore Olympus** — Rachel Smythe's Webtoon retelling of the Hades and Persephone myth is arguably the most mainstream successful webtoon in the West. The pastel color palette and emotional rawness made it a phenomenon.
[Read Lore Olympus](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/lore-olympus)

**34. Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint** — A reader of a web novel finds himself inside the novel he spent years reading. The meta-narrative, the emotional investment in characters the reader already loves, and the absolutely brutal consequences when things go wrong — ORV is special.
[Read Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/omniscient-readers-viewpoint)

**33. Second Life Ranker** — Yeon-woo enters a tower to avenge his dead brother and uses the diary his brother left to advance through floors his brother already mapped. The layered power progression and revenge narrative are perfectly calibrated.
[Read Second Life Ranker](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/second-life-ranker)

**32. Return of the Blossoming Blade** — A brilliant murim manhwa with one of the best regression setups in the genre. The protagonist's relationships in his second life carry real emotional weight because we know what he lost.
[Read Return of the Blossoming Blade](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/return-of-the-blossoming-blade)

**31. Viral Hit (How to Fight)** — Hobin Yoo, a scrawny kid who gets bullied, starts a YouTube channel teaching unconventional fighting techniques. The social media commentary runs alongside genuinely creative fight choreography.
[Read Viral Hit](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/viral-hit)

---

### 30–21: The Elite Tier

**30. Dungeon Reset** — After a dungeon resets and traps him outside the normal progression, Dawoon Jung has to survive using construction and crafting skills the game system wasn't designed for. Clever, funny, and deeply satisfying.
[Read Dungeon Reset](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/dungeon-reset)

**29. Mookyhim** — Raw combat, a protagonist with no supernatural gifts and just sheer bloody-minded determination, and one of the most grounded martial arts progressions in manhwa.
[Read Mookyhim](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/mookyhim)

**28. The Live** — A father who died returns to a brutal survival game for the chance to see his daughter again. The emotional stakes are exceptional, and the survival mechanics are well-constructed.
[Read The Live](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-live)

**27. Her Summon** — Fantasy romance with a genuine sense of danger and a protagonist who earns her power rather than inheriting it.
[Read Her Summon](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/her-summon)

**26. I Reincarnated as the Crazed Heir** — Political scheming in a historical Korean fantasy setting. The protagonist's unpredictable behavior — played as insanity but actually calculated — is one of manhwa's most fun conceits.
[Read I Reincarnated as the Crazed Heir](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/i-reincarnated-as-the-crazed-heir)

**25. The Scholar's Reincarnation** — A powerful martial artist reincarnates into a scholar's body and tries to live peacefully while being quietly one of the most dangerous people on earth. Charming and funny.
[Read The Scholar's Reincarnation](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-scholars-reincarnation)

**24. Doctor's Rebirth** — A doctor from modern Korea reincarnates into a murim novel he was reading. The medical knowledge meets martial arts world angle is fresh and consistently entertaining.
[Read Doctor's Rebirth](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/doctors-rebirth)

**23. SSS-Class Suicide Hunter** — Kim Gongja has the ability to copy the skill of whoever kills him and respawn 24 hours earlier. What that does to a person — psychologically — is explored with unusual depth.
[Read SSS-Class Suicide Hunter](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/sss-class-suicide-hunter)

**22. The World After the Fall** — Hardcore regression/tower manhwa with a protagonist whose ideology is distinctive: Jaehwan refuses to regress with the rest of humanity and chooses to keep moving forward no matter what. One of the most philosophically interesting manhwa in the genre.
[Read The World After the Fall](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-world-after-the-fall)

**21. My Dress-Up Darling** — Technically manga, but its enormous manhwa-adjacent audience earns it a note here. The genuine respect for cosplay craft and the romantic chemistry between Wakana and Marin are second to none.
[Read My Dress-Up Darling](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/my-dress-up-darling)

---

### Top 20: The Manhwa Legends

**20. Bastard** — A psychological horror manhwa about a boy whose father is a serial killer. Youngchan Hwang's work is relentlessly tense and morally complex.
[Read Bastard](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/bastard)

**19. Weak Hero** — Gray Yeon is scrawny, physically unremarkable, and completely terrifying in a fight because he fights like a mathematician. The delinquent genre has never produced a protagonist quite like him.
[Read Weak Hero](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/weak-hero)

**18. Sweet Home** — Before the Netflix adaptation, Carnby Kim's horror manhwa was already a phenomenon. Humans transform into monsters based on their deepest desires. The survivors in an apartment complex try to hold on to what's left of their humanity.
[Read Sweet Home](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/sweet-home)

**17. Tower of God** — SIU's vertical fantasy epic about Bam climbing a mysterious tower to find his only friend is one of the longest-running and most complex manhwa in existence. The world-building is extraordinary.
[Read Tower of God](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/tower-of-god)

**16. The Breaker** — The murim manhwa that proved Korean action comics could match Japanese manga blow for blow. Chunwoo's teaching of Shiho is one of the best mentor-student dynamics in the genre.
[Read The Breaker](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-breaker)

**15. Killing Stalking** — A psychological thriller/dark romance that sparked enormous controversy and equally enormous readership. Not a healthy romance — but an unflinching portrait of obsession and trauma that demands serious consideration as a work of craft.
[Read Killing Stalking](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/killing-stalking)

**14. Like Wind on a Dry Branch** — Historical romance manhwa with exceptional art and a slow-burn romance between an empress and a man who has every reason to despise her.
[Read Like Wind on a Dry Branch](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/like-wind-on-a-dry-branch)

**13. Return of the Mount Hua Sect** — One of the best murim manhwa ever made. A peak-era swordsman reincarnates as the weakest disciple of his former sect and has to rebuild both himself and the sect's glory. Funny, emotionally resonant, and spectacularly drawn.
[Read Return of the Mount Hua Sect](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/return-of-the-mount-hua-sect)

**12. Distant Sky** — A beautifully illustrated apocalyptic manhwa that follows survivors in an underground Seoul after the sky disappears. The art is some of the most stunning in all of manhwa.
[Read Distant Sky](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/distant-sky)

**11. I Am the Sorcerer King** — Tower dungeon fighting, an overpowered protagonist whose power is revealed gradually, and one of the most satisfying escalation arcs in Korean fantasy comics.
[Read I Am the Sorcerer King](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/i-am-the-sorcerer-king)

**10. Hardcore Leveling Warrior** — The first player to be de-ranked to level 1 fights back to the top. The game world is intricate, the character growth is earned, and the emotional payoffs are enormous.
[Read Hardcore Leveling Warrior](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/hardcore-leveling-warrior)

**9. The God of High School** *(elevated)* — Park Yongje's tournament masterpiece earns its top-10 spot through sheer kinetic energy and mythological ambition.
[Read The God of High School](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-god-of-high-school)

**8. Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint** *(elevated)* — The most emotionally complex regression manhwa ever written. The relationship between Dokja and Jonghyuk is one of the most interesting dynamics in modern manhwa.
[Read Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/omniscient-readers-viewpoint)

**7. Lookism** *(elevated)* — The social commentary, the universe-building, and the sheer ambition of turning a webtoon about appearance into a full crime/action thriller universe makes Lookism one of the defining works of Korean comics.
[Read Lookism](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/lookism)

**6. Sweet Home** *(elevated)* — The monster designs, the character psychology, the emotional weight of watching people choose between their humanity and their survival — Sweet Home is a horror masterpiece.
[Read Sweet Home](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/sweet-home)

**5. Tower of God** *(elevated)* — Decades of world-building, a protagonist who subverts every expectation, and a mythological scale that no other manhwa has attempted.
[Read Tower of God](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/tower-of-god)

**4. Weak Hero** *(elevated)* — The cleanest, most satisfying delinquent action manhwa in existence. Gray Yeon is a genuinely iconic protagonist.
[Read Weak Hero](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/weak-hero)

**3. Return of the Mount Hua Sect** *(elevated)* — Perfect murim storytelling. The balance between comedy, action, emotional resonance, and world-building is something most manhwa never achieve.
[Read Return of the Mount Hua Sect](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/return-of-the-mount-hua-sect)

**2. Solo Leveling** — The manhwa that mainstreamed the genre globally. Sung Jinwoo goes from the world's weakest hunter to its absolute apex. The dungeon art, the shadow army, the final boss — Solo Leveling is the gateway manhwa for millions of readers.
[Read Solo Leveling](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/solo-leveling)

**1. Solo Leveling / Tower of God (tie)** — Depending on whether you weight emotional depth (Tower of God) or cultural impact and reading experience (Solo Leveling), either could claim the top spot. Both are essential. Both are mandatory reading.

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the best manhwa to start with?**
Solo Leveling. It's fast, visually stunning, and accessible. Then move to Tower of God for something deeper.

**Q: Is manhwa different from webtoons?**
Manhwa is the Korean word for comics. Webtoons are a digital format (vertical scroll, color). Most modern manhwa is published as webtoons.

**Q: Are there completed manhwa worth reading?**
Yes — Noblesse, Bastard, Killing Stalking, and Return of the Mount Hua Sect are all complete or near-complete.

## 30 Best Manhua of All Time — Chinese Comics Worth Your Time


*Reading time: ~10 min | Category: Rankings | Tags: best manhua, Chinese comics, xianxia manhua, cultivation comics*

---

### Introduction

Manhua — Chinese comics — occupy a fascinating middle ground in the East Asian comics landscape. They share visual DNA with manhwa (color, vertical scroll, digital-first publishing), but their thematic DNA is entirely their own. Cultivation, wuxia, reincarnation into xianxia novels, immortal sects, pill refining, spiritual roots — these are concepts that grew organically from Chinese literary tradition, specifically the wuxia and xianxia web novel genre that exploded in China in the 2000s and 2010s.

The manhua scene has had a complicated journey to international recognition. Translation quality was inconsistent for years. Distribution was scattered. And the sheer volume — China produces an enormous amount of comics — made it hard to separate the genuinely exceptional from the competent-but-generic.

But the best manhua is genuinely world-class. If you haven't explored it, this list is your starting point.

---

### 30–21: The Essential Reads

**30. The Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation (Mo Dao Zu Shi)** — Based on MXTX's beloved novel, this manhua adaptation follows Wei Wuxian, a demonic cultivator who is reincarnated and must work alongside his once-sworn enemy to solve a supernatural mystery. The relationship between Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji is one of fiction's great slow burns.
[Read Mo Dao Zu Shi](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/mo-dao-zu-shi)

**29. The Scum Villain's Self-Saving System (Ren Zha Fanpai Zijiu Xitong)** — Another MXTX adaptation. A reader is transmigrated into the body of the villain of a cultivation novel he hated, and has to survive while the system forces him to play the role. Meta, funny, and genuinely touching.
[Read Scum Villain's Self-Saving System](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/scum-villains-self-saving-system)

**28. Martial Peak** — One of the longest-running and most popular cultivation manhua globally. Yang Kai's climb from the bottom of his sect to the peak of the martial world is enormously satisfying if you're in the mood for a long journey.
[Read Martial Peak](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/martial-peak)

**27. Battle Through the Heavens** — Xiao Yan was a genius, then lost his cultivation, then begins a new climb. The Dou Qi system is one of the cleaner power structures in manhua and the action is reliably kinetic.
[Read Battle Through the Heavens](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/battle-through-the-heavens)

**26. Soul Land (Douluo Dalu)** — Tang San reincarnates into the Soul Land world with the forbidden knowledge of his previous life as a Tang Sect disciple. The spirit beast system, the Shrek Academy setting, and the ensemble cast make this an enduring classic.
[Read Soul Land](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/soul-land)

**25. Tales of Demons and Gods** — Nie Li, the strongest Demon Spiritualist in a past life, is reborn as a teenager and uses his future knowledge to change fate. A foundational reincarnation manhua.
[Read Tales of Demons and Gods](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/tales-of-demons-and-gods)

**24. The King's Avatar** — Ye Xiu, a legendary pro gamer forced out of competition, returns using a new account to reclaim his title. The gaming sequences are the most technically detailed in esports manhua.
[Read The King's Avatar](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-kings-avatar)

**23. Perfect World** — Shi Hao is a divine child who must travel to higher realms to challenge fate. The scale of the manhua — from village to cosmic — is matched by some of the most visually ambitious art in the genre.
[Read Perfect World](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/perfect-world)

**22. Apotheosis (Bai Lian Cheng Shen)** — Luo Zheng becomes a slave after his family's fall, but discovers his body contains something extraordinary. The power escalation here is among the fastest and most satisfying in manhua.
[Read Apotheosis](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/apotheosis)

**21. I Shall Seal the Heavens (Wo Yu Feng Tian)** — Based on Er Gen's legendary novel. Meng Hao enters the Reliance Sect and begins a cultivation journey that spans lifetimes and heavens. The emotional depth in the later arcs is extraordinary.
[Read I Shall Seal the Heavens](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/i-shall-seal-the-heavens)

---

### 20–11: The Cream of the Crop

**20. Spare Me, Great Lord!** — Lu Shu awakens in a world undergoing spiritual energy recovery. His passive power — gaining points from people's distress reactions to him — is one of manhua's most original conceits, and the comedy lands.
[Read Spare Me, Great Lord!](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/spare-me-great-lord)

**19. A Will Eternal** — Bai Xiaochun desperately wants to live forever and is terrified of dying. This produces a protagonist unlike any other in cultivation: cowardly, selfish, funny, and yet genuinely admirable in the moments that matter.
[Read A Will Eternal](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/a-will-eternal)

**18. Against the Gods** — Yun Che, a man betrayed and killed, reincarnates in the body of a crippled boy and carries a mysterious jade — the Sky Poison Pearl. An operatically scaled cultivation revenge saga.
[Read Against the Gods](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/against-the-gods)

**17. Star Martial God Technique** — Ye Xinghe's path in the world of martial arts, governed by stars and their powers. One of the more elegant cultivation systems in manhua.
[Read Star Martial God Technique](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/star-martial-god-technique)

**16. Wu Dong Qian Kun (Martial Movement Upheaval)** — Lin Dong's journey from a small town boy to a supreme powerhouse in the world of martial arts, with Yuan Power and Symbol Masters making up the unique cultivation system.
[Read Wu Dong Qian Kun](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/wu-dong-qian-kun)

**15. Swallowed Star** — Luo Feng, a young martial artist, survives a monster apocalypse and climbs from Earth's defender to cosmic legend. The scope expansion — from Earth to the universe — is handled unusually well.
[Read Swallowed Star](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/swallowed-star)

**14. Doupo Cangqiong (Fights Break Sphere)** — Same universe as Battle Through the Heavens, broader scope. An exceptional cultivation epic in its own right.
[Read Doupo Cangqiong](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/doupo-cangqiong)

**13. Heaven Defying Sword** — Xuan Tian's sword cultivation journey is marked by exceptional fight choreography and one of the cleanest sword-focused power systems in the genre.
[Read Heaven Defying Sword](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/heaven-defying-sword)

**12. Peerless Martial God** — Lin Feng is expelled from his sect and begins a path of absolute revenge. The power fantasy is delivered with unusual commitment.
[Read Peerless Martial God](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/peerless-martial-god)

**11. Forty Millenniums of Cultivation** — A sci-fi/cultivation crossover. Li Yao wants to be a Cultivator in a future where cultivation and technology coexist. Unusually intelligent and grounded for the genre.
[Read Forty Millenniums of Cultivation](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/forty-millenniums-of-cultivation)

---

### Top 10: The Best Manhua Ever Made

**10. The Ravages of Time (Fire Phoenix)** — A brilliant strategic manhua set in the Three Kingdoms era. The historical scope and chess-game plotting are unmatched.
[Read The Ravages of Time](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-ravages-of-time)

**9. Soul Land 3: The Legend of the Dragon King** — Tang Wulin's quest to unify humanity in a world of Soul Masters is the best of the Soul Land sequels, with expanded world-building and more emotionally complex character dynamics.
[Read Soul Land 3](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/soul-land-3)

**8. Martial Peak** *(elevated)* — The sheer scope and longevity of Yang Kai's journey earns its top-10 place.
[Read Martial Peak](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/martial-peak)

**7. Battle Through the Heavens** *(elevated)* — The foundational xianxia manhua. Everything that followed owes it a debt.
[Read Battle Through the Heavens](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/battle-through-the-heavens)

**6. The Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation** *(elevated)* — The character work, the slow-burn romance, the mystery plotting — MXTX adaptations earn literary consideration, not just genre consideration.
[Read Mo Dao Zu Shi](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/mo-dao-zu-shi)

**5. I Shall Seal the Heavens** *(elevated)* — Er Gen's novel deserves every star. The manhua honors it.
[Read I Shall Seal the Heavens](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/i-shall-seal-the-heavens)

**4. Soul Land** *(elevated)* — Tang San's journey is one of manhua's most complete protagonist arcs.
[Read Soul Land](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/soul-land)

**3. The King's Avatar** *(elevated)* — The best esports manhua ever made, and one of the best sports narratives in comics period.
[Read The King's Avatar](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-kings-avatar)

**2. Tales of Demons and Gods** *(elevated)* — The manhua that introduced millions of Western readers to Chinese cultivation comics.
[Read Tales of Demons and Gods](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/tales-of-demons-and-gods)

**1. Mo Dao Zu Shi / The Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation** — For sheer craft — art, narrative structure, emotional complexity, and cultural significance — Mo Dao Zu Shi sits at the top. It's the manhua that proved Chinese comics could achieve literary status.
[Read Mo Dao Zu Shi](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/mo-dao-zu-shi)

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the difference between manhua and manhwa?**
Manhua = Chinese comics. Manhwa = Korean comics. Both are often published as vertical-scroll color webtoons but have distinct genre traditions.

**Q: Is cultivation manhua similar to isekai manhwa?**
They overlap — both feature protagonists growing in power in a fantasy world — but cultivation manhua has its own specific genre vocabulary: spiritual roots, dantian, pill refining, immortal realms.

**Q: Where should I start with manhua?**
Tales of Demons and Gods or Battle Through the Heavens. Both are foundational, both are accessible.

---

## 50 Best Webtoons You Should Read Right Now


*Reading time: ~13 min | Category: Rankings | Tags: best webtoons, top webtoons, webtoon recommendations, webtoon list 2026*

---

### Introduction

The word "webtoon" technically just means a comic published in a vertical scroll digital format. But it's become something more than a format — it's a cultural ecosystem. Webtoon (the platform) and its competitors have produced some of the most-read comics on Earth, and the webtoon aesthetic — full color, smartphone-optimized, emotionally intense, with dramatic panel compositions that use the scroll itself as a pacing device — is now its own visual language.

This list pulls from across platforms: Webtoon, Tapas, Manta, Lezhin, KakaoPage, and others. It includes romance, fantasy, action, horror, and slice-of-life, because the best webtoons work across every genre.

One thing you'll notice: the webtoon format rewards emotional storytelling. The color palette, the music that often accompanies episodes on the platform, the chapter length designed for a single sitting — everything points toward maximum emotional impact. The best webtoons understand this and use it ruthlessly.

Here are the 50 best.

---

### 50–41: Must-Read Webtoons

**50. I Love Yoo** — Quimchee's slow-build romance/slice-of-life is a masterclass in authentic character writing. Scheherazade Yoo's deadpan voice and layered emotional life make this one of the most re-readable webtoons on the platform.
[Read I Love Yoo](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/i-love-yoo)

**49. SubZero** — A politically arranged marriage between the last princess of the Azure Dragon Clan and the Crown Prince of the Red Dragon Clan. The enemies-to-lovers dynamic is one of the most well-executed in romance webtoons.
[Read SubZero](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/subzero)

**48. Boyfriend of the Dead** — A zombie apocalypse romance between a human girl and a zombie who retained his intelligence. The comedy is sharp, the emotional core is genuine, and the art is deceptively expressive.
[Read Boyfriend of the Dead](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/boyfriend-of-the-dead)

**47. Always Human** — A near-future slice-of-life LGBTQ+ romance. Ari and Sunati's relationship feels genuinely real. The colour work is gorgeous. One of the most wholesome completed webtoons on the platform.
[Read Always Human](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/always-human)

**46. Space Boy** — Amy, a girl who grew up in a mining colony in the far reaches of the universe, moves to Earth and finds herself pulled into a mystery involving an amnesiac boy with no emotions. The sci-fi romance is beautifully constructed.
[Read Space Boy](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/space-boy)

**45. My Giant Nerd Boyfriend** — A slice-of-life comedy about life with a very tall, very geeky boyfriend. Short, sweet, and genuinely funny — the kind of webtoon you share with everyone you know.
[Read My Giant Nerd Boyfriend](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/my-giant-nerd-boyfriend)

**44. Hooky** — Witch siblings who missed their first day of magical school and have to navigate a world where humans and magical beings are in conflict. The story starts light and gets progressively darker — in the best way.
[Read Hooky](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/hooky)

**43. Flow** — An environmental thriller webtoon with some of the most striking nature-based artwork in the medium. The story asks hard questions about humanity's relationship with the natural world.
[Read Flow](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/flow)

**42. Eaternal Nocturnal** — A boy who sleeps all day befriends a girl who only appears at night. The visual metaphor of day versus night carrying the weight of their very different emotional worlds is beautifully executed.
[Read Eaternal Nocturnal](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/eaternal-nocturnal)

**41. Cursed Princess Club** — A princess who doesn't fit the conventional mold discovers the Cursed Princess Club — a group of similarly "cursed" women. A genuine, funny, and heartfelt story about self-acceptance.
[Read Cursed Princess Club](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/cursed-princess-club)

---

### 40–31: The Next Level

**40. Eleceed** — Already mentioned in the manhwa list, it deserves a webtoon-specific shout. The color palette, the cat-shifter character design, and the kinetic fight sequences all benefit enormously from the full-color format.
[Read Eleceed](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/eleceed)

**39. Castle Swimmer** — A beacon born to fulfill prophecies meets the prince destined to kill him. The aquatic world design is among the most imaginative in any webtoon, and the forbidden-romance tension is perfectly calibrated.
[Read Castle Swimmer](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/castle-swimmer)

**38. The Makeup Remover** — A model at the end of her career finds a second life in a different part of the beauty industry. Mature, emotionally sophisticated, and a genuine exploration of beauty standards.
[Read The Makeup Remover](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-makeup-remover)

**37. Mage & Demon Queen** — Malori the mage keeps trying to reach the Demon Queen's tower — not to fight her, but to confess her love. The comedic inversion of the dungeon fantasy trope is executed brilliantly.
[Read Mage & Demon Queen](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/mage-and-demon-queen)

**36. The Remarried Empress** *(webtoon context)* — The political scheming and visual storytelling in the full color webtoon format elevate this already excellent story.
[Read The Remarried Empress](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-remarried-empress)

**35. My Dear Cold-Blooded King** — A merchant's daughter is captured by the king's men and finds herself drawn into palace intrigue and a complicated romance. Beautiful historical setting and art.
[Read My Dear Cold-Blooded King](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/my-dear-cold-blooded-king)

**34. Down to Earth** — A celebrity alien falls in love with a regular human girl who initially wants nothing to do with him. The sci-fi romance comedy is sweet without being saccharine.
[Read Down to Earth](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/down-to-earth)

**33. Everything is Fine** — A horror/psychological webtoon about a neighborhood where everyone is inexplicably happy. The creeping dread, the color design shifting subtly as the horror escalates — this is webtoon horror done right.
[Read Everything is Fine](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/everything-is-fine)

**32. Freaking Romance** — Two people from different time dimensions share the same apartment. The romance mechanics are original, the chemistry is electric, and the time-period visual contrast is gorgeous.
[Read Freaking Romance](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/freaking-romance)

**31. Neon Masquerade** — Cyberpunk aesthetics meet identity and masquerade themes. One of the most visually distinctive original webtoons on the platform.
[Read Neon Masquerade](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/neon-masquerade)

---

### 30–21: The Webtoon Heavyweights

**30. Isekai Manhwa** crossover: **The Beginning After the End** — Arthur Leywin's arc is among the most emotionally engaging in all of fantasy webtoons. The color art amplifies every emotional beat.
[Read The Beginning After the End](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-beginning-after-the-end)

**29. The Evil Queen's Beautiful Butler** — A villainess forced to flee her own story, disguising herself as a butler. The role reversal and the master/servant dynamic are deliciously done.
[Read The Evil Queen's Beautiful Butler](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-evil-queens-beautiful-butler)

**28. It's Mine** — A cold, ruthless girl in a romance novel tries to avoid the plot while accidentally attracting every male lead. The comedy of errors and the protagonist's exasperation are endlessly entertaining.
[Read It's Mine](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/its-mine)

**27. A Business Proposal** — A woman goes on a blind date in her friend's place to scare him off — only to find her boss is the date. A rom-com with phenomenal comedic timing and a romance that escalates beautifully.
[Read A Business Proposal](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/a-business-proposal)

**26. Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint** *(webtoon format)* — Already a masterpiece in text. The visual adaptation makes the emotional moments even more devastating.
[Read Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/omniscient-readers-viewpoint)

**25. The Abandoned Empress** — Aristia is discarded by the emperor for a new love interest and must navigate her changed fate. The emotional weight of being replaced — and what one does with that pain — is handled with real sophistication.
[Read The Abandoned Empress](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-abandoned-empress)

**24. The Secret of Angel** — A school romance with an unusual gender-identity twist and surprising emotional depth beneath a light exterior.
[Read The Secret of Angel](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-secret-of-angel)

**23. Who Made Me a Princess** — Athanasia is reincarnated as a princess doomed to be killed by her own father. Her attempts to avoid her fate while secretly winning her cold father's affection are both funny and heartbreaking.
[Read Who Made Me a Princess](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/who-made-me-a-princess)

**22. Doctor Elise: The Royal Lady with the Lamp** — A surgeon reincarnated as a princess she read about in a novel. The medical knowledge meets royal court drama angle is uniquely compelling.
[Read Doctor Elise](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/doctor-elise)

**21. Weak Hero** *(webtoon context)* — The full-color webtoon presentation makes Gray's fights hit even harder visually.
[Read Weak Hero](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/weak-hero)

---

### Top 20: The Essential Webtoons

**20. Tower of God** — The webtoon that proved the format could support epic world-building at manga scale.
[Read Tower of God](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/tower-of-god)

**19. Sweet Home** — Horror done with full-color intensity. Essential.
[Read Sweet Home](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/sweet-home)

**18. Lookism** — The defining social commentary webtoon.
[Read Lookism](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/lookism)

**17. UnOrdinary** — The slowest of slow burns, with a payoff that earns every chapter of setup.
[Read UnOrdinary](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/unordinary)

**16. True Beauty** — The webtoon that bridged K-drama and comics culture globally.
[Read True Beauty](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/true-beauty)

**15. The Remarried Empress** — The political romance webtoon.
[Read The Remarried Empress](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-remarried-empress)

**14. Who Made Me a Princess** — Perfectly paced fantasy romance.
[Read Who Made Me a Princess](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/who-made-me-a-princess)

**13. A Business Proposal** — The gold standard of webtoon rom-com.

## Best Completed Manga — Finished Stories That Are Worth Every Page


*Reading time: ~11 min | Category: Rankings | Tags: completed manga, finished manga, manga with endings, best manga to binge*

---

### Introduction

There is a specific joy to picking up a completed manga. No waiting. No hiatuses. No wondering whether the author will stick the landing. The whole story is right there, start to finish, and you get to experience it as a complete work.

Completed manga also has a different kind of critical weight — you can evaluate the whole arc, the ending, the sense of thematic resolution. And some of the greatest manga ever made are completed series.

This list focuses exclusively on manga with satisfying, complete stories.

---

### The Best Completed Manga Ever Made

**Death Note** — 108 chapters. A perfect psychological thriller with one of the best narrative rivalries in comics history. Read it in a weekend. Think about it for a year.
[Read Death Note](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/death-note)

**Fullmetal Alchemist** — 108 chapters. Arakawa planned this from the beginning and it shows. The thematic resolution — about sacrifice, equivalent exchange, and what family means — is one of manga's finest endings.
[Read Fullmetal Alchemist](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/fullmetal-alchemist)

**Attack on Titan** — The ending is debated. The complete work is extraordinary. Read it knowing the debate exists and form your own opinion.
[Read Attack on Titan](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/attack-on-titan)

**Fruits Basket** — 136 chapters plus the Prelude. A slow, beautiful story about broken people healing each other. The ending earns every tear.
[Read Fruits Basket](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/fruits-basket)

**A Silent Voice** — Seven volumes. The best single-story manga about bullying, guilt, and redemption in the medium.
[Read A Silent Voice](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/a-silent-voice)

**Goodnight Punpun** — 147 chapters. Psychologically devastating. One of the most honest depictions of depression, trauma, and the difficulty of growing up in any medium.
[Read Goodnight Punpun](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/goodnight-punpun)

**20th Century Boys** — 249 chapters. Urasawa's thriller masterpiece. The mystery, the scale, the final revelation — extraordinary.
[Read 20th Century Boys](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/20th-century-boys)

**Monster** — 162 chapters. Urasawa again. The most sophisticated thriller in manga.
[Read Monster](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/monster)

**Demon Slayer** — 205 chapters. Completed beautifully. The final arcs give every character their moment.
[Read Demon Slayer](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/demon-slayer)

**Slam Dunk** — 276 chapters. The greatest sports manga. Complete. Perfect.
[Read Slam Dunk](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/slam-dunk)

**Claymore** — 155 chapters. Underrated dark fantasy with one of the best female ensemble casts in manga and a satisfying conclusion.
[Read Claymore](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/claymore)

**The Promised Neverland (first arc)** — Read chapters 1–37. Quit if the second arc disappoints you. The first arc is one of manga's finest thrillers.
[Read The Promised Neverland](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-promised-neverland)

**Tokyo Ghoul + :re** — The complete story, both parts. Ishida's visuals in :re's finale are among manga's most beautiful pages.
[Read Tokyo Ghoul](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/tokyo-ghoul)

**Rurouni Kenshin** — The Kyoto Arc is legendary. The Jinchuu Arc is cathartic. Read the complete story.
[Read Rurouni Kenshin](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/rurouni-kenshin)

**Mushishi** — 10 volumes of short stories. One of the most beautiful manga reading experiences available.
[Read Mushishi](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/mushishi)

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the best completed manga for someone who doesn't read much?**
Death Note and A Silent Voice. Both are relatively short, immediately accessible, and have clear narrative purpose.

**Q: Is there a completed manga with a great ending?**
Fullmetal Alchemist has one of manga's most satisfying conclusions. Fruits Basket's ending is emotionally devastating in the best way.

## Most Underrated Manga You Should Read — Hidden Gems That Deserve More Readers


*Reading time: ~11 min | Category: Rankings | Tags: underrated manga, hidden gem manga, lesser known manga, manga recommendations*

---

### Introduction

Every conversation about manga gravitates toward the same titles. One Piece. Berserk. Death Note. They deserve it — but there's a massive world of manga that never gets mentioned, never gets the anime adaptation bump, and never trends on social media, yet is genuinely extraordinary.

These are the ones. The manga your average reader hasn't heard of but that the serious readers know by heart.

---

### Underrated Manga Worth Finding

**Dungeon Meshi (Delicious in Dungeon)** — Ryoko Kui's manga about adventurers who cook and eat monsters while dungeon-diving sounds like a comedy and is actually one of the most thoughtful fantasy manga in years. The world-building is meticulously detailed. The character growth is genuine. And somehow the food manga elements and the fantasy action elements complement each other perfectly. It got an anime in 2024 — but the manga was underrated for a decade before that.
[Read Dungeon Meshi](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/dungeon-meshi)

**Dungeon Nursery** — A surprisingly touching manga about a warrior in a dungeon who finds and raises abandoned monster children. The tone balance between comedy, action, and genuine parental warmth is exceptional.
[Read Dungeon Nursery](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/dungeon-nursery)

**Shamo** — Brutal. Uncomfortable. A young man convicted of killing his parents trains in karate in prison and emerges as a terrifying martial artist. One of the most unflinching character studies in manga.
[Read Shamo](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/shamo)

**Biomega** — Tsutomu Nihei's sci-fi manga about a synthetic human on a motorcycle fighting through a dying world. Atmospheric, sparse, visually extraordinary.
[Read Biomega](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/biomega)

**The Climber (Kokou no Hito)** — A manga about free solo mountain climbing. The isolation, the physical extremity, the psychological portrait of someone who can only feel alive when they're about to die — it's one of manga's great sports/psychology crossovers.
[Read The Climber](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-climber)

**Usogui** — A gambling manga where the stakes are life and death. Baku Madarame is one of manga's great protagonists — a gambler who plays not to win, but to expose the psychology of those who oppose him.
[Read Usogui](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/usogui)

**Holyland** — A bullied teenager discovers the art of boxing and begins fighting on the streets of Shinjuku. Gritty, realistic, and deeply human in a way most action manga isn't.
[Read Holyland](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/holyland)

**Pluto** — Already on the main list, but wildly underread relative to its quality. Urasawa's Astro Boy reimagining deserves to be in every top-10 conversation.
[Read Pluto](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/pluto)

**Toriko** — Mentioned before and deliberately included here again. Shimabukuro's food adventure deserves a massive international readership it never quite got.
[Read Toriko](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/toriko)

**Lucifer and the Biscuit Hammer** — Satoshi Mizukami's fantasy about a boy who wants to destroy the world, fighting alongside people who want to save it, is one of the most emotionally resonant superhero-adjacent manga ever written.
[Read Lucifer and the Biscuit Hammer](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/lucifer-and-the-biscuit-hammer)

**Spirit Circle** — Another Mizukami masterpiece. A boy and a girl who have been enemies across multiple reincarnations work to understand their past lives. Short. Perfect. Go read it now.
[Read Spirit Circle](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/spirit-circle)

**Frieren: Beyond Journey's End** — Getting more attention now thanks to its anime. But for years this was a quiet gem — an elf mage reflecting on the human companions she outlived and wondering what it means to have known them. Beautiful, melancholy, essential.
[Read Frieren](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/frieren-beyond-journeys-end)

---

### FAQ

**Q: Why are great manga underrated?**
Usually: no major anime adaptation, niche genre, older publication date, or inconsistent scanlation history. None of these affect the quality of the manga itself.

**Q: What's the single most underrated manga?**
Spirit Circle by Satoshi Mizukami. It's short enough to read in an afternoon and one of the most emotionally resonant manga ever written.

## Most Underrated Manhwa You Should Read — Korean Comics That Flew Under the Radar


*Reading time: ~11 min | Category: Rankings | Tags: underrated manhwa, hidden gem manhwa, lesser known manhwa, manhwa recommendations*

---

### Introduction

Solo Leveling, Tower of God, Return of the Mount Hua Sect — the big manhwa titles have massive readerships and dedicated communities. But for every Solo Leveling, there are dozens of manhwa that are just as good — sometimes better — and never find the same audience.

These are the ones you should be reading that you probably aren't.

---

### Underrated Manhwa That Deserve Your Attention

**The World After the Fall** — This one is starting to get recognition, but it still flies under the radar relative to its quality. Jaehwan refusing the regression that the rest of humanity takes is a genuinely radical premise, and what Singshong does with it — philosophically, emotionally, thematically — puts this in the top tier of the genre. If you're bored of standard regression manhwa, this is your next read.
[Read The World After the Fall](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-world-after-the-fall)

**Mookyhim** — Raw, gritty, and featuring one of the most grounded martial artist protagonists in manhwa. No supernatural abilities. No system. Just a body pushed past its limits and a mind that refuses to stop.
[Read Mookyhim](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/mookyhim)

**The Live** — A father given a second chance through a survival game. The emotional stakes are among the highest in manhwa, and the game mechanics are clever.
[Read The Live](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/the-live)

**Dungeon Reset** — Dawoon's practical engineering solutions to dungeon survival are funnier and more creative than any other manhwa in the genre. This deserves the same audience as Solo Leveling.
[Read Dungeon Reset](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/dungeon-reset)

**Distant Sky** — A completed apocalyptic manhwa with some of the most beautiful art ever drawn in the format. The premise is haunting: Seoul's sky disappears and survivors are trapped underground.
[Read Distant Sky](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/distant-sky)

**I Reincarnated as the Crazed Heir** — Political intrigue in a historical fantasy setting with a protagonist who weaponizes the perception of madness. Genuinely clever and underread.
[Read I Reincarnated as the Crazed Heir](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/i-reincarnated-as-the-crazed-heir)

[Read Her Summon](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/her-summon)

**Return of the Blossoming Blade** — One of the best pure murim manhwa that doesn't get mentioned enough. The regression setup is emotionally grounded and the sword cultivation arc is visually extraordinary.
[Read Return of the Blossoming Blade](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/return-of-the-blossoming-blade)

**Ability** — Action manhwa that builds its power system carefully rather than front-loading the protagonist's power. The restraint is refreshing.
[Read Ability](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/ability)

**Nano Machine** — Actually well-read in the manhwa community, but deserves mention here for readers coming from the Japanese manga world who haven't discovered it yet. Best cultivation-meets-murim manhwa by a wide margin.
[Read Nano Machine](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/nano-machine)

**Wind Breaker** — Cycling as the backdrop for a delinquent action story. The technical cycling detail and the team dynamics set this apart from every other delinquent action manhwa.
[Read Wind Breaker](https://mangakakalot.gg/manga/wind-breaker)

Look beyond the algorithm — browse by genre rather than popularity rankings. Community recommendations on Reddit's r/manhwa and r/webtoons consistently surface hidden gems.

## Best Romance Manga — Love Stories That Actually Hit Different


*Reading time: ~12 min | Category: Romance | Tags: best romance manga, romance manga recommendations, manga love stories*

---

### Introduction

Romance manga has this reputation problem where people assume it's all cherry blossoms and confession scenes and doe-eyed protagonists misunderstanding each other for fifty chapters. And sure, some of it is exactly that — and there's nothing wrong with that either. But the best romance manga is something else entirely. It's the kind of story that makes you feel the butterflies, the heartbreak, the quiet devastation of almost, and the extraordinary warmth of finally.

Romance in manga has produced some of the most emotionally precise storytelling in the medium. Not because love is simple — but because manga artists have learned to use the visual language of their craft to communicate things that prose struggles to articulate: the weight of a held gaze, the specific way someone's shoulders drop when they're trying not to cry, the color that bleeds into a panel when a feeling becomes too large to contain.

This list covers the full spectrum — slow burns, dramatic melodramas, high school romances, adult love stories, fantasy romance, and the kind of bittersweet stories that stay with you long after you've finished them.

---

### What Makes Great Romance Manga?

Before the list, let's talk criteria, because not all romance manga is created equal.

The best romance manga has **characters worth caring about** before the romance begins. It makes the romantic tension feel **earned rather than manufactured**. It handles **misunderstandings and conflict** in ways that feel psychologically real rather than contrived. And crucially — it knows whether it wants to end happily or honestly, and commits to that choice.

With that in mind:

---

### Classic Romance Manga You Can't Skip

**Fruits Basket** — Natsuki Takaya's masterpiece about a girl living with a family cursed to transform into zodiac animals is many things: a found-family story, a trauma healing narrative, a meditation on worth and belonging. But at its center is one of manga's most precisely written romances. Tohru and Kyo's relationship develops with patience and care across the full run, and the payoff is one of manga's most emotionally complete endings. Don't let the premise fool you — this one goes genuinely deep.
[Read Fruits Basket](/manga/fruits-basket)

**Clannad (manga)** — Based on the visual novel, but the manga adaptation holds up as its own emotional experience. Tomoya and Nagisa's story of falling in love, building a life, and facing grief together is one of the most devastating romances in any medium.
[Read Clannad](/manga/clannad)

**Kaguya-sama: Love Is War** — Miyuki Shirogane and Kaguya Shinomiya are both in love with each other and both too proud to confess first. The premise sounds like it could get old fast. Instead, it's one of the funniest, most inventively constructed romance manga in years, with character depth that accumulates quietly and then detonates in your face when you least expect it.
[Read Kaguya-sama](/manga/kaguya-sama-love-is-war)

**Horimiya** — Kyoko Hori is popular at school. Izumi Miyamura is quiet and assumed to be boring. Outside school, they're both completely different people. Horimiya is the rare high school romance manga that actually feels like how teenagers interact — messy, funny, sincere, and genuinely warm.
[Read Horimiya](/manga/horimiya)

**Nana** — Ai Yazawa's unfinished masterpiece about two women named Nana sharing an apartment in Tokyo is one of the most emotionally honest manga about love, ambition, and the price of both. The romance here isn't the idealized kind — it's complicated, sometimes painful, and always achingly real.
[Read Nana](/manga/nana)

**Inuyasha** — Rumiko Takahashi's feudal-era adventure built one of manga's most iconic romances across 558 chapters. Kagome and Inuyasha's relationship — complete with its longing, its miscommunications, and its genuine emotional stakes — is the template for a generation of fantasy romance.
[Read Inuyasha](/manga/inuyasha)

---

### Modern Romance Manga Worth Reading

**My Dress-Up Darling** — Wakana Gojo is a doll craftsman who keeps his passion hidden. Marin Kitagawa is a popular girl who loves cosplay and doesn't care who knows it. What starts as a collaboration becomes something much warmer, and the series handles physical attraction and emotional connection with unusual maturity for its genre.
[Read My Dress-Up Darling](/manga/my-dress-up-darling)

**Shikimori's Not Just a Cutie** — A romance where the girl is the cool, protective one and the boyfriend is the accident-prone, soft one. The gender dynamic reversal is handled with warmth rather than making a point of it, which makes it even more charming.
[Read Shikimori's Not Just a Cutie](/manga/shikomoris-not-just-a-cutie)

**Domestic Girlfriend** — Controversial, messy, emotionally reckless — and exactly what it's trying to be. Natsuo's complicated feelings for his stepsister Hina are handled with a soapy intensity that's genuinely compelling if you're in the mood for it.
[Read Domestic Girlfriend](/manga/domestic-girlfriend)

**A Silent Voice** — Not a romance in the conventional sense, but the relationship between Shoya and Shoko is one of manga's most carefully drawn emotional connections. The weight of past hurt and the difficulty of moving through it makes their bond feel extraordinarily real.
[Read A Silent Voice](/manga/a-silent-voice)

**Your Lie in April** — A pianist who lost the ability to hear his own playing meets a violinist who plays like the world is ending every time. The romance is beautiful and the tragedy is inevitable. Bring tissues.
[Read Your Lie in April](/manga/your-lie-in-april)

**Ao Haru Ride (Blue Spring Ride)** — Futaba and Kou reconnect years after losing contact. The manga handles the way people change — and the way old feelings adapt rather than disappear — with genuine emotional intelligence.
[Read Ao Haru Ride](/manga/ao-haru-ride)

**ReLife** — An adult man is given a drug that makes him look young and sent back to high school for a year. The adult perspective on teenage romance makes this stand out from almost everything in its genre.
[Read ReLife](/manga/relife)

---

### Slow Burn and Mature Romance

**Lovely Complex** — A tall girl and a short boy fall into a rivalry that becomes something else. The comedy is excellent, the chemistry is earned, and the confession arc is one of manga's most memorable.
[Read Lovely Complex](/manga/lovely-complex)

**Takane & Hana** — An age-gap romance between a high school girl and a arrogant young CEO who can't stop testing each other. Funnier than it sounds, sweeter than you'd expect.
[Read Takane & Hana](/manga/takane-and-hana)

**We Were There (Bokura ga Ita)** — A first love story that turns into a meditation on how the past haunts the present. The realism of how teenage heartbreak can shape adult behavior gives this one unusual resonance.
[Read We Were There](/manga/we-were-there)

**Kimi ni Todoke** — Sawako Kuronuma is misunderstood because she looks scary. Shota Kazehaya is the most popular boy in class. The sheer purity of this story is disarming. The slowness is the whole point.
[Read Kimi ni Todoke](/manga/kimi-ni-todoke)

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the best romance manga with a happy ending?**
Horimiya, Fruits Basket, and Lovely Complex all end happily and satisfyingly. Kaguya-sama also concludes its romance arc beautifully.

**Q: What romance manga has the best slow burn?**
Kimi ni Todoke and Kaguya-sama are the kings of slow burn. If you want adult slow burn, ReLife is exceptional.

**Q: Is romance manga only for teenagers?**
Not at all. Nana, ReLife, and many others specifically address adult relationships, professional ambitions, and mature emotional dynamics.

## Best Romance Manhwa — Korean Webtoons That Will Wreck Your Heart (In the Best Way)


*Reading time: ~12 min | Category: Romance | Tags: best romance manhwa, romance webtoons, Korean romance comics*

---

### Introduction

Romance manhwa has quietly become one of the most-read comic genres on Earth. The combination of full-color art, smartphone-optimized vertical scrolling, weekly updates, and stories calibrated for maximum emotional impact has produced a romance reading experience unlike anything else in comics.

What sets romance manhwa apart from manga or Western comics? A few things. The villainess genre — where the protagonist is reincarnated as the doomed antagonist of a romance novel — is almost entirely a Korean invention. The regression romance — where a heartbroken character returns to the past to change their fate — is refined in manhwa to an art. And the sheer visual expressiveness of Korean webtoon art, with its lush color work and its mastery of the emotional close-up, makes romantic moments hit differently.

Whether you're new to manhwa or a veteran looking for something new to spiral into, this is your list.

---

### The Foundation: Romance Manhwa Everyone Should Read

**True Beauty** — Jugyeong Lim is insecure about her natural appearance and becomes popular through skilled makeup application. The romance between her, Suho, and Seojun is one of the most genuinely agonizing love triangles in manhwa. Yaongyi doesn't let you comfortably pick a side — both love interests are real, both have genuine connections with Jugyeong, and the story takes both seriously. The art is stunning.
[Read True Beauty](/manga/true-beauty)

**A Business Proposal** — Haeri goes on a blind date as a favor to her friend, planning to be so terrible the date runs away. The date turns out to be her CEO boss. The rom-com mechanics are executed with almost perfect timing — every misunderstanding lands, every romantic development is earned, and the secondary couple subplot is as good as the main one.
[Read A Business Proposal](/manga/a-business-proposal)

**The Remarried Empress** — Navier is the perfect empress — composed, competent, beloved. Her emperor husband falls for another woman and sets in motion events that force Navier to make an extraordinary choice. This is political romance at its finest: a woman who refuses to be diminished, and a story that lets her be magnificent.
[Read The Remarried Empress](/manga/the-remarried-empress)

**Who Made Me a Princess** — Athanasia wakes up as the princess of a fantasy kingdom doomed to be executed by her own cold-hearted father. Her attempts to survive, her gradual thawing of her father's heart, and the genuine warmth that develops between them is one of manhwa's most beloved father-daughter stories embedded inside a romance narrative.
[Read Who Made Me a Princess](/manga/who-made-me-a-princess)

**Lore Olympus** — Rachel Smythe's reimagining of Hades and Persephone for a modern adult audience is the Western world's entry point into webtoon romance. The use of color as emotion — Persephone's pink softness, Hades' measured blues — is genuinely innovative visual storytelling.
[Read Lore Olympus](/manga/lore-olympus)

---

### Historical and Fantasy Romance Manhwa

**Like Wind on a Dry Branch** — Set in a historical fantasy world, this follows Canillia, a woman who has lived through centuries of tragedy and finds herself drawn to a man who sees through her perfect exterior. The art is exceptional — detailed, atmospheric, and deeply expressive. One of the most underrated romance manhwa in the historical genre.
[Read Like Wind on a Dry Branch](/manga/like-wind-on-a-dry-branch)

**The Abandoned Empress** — Aristia was raised from birth to be the emperor's chosen. When a new girl appears and the emperor turns away from Aristia, the emotional devastation — and Aristia's journey through it — is one of the most raw depictions of romantic rejection in manhwa.
[Read The Abandoned Empress](/manga/the-abandoned-empress)

**Doctor Elise: The Royal Lady with the Lamp** — A modern cardiac surgeon reincarnated as the selfish princess she read about in a novel. Her medical knowledge, her changed personality, and the slow-burn romance with the crown prince as she tries to avert her original fate are handled beautifully.
[Read Doctor Elise](/manga/doctor-elise)

**SubZero** — Clove, the last princess of her people, must marry the crown prince of her ancestral enemies to end a war. The arranged marriage romance is built on real tension — political, cultural, and personal — and both leads are given genuine complexity.
[Read SubZero](/manga/subzero)

**Her Summon** — A female protagonist summoned into a fantasy world who builds her own power rather than relying on romantic protection. The romance develops alongside genuine character growth, which makes it more satisfying than most.
[Read Her Summon](/manga/her-summon)

**Unholy Blood** — A half-vampire woman living as a normal human is pulled back into conflict when a detective investigating vampire murders crosses her path. The romance develops in the gaps between action sequences and hits harder for it.
[Read Unholy Blood](/manga/unholy-blood)

---

### Office, School, and Contemporary Romance

**I Love Yoo** — Quimchee's slice-of-life romance is the most psychologically realistic romance webtoon on the platform. Scheherazade Yoo is a complicated, funny, emotionally guarded protagonist, and watching her relationships slowly shift is one of the most authentic romance reading experiences in manhwa.
[Read I Love Yoo](/manga/i-love-yoo)

**Freaking Romance** — Two people from different time dimensions share the same apartment — one appears during the day, one at night. The romantic tension across a dimensional barrier is one of the most original conceits in webtoon romance.
[Read Freaking Romance](/manga/freaking-romance)

**Positively Yours** — A one-night stand results in a pregnancy. The manhwa handles the subsequent relationship development with surprising maturity and avoids the traps of the genre.
[Read Positively Yours](/manga/positively-yours)

**My ID Is Gangnam Beauty** — Mirae undergoes plastic surgery and enters university, where she struggles with how others perceive her appearance. The romance runs alongside a genuine examination of beauty standards, self-worth, and the cruelty that can hide behind conventional beauty.
[Read My ID Is Gangnam Beauty](/manga/my-id-is-gangnam-beauty)

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the best completed romance manhwa?**
A Business Proposal, Who Made Me a Princess, and Lore Olympus are all complete with satisfying endings.

**Q: What romance manhwa has the best female lead?**
The Remarried Empress. Navier is one of manhwa's most extraordinary protagonists — competent, dignified, and given genuine agency.

**Q: Is there romance manhwa for adults that isn't just high school drama?**
I Love Yoo, Like Wind on a Dry Branch, Positively Yours, and The Remarried Empress all feature adult relationships and dynamics.

## Best Romance Manhua — Chinese Comics With Love Stories Worth Reading


*Reading time: ~10 min | Category: Romance | Tags: romance manhua, Chinese romance comics, best manhua romance*

---

### Introduction

Romance manhua occupies a specific and fascinating niche. On one hand, you have the transmigration and villainess stories that Chinese webnovel culture exported to comics — the heroine reborn into a novel she read, navigating its plot with the advantage of foreknowledge. On the other, you have modern contemporary romances rooted in Chinese urban culture, and the historical xianxia romances that blend cultivation, palace intrigue, and love stories with operatic intensity.

The best romance manhua leans hard into emotional sincerity. Chinese romantic fiction, in both novel and comic form, tends toward grand gestures, sweeping fate, and love stories written with the scale of destiny rather than the scale of everyday life. When it works, it's extraordinary.

---

### Best Romance Manhua

**The Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation (Mo Dao Zu Shi)** — Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji's relationship is one of the great slow burns in all of comics, not just manhua. The layers — the original antagonism, the respect, the tragedy of their separation, the reunion across death — are built with real craft. The art in the manhua adaptation is gorgeous.
[Read Mo Dao Zu Shi](/manga/mo-dao-zu-shi)

**Heaven Official's Blessing (Tian Guan Ci Fu)** — Another MXTX adaptation. Xie Lian, a god who has fallen from heaven three times, meets the Ghost King Hua Cheng, who has been devoted to him across 800 years. The scope of this love story — literally spanning centuries and multiple lifetimes — is handled with the emotional precision of a much smaller story.
[Read Heaven Official's Blessing](/manga/heaven-officials-blessing)

**The Scum Villain's Self-Saving System** — Played partly for comedy, but the romance between Shen Qingqiu and Luo Binghe builds with genuine warmth beneath the meta-narrative humor.
[Read Scum Villain's Self-Saving System](/manga/scum-villains-self-saving-system)

**I Shall Seal the Heavens** — The cultivation epic also contains one of manhua's most emotionally complete romances: Meng Hao and Xu Qing's story across lifetimes and heavens is devastating.
[Read I Shall Seal the Heavens](/manga/i-shall-seal-the-heavens)

**Who Gets the World (Qie Shi Tian Xia)** — A female martial arts master with all the power and none of the desire to use it meets an equally capable love interest. The gender dynamic is refreshingly equal.
[Read Who Gets the World](/manga/who-gets-the-world)

**Song of the Long March (Chang Ge Xing)** — Historical manhua set in the Tang Dynasty, following Li Chang Ge, a princess fighting for survival and vengeance. The romance is secondary to the action and strategy — but it's exactly the kind of romance that earns every moment.
[Read Song of the Long March](/manga/song-of-the-long-march)

**My Quiet Blacksmith Life in Another World** — A transmigration romance where the focus is genuinely on daily life and a gradual, understated romance. A palate cleanser between epics.
[Read My Quiet Blacksmith Life](/manga/my-quiet-blacksmith-life)

**Remarried Empress (Manhua)** — The Chinese adaptation and original Chinese novel versions explore similar political romance themes with the aesthetics of Chinese court drama.
[Read Remarried Empress Manhua](/manga/remarried-empress-manhua)

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the best romance manhua based on a novel?**
Mo Dao Zu Shi and Heaven Official's Blessing are both exceptional novel-to-manhua adaptations that honor their source material.

**Q: Is there romance manhua that isn't cultivation/fantasy?**
Yes — contemporary Chinese romance manhua exists, though it's less internationally available than the fantasy titles.

## Best Romance Webtoons — Scroll-Stopping Love Stories


*Reading time: ~11 min | Category: Romance | Tags: best romance webtoons, romance webtoon list, webtoon love stories 2026*

---

### Introduction

Romance webtoons have a superpower that manga and print comics don't — the scroll. In a vertical webtoon, the artist controls your pacing by controlling what you see and when. A panel that slowly reveals a character's expression as you scroll down. A color shift that tells you something has changed before any dialogue does. A single image that fills your entire phone screen at the exact moment the emotion peaks.

The best romance webtoon artists understand this. They build tension through the scroll, release it through the reveal, and use the full-color palette to do emotional work that prose couldn't.

These are the romance webtoons that use all of that to maximum effect.

---

### The Must-Read Romance Webtoons

**Lore Olympus** — Already covered elsewhere, but it earns its place on every romance list. Persephone and Hades fall in love slowly, painfully, and beautifully. The pastel color work and the contemporary mythological setting are used with real visual intelligence.
[Read Lore Olympus](/manga/lore-olympus)

**True Beauty** — The gold standard of contemporary romance webtoons. The love triangle actually hurts because both love interests are written as real, valuable relationships.
[Read True Beauty](/manga/true-beauty)

**SubZero** — Political arranged-marriage romance between dragon clan royals. The world design and the tension between duty and feeling are exceptional.
[Read SubZero](/manga/subzero)

**Castle Swimmer** — The beacon and the prince destined to kill him. The forbidden romance mechanics and the genuinely beautiful aquatic world make this one of the most visually distinctive romance webtoons available.
[Read Castle Swimmer](/manga/castle-swimmer)

**I Love Yoo** — For readers who want romance grounded in realistic emotional dynamics rather than dramatic fantasy setups.
[Read I Love Yoo](/manga/i-love-yoo)

**Freaking Romance** — Dimensional barrier romance. The color design communicating the day/night divide is genuinely clever.
[Read Freaking Romance](/manga/freaking-romance)

**Down to Earth** — A celebrity alien falls for a human who initially wants nothing to do with him. The comedy is sharp and the emotional landing is earned.
[Read Down to Earth](/manga/down-to-earth)

**My Dear Cold-Blooded King** — Historical fantasy romance with atmospheric world design and a female protagonist who is consistently interesting.
[Read My Dear Cold-Blooded King](/manga/my-dear-cold-blooded-king)

**The Abandoned Empress** — One of the most emotionally raw romances in fantasy webtoons. The pain of being replaced and the journey through it is handled with genuine craft.
[Read The Abandoned Empress](/manga/the-abandoned-empress)

**Who Made Me a Princess** — A comedy-adjacent villainess romance that becomes genuinely moving in its treatment of parent-child relationships.
[Read Who Made Me a Princess](/manga/who-made-me-a-princess)

**A Business Proposal** — The best pure rom-com webtoon. Funny, sweet, and perfectly paced.
[Read A Business Proposal](/manga/a-business-proposal)

**Always Human** — A completed LGBTQ+ romance set in a near-future world. Quiet, warm, and beautifully drawn.
[Read Always Human](/manga/always-human)

**Mage & Demon Queen** — Comedy romance with the best premise: a human mage who keeps storming the Demon Queen's tower to confess her love, not to fight her.
[Read Mage & Demon Queen](/manga/mage-and-demon-queen)

|----------|-----------|
| Fantasy romance | Lore Olympus / SubZero |

**Q: What romance webtoon has the best art?**
Lore Olympus for color work. SubZero for character design. Castle Swimmer for world design.

**Q: What's a good starter romance webtoon?**
True Beauty or A Business Proposal. Both are accessible, funny, and emotionally engaging from the first chapter.

## Best Historical Romance Manga — Love Stories Set in Another Time


*Reading time: ~10 min | Category: Romance | Tags: historical romance manga, period romance manga, feudal romance manga*

---

### Introduction

Historical romance manga sits at the intersection of two things manga does brilliantly: meticulous period setting and emotionally precise character work. When you set a love story in Meiji-era Japan, the Heian court, feudal China, or a medieval fantasy analogue, the constraints of the era become part of the romantic tension. Class barriers, arranged marriages, duty to family versus personal feeling, the scandal of an unapproved attachment — all of these add layers that contemporary romance stories can't produce.

The best historical romance manga uses its setting not just as backdrop but as active pressure on the relationship at its center.

---

### Best Historical Romance Manga

**Inuyasha** — Set between feudal Japan and the modern era, Kagome and Inuyasha's relationship is one of the most iconic in manga history. The historical setting adds genuine stakes — their worlds are literally incompatible, which makes every choice to stay together meaningful.
[Read Inuyasha](/manga/inuyasha)

**Rurouni Kenshin** — Meiji-era Japan. Kenshin's vow never to kill again and the romantic relationship that develops with Kaoru sits alongside extraordinary action. The love story is restrained in the classic shounen way — which makes the moments it surfaces all the more powerful.
[Read Rurouni Kenshin](/manga/rurouni-kenshin)

**Ōoku: The Inner Chambers** — An alternate Edo Japan where a plague has killed most men, reversing gender roles completely. The romance in this manga is sophisticated, political, and unlike anything else in the historical genre.
[Read Ōoku](/manga/ooku-the-inner-chambers)

**Natsume's Book of Friends (seasonal romance elements)** — Set in contemporary Japan but deeply rooted in traditional folklore, the romantic elements are understated but real.
[Read Natsume's Book of Friends](/manga/natsumes-book-of-friends)

**Ceres: Celestial Legend** — Yuu Watase's dark historical fantasy romance about a girl who carries the celestial maiden Ceres within her. The romance is dramatic, operatic, and deeply emotionally committed.
[Read Ceres: Celestial Legend](/manga/ceres-celestial-legend)

**Fushigi Yuugi** — A girl pulled into an ancient Chinese fantasy world and the general who becomes her protector and love interest. Over-the-top, emotionally intense, and enormously influential in the historical romance genre.
[Read Fushigi Yuugi](/manga/fushigi-yuugi)

**Red River (Anatolia Story)** — A modern girl transported to ancient Hittite civilization. The historical research in this manga is genuinely impressive, and the romance between Yuri and Kail develops across years of shared danger.
[Read Red River](/manga/red-river)

**From Far Away (Kanata Kara)** — A girl transported to a fantasy world that feels grounded in historical traditions. The romance with Izark is a slow, quiet burn that respects the emotional pacing of real relationship development.
[Read From Far Away](/manga/from-far-away)

---

### Historical Romance Manhwa Worth Adding

**The Remarried Empress** — Court politics in a historical fantasy setting. Navier's story is one of manhwa's finest historical romances.
[Read The Remarried Empress](/manga/the-remarried-empress)

**Like Wind on a Dry Branch** — Perhaps the single best pure historical romance in manhwa. The art and the emotional restraint are extraordinary.
[Read Like Wind on a Dry Branch](/manga/like-wind-on-a-dry-branch)

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the best historical romance manga for beginners?**
Inuyasha — it's long but very accessible, and the romance develops naturally across the adventure.

**Q: Are there historical romance manga set outside Japan?**
Yes — Red River is set in ancient Anatolia, Fushigi Yuugi in ancient China, and Ōoku reimagines Edo Japan.
