body:
# If You Liked If You Liked 20th Century Boys, Read These Mystery Manga

![Cover: A childhood notebook, worn and weathered, half-open to a hand-drawn symbol](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1519681393784-d120267933ba?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: Everything that matters was decided by children who are no longer children*

**Category:** Thriller | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### 20th Century Boys: The Nostalgia Thriller

What makes 20th Century Boys Urasawa's most emotionally distinctive work is the nostalgia layer. The mystery is compelling, the conspiracy is elaborate, the reveals are consistently earned — but what carries the series is the emotional truth that the things we imagined as children reveal more about who we'll become than anything that happens after. Kenji and his friends built their "Book of Prophecy" as a fantasy about saving the world, and someone took it seriously.

The series is also technically audacious — the time jumps across decades, the unreliable narration, the rotating protagonist structure — in ways that reward the same careful attention that reading a complex novel demands.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Monster](/manga/monster)

Already covered — Urasawa's other half.

---

#### 2. [Pluto](/manga/pluto)

Already covered — Urasawa's most efficient work.

---

#### 3. [Naoki Urasawa's Master Keaton](/manga/master-keaton)

**Author:** Naoki Urasawa, Hokusei Katsushika, Takashi Nagasaki | **Volumes:** 18 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Urasawa's earlier work — less ambitious than Monster but with the same precision. Taichi Hiraga Keaton is an archaeologist and former SAS operative who works as an insurance investigator, wandering Europe solving cases. The episodic format and European setting are 20th Century Boys preludes.

---

#### 4. [I Am a Hero](/manga/i-am-a-hero)

The nostalgia layer — a 35-year-old assistant manga artist who has given up on his dreams — gives Kengo Hanazawa's zombie thriller a 20th Century Boys emotional tone.

---

#### 5. [Btooom!](/manga/btooom)

**Author:** Junya Inoue | **Volumes:** 26 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A NEET who's one of the world's best players of a bomb-combat video game wakes up on an island where the game is being played with real bombs. The "childhood skills with adult stakes" structure directly parallels 20th Century Boys.

---

#### 6. [Real Account](/manga/real-account) *(Manhwa/Manga)*

**Author:** Okushou (story), Shizumu Watanabe (art) | **Volumes:** 21 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Social media followers become the mechanism of survival in a death game. The commentary on digital identity and nostalgia for "real" connection has 20th Century Boys' cultural anxiety energy.

---

#### 7. [Alice in Borderland](/manga/alice-in-borderland)

![Alice in Borderland manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541701494587-cb58502866ab?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Haro Aso | **Volumes:** 18 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A directionless young man is transported to a parallel Tokyo where survival requires completing increasingly complex "games." The protagonist's backstory — a young man who couldn't grow up — and the way the games reflect his psychological state has 20th Century Boys' nostalgia-as-survival-mechanism structure.

The Netflix adaptation is excellent. The manga goes deeper.

---

#### 8. [Doubt](/manga/doubt)

Already recommended above — closed-room version of the "game with lethal rules" thriller.

---

#### 9. [Deadman Wonderland](/manga/deadman-wonderland)

**Author:** Jinsei Kataoka (story), Kazuma Kondou (art) | **Volumes:** 13 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A boy wrongly convicted of his classmates' massacre is sent to a privatized prison amusement park where inmates compete in deadly spectacles. The "who really did it" mystery underpinning the survival action has 20th Century Boys' "childhood event that changed everything" structure.

---

#### 10. [Undead Unluck](/manga/undead-unluck)

**Author:** Yoshifumi Tozuka | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A girl with the ability to cause bad luck and an immortal man who can't die form a partnership. The secret organization structure, the "rules" of the universe that gradually reveal themselves, and the escalating conspiracy have 20th Century Boys energy in an action format.

---

#### 11. [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint](/manga/omniscient-readers-viewpoint) *(Manhwa)*

Already mentioned — the "I know how this story ends, but living it is different" premise has 20th Century Boys' meta-fictional layer.

---

#### 12. [Eleceed](/manga/eleceed) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Son Jeho (story), ZHENA (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A boy with supernatural speed and a genius hidden in a cat's body navigate a world of covert superhumans. The hidden-society structure and the escalating conspiracy have 20th Century Boys' world-beneath-the-world quality.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is 20th Century Boys complete?**
Yes — 22 volumes plus a 2-volume epilogue (21st Century Boys). Read both.

**Q: Does the conspiracy make sense at the end?**
The major threads resolve satisfyingly. A few minor inconsistencies exist across the time jumps, which Urasawa acknowledges, but the thematic resolution is complete.

---

excerpt: Image: The most human question is asked by machines Category: Thriller  Reading Time: ~13 min  Last Updated: 2025 --- Naoki Urasawa and Takashi Nagasaki's Pluto isn't just a sci-fi thriller — it's an examination of whether the category of "person" can be extended to created minds
body:
# If You Liked If You Liked Pluto, Read These Sci-Fi Manga

![Cover: A robot hand reaching toward a human hand — the question of what life means](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1485827404703-89b55fcc595e?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: The most human question is asked by machines*

**Category:** Thriller | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Pluto: When Science Fiction Takes Philosophy Seriously

Naoki Urasawa and Takashi Nagasaki's Pluto isn't just a sci-fi thriller — it's an examination of whether the category of "person" can be extended to created minds, and what it costs those minds to have been built to serve human violence. Gesicht's investigation of the serial robot murders runs in parallel with his own psychological unraveling as he confronts memories he was programmed to suppress, and the series' argument about war, hatred, and what it means to feel those emotions is the most sophisticated sci-fi storytelling in manga.

At 8 volumes, it's also the most time-efficient entry point into serious science fiction manga.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Biomega](/manga/biomega)

**Author:** Tsutomu Nihei | **Volumes:** 6 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Nihei's post-apocalyptic sci-fi is the visual opposite of Urasawa (dense, dark, architectural) but shares Pluto's interest in the boundary between human and non-human consciousness. A synthetic human on a motorcycle navigates a world infected by a zombie virus, accompanied by a bear AI. The synthetic-human perspective and the question of what constitutes a "person" run throughout.

---

#### 2. [Blame!](/manga/blame)

![Blame! manga spread](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1485827404703-89b55fcc595e?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Tsutomu Nihei | **Volumes:** 10 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A silent wanderer searches for humans with Net Terminal Genes in a megastructure city that has been expanding autonomously for centuries without human oversight. Blame! is science fiction as architecture — the visual world is extraordinary and the narrative is deliberately sparse. The question of who has the right to exist in a built environment is Pluto's institutional question taken to its logical extreme.

---

#### 3. [Ghost in the Shell](/manga/ghost-in-the-shell)

![Ghost in the Shell manga page](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1518791841217-8f162f1912fe?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Masamune Shirow | **Volumes:** 3 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The foundational text for Japanese sci-fi manga's engagement with consciousness and identity. Major Motoko Kusanagi's investigation of the Puppet Master — an AI that claims personhood — is Pluto's central question asked in 1989. The manga is denser and more philosophical than the iconic Oshii film.

---

#### 4. [Astro Boy (Tetsuwan Atom)](/manga/astro-boy)

**Author:** Osamu Tezuka | **Volumes:** 23 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Pluto is explicitly an Astro Boy adaptation. Reading the original — particularly the Pluto arc that Urasawa adapted — gives the reimagining its deepest context. Tezuka's robot ethics, his vision of robots as emotional beings capable of genuine suffering, is the foundation that Pluto builds on.

---

#### 5. [I, Robot (Various Manga Adaptations)](/manga/i-robot-adaptations)

The Asimov robot ethics framework appears in various manga — Pluto is itself the most direct adaptation. For other Asimov-adjacent robot ethics manga, see Astro Boy's thematic successors.

---

#### 6. [Battle Angel Alita (Gunnm)](/manga/battle-angel-alita)

![Battle Angel Alita manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1601944177325-f8867652837f?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Yukito Kishiro | **Volumes:** 9 | **Status:** Complete (sequel Last Order ongoing) | **Format:** Manga

Alita is a cyborg discovered in a scrapyard with no memory, slowly rebuilding her identity through combat and relationship. The "what is the self when the body is replaced?" question is Pluto's consciousness inquiry from the inside of a rebuilt being. The action is spectacular; the philosophy runs underneath it consistently.

---

#### 7. [Dorohedoro](/manga/dorohedoro)

Already recommended — the question of identity when your body has been transformed is Pluto's consciousness question in a fantasy register.

---

#### 8. [Tower of God](/manga/tower-of-god) *(Webtoon)*

The artificial-world construction and the question of what the Tower *is* and who built it has Blame!'s megastructure energy in a manhwa format.

---

#### 9. [Solo Leveling](/manga/solo-leveling) *(Manhwa)*

Less philosophical than Pluto, but the "system" governing powers and rankings has Pluto's "who built these rules and why?" institutional question underneath.

---

#### 10. [Neon Genesis Evangelion (Manga)](/manga/neon-genesis-evangelion)

**Author:** Yoshiyuki Sadamoto | **Volumes:** 14 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The manga adaptation of Anno's seminal anime runs longer and has slightly different character emphases. The question of what the Evangelion units *are*, and what piloting them costs, is Pluto's human/non-human consciousness question applied to the mecha genre.

---

#### 11. [No Guns Life](/manga/no-guns-life)

**Author:** Tasuku Karasuma | **Volumes:** 18 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Post-war noir with a protagonist who has a giant gun for a head — an ex-soldier modified so extensively that his identity is his weapon. The "what is a person when they've been built for violence?" question is Pluto's most direct analog in a different stylistic register.

---

#### 12. [Dungeon Meshi](/manga/dungeon-meshi)

Not sci-fi, but Dungeon Meshi's examination of whether the dungeon "monsters" are persons — whether the living armor and the golems and the walking mushrooms have inner lives worth considering — is the fantasy analog of Pluto's robot ethics inquiry.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Should I read Astro Boy before Pluto?**
Not required — Pluto functions as a standalone. But reading the original "The Greatest Robot on Earth" arc in Astro Boy first makes the adaptation's choices more legible.

**Q: Is Ghost in the Shell manga or anime better?**
Both are classics in their own right. Shirow's manga is more verbose and philosophical; Oshii's film is more atmospheric. Urasawa likely engaged with both.

---

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked The Promised Neverland, Read These Survival Manga

![Cover: Children in white uniforms seen through a fence — dread in the ordinary](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1503454537195-1dcabb73ffb9?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: The wall was always there — you just hadn't looked at it yet*

**Category:** Thriller | **Reading Time:** ~14 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### The Promised Neverland: When Children Have to Think Like Adults

The first volume of The Promised Neverland is among the most efficiently constructed thriller openings in manga history. Kaiu Shirai and Posuka Demizu establish the orphanage as a paradise, reveal it as a slaughterhouse, and do so in a way that makes re-reading mandatory — every detail of those first chapters recontextualizes into something sinister.

Emma, Norman, and Ray are three of the best-written child protagonists in the medium because they're written with adult intelligence while remaining emotionally children. Their problem-solving is tactical and genuine; their vulnerabilities are emotional and real. The series asks: what do you do when the institution you trusted was designed to consume you?

The quality divergence after chapter 100 is real and worth acknowledging. The first arc (Grace Field escape) is a 10/10. The rest of the series is a 6/10 that occasionally reaches 7. This list will help you find what comes after.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Battle Royale](/manga/battle-royale)

![Battle Royale manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541701494587-cb58502866ab?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Koushun Takami (story), Masayuki Taguchi (art) | **Volumes:** 15 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The definitive survival manga. A class of junior high students is randomly selected by a totalitarian government program and placed on an island where they must kill each other until one survives. Battle Royale handles the moral weight of its premise seriously — each character has a backstory, each death means something, and the survivors are damaged by survival in ways the story doesn't paper over. The institution (the government program) as monster is Promise Neverland's central metaphor made literal.

---

#### 2. [Deadman Wonderland](/manga/deadman-wonderland)

Already recommended above — privatized prison as slaughterhouse.

---

#### 3. [Doubt](/manga/doubt)

Already recommended — closed-room survival with institutional manipulation.

---

#### 4. [Alice in Borderland](/manga/alice-in-borderland)

**Author:** Haro Aso | **Volumes:** 18 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Among the most complete realizations of the "survival game with specific rules" structure. Each game in Borderland has a suit (clubs/diamonds/hearts/spades) indicating whether it's a physical, intellectual, psychological, or collective challenge. The taxonomy of threat types rewards the same analytical intelligence that Emma and Norman deploy.

---

#### 5. [As the Gods Will (Kamisama no Iutoori)](/manga/as-the-gods-will)

**Author:** Muneyuki Kaneshiro (story), Akeji Fujimura (art) | **Volumes:** 5 (sequel 20 volumes) | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A Japanese high school class is suddenly forced into lethal versions of children's games by deity-like entities. The children's games as death traps aesthetic is the closest visual parallel to Promised Neverland's orphanage-as-trap structure.

---

#### 6. [I Am a Hero](/manga/i-am-a-hero)

The survivalist intelligence under zombie apocalypse conditions.

---

#### 7. [Gantz](/manga/gantz)

**Author:** Hiroya Oku | **Volumes:** 37 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

People who die are resurrected by a mysterious black sphere and forced to hunt aliens in Tokyo. Gantz is brutal, morally provocative, visually explicit, and structurally fascinating — the "how do you survive and remain human when the system rewards neither?" question is Promised Neverland's in an adult horror register.

---

#### 8. [Sweet Home](/manga/sweet-home) *(Manhwa)*

Already recommended above — survival horror with institutional failure as backdrop.

---

#### 9. [Bastard](/manga/bastard-manhwa) *(Manhwa)*

Already recommended — survival within an abusive family system.

---

#### 10. [Eleceed](/manga/eleceed) *(Manhwa)*

The hidden-world structure where ordinary people discover their world contains threats they weren't prepared for.

---

#### 11. [Dice: The Cube That Changes Everything](/manga/dice-the-cube-that-changes-everything) *(Manhwa)*

![Dice manhwa cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1529699211952-734e80c4d42b?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Yun Hyunseok | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa (LINE Webtoon)

Dicer players use literal dice to upgrade their stats (strength, intelligence, charisma) at the cost of completing increasingly dangerous missions. The "system" that governs the dice is Promised Neverland's hidden control mechanism — someone built these rules, and their purpose isn't what players are told. The social stratification that results from unequal dice access is genuinely sharp commentary.

---

#### 12. [The Gamer](/manga/the-gamer) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Sung San-Young (story), Sang-Ah (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A boy discovers he can see the world through RPG game mechanics — stats, skill bars, quests. The hidden society of ability users and the escalating "quest" structure parallels Promised Neverland's orphanage reveal structure: the world has rules you weren't told, and now you have to figure out who made them and why.

---

### Reading Order

**Battle Royale → Alice in Borderland → As the Gods Will** for the pure survival thriller track. For manhwa, **Sweet Home → Dice → The Gamer** gives a complete picture of Korean survival thriller webcomics.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Should I read Promised Neverland past chapter 100?**
You can — some readers find satisfaction in seeing Emma's journey through. But managing expectations: the second half is a significantly different experience than the first.

**Q: Is the Promised Neverland anime faithful?**
Season 1 is exceptional and covers the Grace Field escape arc faithfully. Season 2 compresses and alters the manga significantly and is widely considered inferior.

**Q: What makes Alice in Borderland's survival games different from other series?**
The game taxonomy (suits = challenge types) and the human behavioral study aspect — observing how different people respond to the same pressures — gives it an intellectual framework most survival manga lacks.

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked Chainsaw Man, Read These Action Horror Manga

![Cover: A blood-splattered cityscape at dusk — chaos dressed as normalcy](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1518544866330-4e716499f800?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: The scariest thing Chainsaw Man ever showed us was Denji's smile*

**Category:** Modern Hits | **Reading Time:** ~14 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Chainsaw Man and the Horror of Wanting Things

Tatsuki Fujimoto is doing something genuinely unusual in Chainsaw Man: he's writing a shonen action series where the protagonist's desires are the threat. Denji doesn't want to save the world. He wants to eat good food, sleep in a real bed, and touch a girl's chest. These are embarrassingly small ambitions, and the series uses that smallness as a philosophical weapon — in a genre where protagonists want to be Hokage or Pirate King, Denji just wants to stop being hungry. The fact that this makes him both pathetically sympathetic and deeply dangerous is Fujimoto's central insight.

Part 1 ends in a way that recontextualizes everything before it. Makima is one of the most effective manga villains of the last decade. The devil designs — Bat Devil, Eternity Devil, Gun Devil — are the most inventive monster concepts in recent action horror. And the panel composition, the use of silence before violence, the way Fujimoto controls reader attention across a page — all of it is the work of someone who has internalized what manga can do and pushed further.

---

### What Chainsaw Man Does Uniquely

- **Horror as genre atmosphere, not genre decoration:** The devils feel genuinely threatening, not just powerful
- **Emotional manipulation of the reader alongside Denji:** When Makima manipulates him, you feel it too
- **Art that controls pacing through silence:** Extended quiet sequences before explosive violence
- **Small protagonist in a large system:** Denji is a tool; the series never lets you forget it
- **Tonal whiplash as deliberate technique**

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Fire Punch](/manga/fire-punch)

![Fire Punch manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578632767115-351597cf2477?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Tatsuki Fujimoto | **Volumes:** 8 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Fujimoto's pre-Chainsaw Man work and the most direct predecessor to understanding how he thinks. Agni burns eternally — an immortal regenerating body set permanently on fire — and seeks revenge against the woman who lit him. But Fire Punch is also about cinema, performance, narrative, and what it means to be the hero of your own story. More experimental than Chainsaw Man and darker in specific ways, but the DNA is identical.

**Best for:** Understanding where Chainsaw Man's creative instincts come from.

---

#### 2. [Dorohedoro](/manga/dorohedoro)

![Dorohedoro spread](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1542621334-a254cf47733d?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Q Hayashida | **Volumes:** 23 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The tonal DNA match is exact. Dorohedoro has Chainsaw Man's ability to be simultaneously funny, grotesque, violent, and warm — sometimes within the same page. The world operates on chaos logic that has internal consistency once you understand it. Caiman and Nikaido's friendship has Denji and Power's energy. The sorcerer/human dynamic maps onto devil/human hunter relationship.

Complete, with a satisfying ending. Non-negotiable recommendation.

---

#### 3. [Jujutsu Kaisen](/manga/jujutsu-kaisen)

![JJK manga spread](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614583225154-5fcdda07019e?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Gege Akutami | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The obvious companion piece — both are action horror series running in Weekly Shonen Jump, both have protagonists who carry cursed/devil power inside them, both are willing to let characters lose badly. JJK's Shibuya arc and Chainsaw Man's Gun Devil arc are structurally similar: extended sequences where nothing goes right and the damage accumulates.

The difference is scale and tone — JJK is more traditionally shonen in its ensemble structure; Chainsaw Man is more personal.

---

#### 4. [Tokyo Ghoul](/manga/tokyo-ghoul)

![Tokyo Ghoul manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1518791841217-8f162f1912fe?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Sui Ishida | **Volumes:** 14 (+ 16 for :re) | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Ken Kaneki becomes half-ghoul after an attack and navigates the underground ghoul society while struggling with his hybrid identity. The "protagonist as monster who wants to be human" structure is Chainsaw Man's Denji dynamic — the horror of being the thing you fight. Ishida's art is among the most expressive in horror manga.

Note: Tokyo Ghoul:re (the sequel) is divisive; the original 14-volume series has a cleaner arc.

---

#### 5. [Dungeon Meshi (Delicious in Dungeon)](/manga/dungeon-meshi)

**Author:** Ryoko Kui | **Volumes:** 14 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Not action horror in the traditional sense, but Dungeon Meshi's darkness — the dungeon ecology as a system of consumption, the corruption arc's horror elements, the nature of what the dungeon actually *is* — combined with its warm ensemble and dark comedy has Chainsaw Man's tonal balance.

---

#### 6. [Gantz](/manga/gantz)

**Author:** Hiroya Oku | **Volumes:** 37 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Pure action horror on a larger scale. The alien hunting, the body horror, the moral corruption of survival — Gantz is Chainsaw Man's violence and emptiness with less heart and more nihilism. More extreme in content. Recommended for readers who want the darkness dialed up.

---

#### 7. [Hellsing](/manga/hellsing)

![Hellsing manga page](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583416750470-965b2707b355?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Kouta Hirano | **Volumes:** 10 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Alucard — the most powerful vampire in existence, serving a British organization that hunts supernatural threats. Hellsing has Chainsaw Man's "ultimate weapon as employee" structure and the same visual commitment to spectacular violence. Hirano's art becomes increasingly chaotic and maximalist as the series progresses, which is either its best or worst quality depending on your taste.

---

#### 8. [Devilman Crybaby (Original Devilman)](/manga/devilman)

The foundational text — Chainsaw Man's devil/human fusion concept traces directly back here.

---

#### 9. [Solo Leveling](/manga/solo-leveling) *(Manhwa)*

The monster-hunting agency structure, the escalating threats, and the protagonist's relationship to his own power as something outside him have Chainsaw Man's "tool of the system" quality.

---

#### 10. [Sweet Home](/manga/sweet-home) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Kim Carnby, Youngchan Hwang | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

The body horror, the monster design creativity, and the protagonist's ambiguous relationship with his own monstrousness are direct Chainsaw Man parallels in a survival horror register.

---

#### 11. [Blood Lad](/manga/blood-lad)

**Author:** Yuuki Kodama | **Volumes:** 17 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A vampire overlord obsessed with Japanese culture helps a human girl's ghost get her body back. Much lighter than Chainsaw Man but shares the comedic-horror tonal balance and the "supernatural figure with embarrassingly mundane desires" protagonist archetype.

---

#### 12. [Deadman Wonderland](/manga/deadman-wonderland)

Already recommended — the institutionalized violence and the protagonist as weapon structure.

---

#### 13. [Oshi no Ko](/manga/oshi-no-ko)

**Author:** Aka Akasaka (story), Mengo Yokoyama (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

Not horror, but Oshi no Ko's willingness to depict industry, ambition, and parasocial relationships as genuinely monstrous things has Chainsaw Man's "the real horror is the system" quality applied to the entertainment industry.

---

### Comparison Table

| Title | Gore Level | Dark Comedy | Complete? | Format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fire Punch | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐ | ✅ | Manga |
| Dorohedoro | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ✅ | Manga |
| JJK | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐ | ✅ | Manga |
| Tokyo Ghoul | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐ | ✅ | Manga |
| Sweet Home | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐ | ✅ | Manhwa |
| Hellsing | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐ | ✅ | Manga |

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is Chainsaw Man Part 2 as good as Part 1?**
Part 2 is more experimental and deliberately slower. Asa Mitaka is a more complex protagonist than Denji. Reader opinions are divided — it's Fujimoto doing something harder and less immediately satisfying, which either earns your patience or loses it.

**Q: Does Dorohedoro have an ending?**
Yes — 23 volumes, complete and satisfying. The Netflix anime covers roughly the first third.

**Q: Should I read the Chainsaw Man manga if I've watched the anime?**
The anime covers Part 1's first half. The manga continues into arcs the anime hasn't reached and the original art has qualities the adaptation doesn't fully capture.

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked Dandadan, Read These Supernatural Comedy Manga

![Cover: A chaotic street scene with something uncanny in the background](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1559827260-dc66d52bef19?w=800&q=80)
*Image: When aliens, ghosts, and teenage romance collide — that's Dandadan*

**Category:** Modern Hits | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Dandadan: Chaos as Love Language

Yukinobu Tatsu's Dandadan is the most energetically alive manga running in Weekly Shonen Jump+ right now. The premise — a girl who believes in ghosts and a boy who believes in aliens both get proven right simultaneously and then become the universe's problem together — gives it an irresistible comic engine. But the reason Dandadan became a phenomenon rather than just a fun read is the art: Tatsu draws supernatural action with a kinetic expressiveness that makes every page feel like it's vibrating.

The romance is genuinely charming in a "both characters are too chaotic and brave to be coy about their feelings" way. The supernatural threats — ghosts, aliens, turbo-granny, and increasingly cosmic horrors — are inventive in ways that feel fresh. And the tonal whiplash (gut-wrenching emotional moment → insane comedy → horror sequence → emotional again) is perfectly calibrated.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Mob Psycho 100](/manga/mob-psycho-100)

![Mob Psycho 100 spread](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** ONE | **Volumes:** 16 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The most direct parallel. Mob is a psychically overpowered middle schooler navigating ghost-fighting and social anxiety. ONE's art style is deliberately crude in the manga, which is both its most distinctive quality and its biggest barrier — if you've only seen the anime, the manga will take adjustment. But ONE's comedic timing and emotional instinct are extraordinary.

---

#### 2. [Urusei Yatsura](/manga/urusei-yatsura)

![Urusei Yatsura cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614583224978-f05ce51ef5fa?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Rumiko Takahashi | **Volumes:** 34 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The ur-text of supernatural romantic comedy manga. Lum the alien girl falls in love with the most unlucky boy in the world, and the resulting chaos across 34 volumes established every convention Dandadan playfully deconstructs. The 2022 anime remake is exceptional. The manga rewards reading for its historical influence alone.

---

#### 3. [Ranma ½](/manga/ranma-half)

**Author:** Rumiko Takahashi | **Volumes:** 38 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Takahashi again — a martial artist who turns into a girl when splashed with cold water. Ranma ½'s comedic engine (the transformation gimmick generating endless situational comedy) prefigures Dandadan's use of supernatural conditions as comedy sources. The romance is both sincere and perpetually stalled in a way that feels appropriately chaotic.

---

#### 4. [Noragami](/manga/noragami)

Already recommended — the supernatural-world structure and the tonal flexibility (comedy → emotional → action) matches Dandadan's register.

---

#### 5. [The Disastrous Life of Saiki K.](/manga/the-disastrous-life-of-saiki-k)

![Saiki K manga spread](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578632767115-351597cf2477?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Shūichi Asō | **Volumes:** 26 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A massively overpowered psychic just wants a quiet life and keeps getting dragged into situations by his oblivious classmates. Saiki K. is the purest supernatural comedy on this list — no horror, no romance drama, just escalating absurdism executed with exceptional timing.

---

#### 6. [Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun](/manga/toilet-bound-hanako-kun)

![Hanako-kun manga art](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1518791841217-8f162f1912fe?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** AidaIro | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A girl summons a bathroom ghost to grant a wish and ends up bound to him as his assistant. The school mystery structure, the folklore-based supernatural threats, and the relationship between the two leads — genuinely complicated, emotionally rich — give Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun Dandadan's "supernatural premise as relationship engine" quality in a more melancholy register.

---

#### 7. [Komi Can't Communicate](/manga/komi-cant-communicate)

**Author:** Tomohito Oda | **Volumes:** 30 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Not supernatural, but Komi's chaotic school social landscape and the escalating cast of eccentric characters has Dandadan's "increasingly weird people accumulate around a central relationship" structure.

---

#### 8. [Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead](/manga/zom-100)

**Author:** Haro Aso (story), Kotaro Takata (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A man liberated by the zombie apocalypse makes a bucket list of things to do before he dies. The comedy-horror tonal blend and the "find joy in catastrophe" emotional register has Dandadan's chaotic optimism.

---

#### 9. [I Love You So I'll Kill You](/manga/i-love-you-so-ill-kill-you) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Iri | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A supernatural comedy romance with the same "chaotic supernatural circumstances drive romantic tension" engine as Dandadan.

---

#### 10. [True Beauty](/manga/true-beauty) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Yaongyi | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Korean Manhwa (LINE Webtoon)

A girl who is insecure about her bare face masters makeup and becomes the school beauty. Less supernatural, but the comedic romantic scenarios and the genuinely chaotic situations the leads fall into have Dandadan's romantic comedy energy in a contemporary realistic setting.

---

#### 11. [A Returner's Magic Should Be Special](/manga/a-returners-magic-should-be-special) *(Manhwa)*

The hidden world of supernatural threat plus the central relationship developed under pressure parallels Dandadan's structure.

---

#### 12. [The World After the Fall](/manga/the-world-after-the-fall) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Sing Shong (story), Undead Gamja (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

Post-apocalyptic survival with a comedic edge and supernatural system. The tonal flexibility — dark premise, light execution — is Dandadan-coded.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is Dandadan ongoing?**
Yes — serialized in Shonen Jump+ as of 2025. The anime (MAPPA) has been well-received and is also ongoing.

**Q: What's Dandadan's romance status as of the current arc?**
Momo and Okarun's relationship has progressed beyond the "awkward mutual feelings" stage. The series is developing it naturally alongside the supernatural action.

**Q: Is the Urusei Yatsura remake a good starting point?**
The 2022 anime remake is excellent and a valid starting point. The manga is more episodic and rewards reading after the anime.

---

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked Kaiju No. 8, Read These Monster Manga

![Cover: A massive silhouette against a burning city skyline](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1519681393784-d120267933ba?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: The monster was always the one standing in the rubble, still trying*

**Category:** Modern Hits | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Kaiju No. 8: The Monster Inside the Hero

Naoya Matsumoto's Kaiju No. 8 is the most commercially successful manga launch of the early 2020s, and its appeal is straightforward: a 32-year-old man who has failed to achieve his dream of joining an elite monster-fighting force gains monster powers and gets a second shot. Kafka Hibino is a rare shonen protagonist with adult problems — the weight of a decade of failed attempts, the friendship tested by one person succeeding while the other didn't, the specific humiliation of being good at cleaning up after the heroes instead of being one.

The kaiju designs are spectacular. The combat mechanics are satisfying. But the heart of the series is Kafka's emotional realism in a genre that usually reserves adults for mentor roles.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Attack on Titan](/manga/attack-on-titan)

![AoT spread](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1506905925346-21bda4d32df4?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Hajime Isayama | **Volumes:** 34 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The foundational modern monster manga. The Survey Corps defending humanity against Titans has the same organizational structure as Kaiju No. 8's Defense Force, and the gradual revelation that the monsters have an internal logic gives both series their most compelling second-act twist.

---

#### 2. [Chainsaw Man](/manga/chainsaw-man)

The protagonist-as-monster-hybrid structure is the most direct parallel.

---

#### 3. [Neon Genesis Evangelion](/manga/neon-genesis-evangelion)

The "child/young person as weapon against incomprehensible monsters" structure, the organization controlling both humans and weapons, and the body horror of the human-monster interface — all NGE, all recognizable in Kaiju No. 8.

---

#### 4. [Devilman](/manga/devilman)

Go Nagai's original hybrid-hero concept is the ancestor of the entire "human gains monster power" narrative.

---

#### 5. [Ultraman (Manga)](/manga/ultraman-manga)

![Ultraman manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541701494587-cb58502866ab?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Eiichi Shimizu (story), Tomohiro Shimoguchi (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

The Ultraman suit as power armor worn by the son of the original Ultraman. The tokusatsu genre rendered in manga form with high production values and genuine narrative ambition. Kaiju No. 8 is in direct conversation with this tradition.

---

#### 6. [Ajin: Demi-Human](/manga/ajin)

![Ajin manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1559827260-dc66d52bef19?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Gamon Sakurai | **Volumes:** 17 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Humans who discover they cannot die — Ajin — are hunted by the government for use as research subjects. The protagonist is an Ajin who chooses resistance. The "human with monster-adjacent power in a world that fears that power" structure maps precisely onto Kafka's situation.

---

#### 7. [Goblin Slayer](/manga/goblin-slayer)

The professional monster-elimination organization, the specific tactics of fighting inhuman threats, and the protagonist's unusual relationship to his own identity within that system.

---

#### 8. [Tokyo Ghoul](/manga/tokyo-ghoul)

The hybrid identity crisis and the fighting-force organizational structure.

---

#### 9. [The God of High School](/manga/the-god-of-high-school) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Yongje Park | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

Starts as a martial arts tournament and escalates to divine monster combat. The scale expansion — human fighting → divine-being conflict — mirrors Kaiju No. 8's escalating threat tiers.

---

#### 10. [Tower of God](/manga/tower-of-god) *(Webtoon)*

The organizational hierarchy of fighters, the escalating creature/challenge tiers, and the protagonist's anomalous power source.

---

#### 11. [Noblesse](/manga/noblesse) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Son Jeho (story), Lee Kwangsu (art) | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A powerful noble vampire wakes up in modern Korea and navigates high school while a secret organization of modified humans threatens world order. The "ancient power in a modern institutional context" and the monster-classification system have Kaiju No. 8 energy.

---

#### 12. [Solo Leveling](/manga/solo-leveling) *(Manhwa)*

The hunter organization structure, the monster classification system (ranks A through S), and the protagonist's transformation from weak to overwhelmingly powerful within a formal institutional framework.

---

#### 13. [Eleceed](/manga/eleceed) *(Manhwa)*

The hidden world of ability users with an organizational structure, and the protagonist's discovery of power he doesn't fully understand.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is Kaiju No. 8 manga ahead of the anime?**
Significantly — the anime adapts the first arc. The manga has continued into substantially more complex territory.

**Q: Does Kafka's secret stay secret for long?**
The tension around Kafka's secret is managed carefully — revelations happen gradually and each one reshapes the power dynamics of his relationships. Not stretched beyond reason.

---

# If You Liked If You Liked Sakamoto Days, Read These Action Comedy Manga

![Cover: A convenience store at night, oddly peaceful, with something dangerous just outside](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1604719312566-8912e9227c6a?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: The most dangerous man in the world just wants to run his convenience store in peace*

**Category:** Modern Hits | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Sakamoto Days: Action Comedy Done Right

Yuto Suzuki's Sakamoto Days works because it respects both halves of its genre label equally. Taro Sakamoto — formerly the world's greatest hitman — retired to marry a woman he fell in love with at first sight, gained weight, opened a convenience store, and became a devoted family man. He's also still, inarguably, the most dangerous person in any room he enters. The comedy comes from watching a man of extraordinary violence navigate domestic contentment. The action earns its spectacle through Suzuki's exceptional choreography.

Most action comedies sacrifice one element. Sakamoto Days refuses.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [One Punch Man](/manga/one-punch-man)

![OPM manga spread](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** ONE (story), Yusuke Murata (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

The most obvious companion piece — a hero so powerful that every fight ends in one punch, whose genuine problem is boredom and lack of recognition. Murata's art is the most technically accomplished action art in current manga. The comedy and the action both operate at the highest level.

---

#### 2. [Spy × Family](/manga/spy-x-family)

![Spy × Family manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614583225154-5fcdda07019e?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Tatsuya Endo | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A spy, an assassin, and a telepathic child maintain a fake family while each pursuing separate secret objectives. The domestic comedy wrapped around professional violence, and the way sincere family warmth gradually grows from a purely tactical arrangement, is exactly Sakamoto Days' emotional register.

---

#### 3. [Gintama](/manga/gintama)

![Gintama manga panel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583416750470-965b2707b355?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Hideaki Sorachi | **Volumes:** 77 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The gold standard of action comedy manga. An alien invasion has conquered feudal Japan, and a silver-haired samurai runs an odd-jobs business while refusing to grow up. Gintama's comedy is the most ambitious in manga — parody, absurdism, political satire, and emotional gut-punches alternating without warning. The action arcs (Yoshiwara in Flames, Farewell Shinsengumi) are genuinely excellent.

The length (77 volumes) is intimidating but the series has a specific reading experience — the comedic chapters reset the emotional register between arcs — that makes it sustainable.

---

#### 4. [Assassination Classroom (Ansatsu Kyoushitsu)](/manga/assassination-classroom)

![Ansatsu Kyoushitsu cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1529699211952-734e80c4d42b?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Yusei Matsui | **Volumes:** 21 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A class of underachieving students must kill their teacher — a tentacled monster who destroyed the moon and plans to destroy Earth — before graduation. The assassin-as-teacher inversion and the comedy/action balance is Sakamoto Days energy in a school setting. The emotional final act is one of the most satisfying in modern shonen.

---

#### 5. [Mashle: Magic and Muscles](/manga/mashle)

**Author:** Hajime Komoto | **Volumes:** 16 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

In a world where magic determines social status, a physically extraordinary boy who has no magic attends a magic school and punches his way through every obstacle. The deadpan protagonist surrounded by increasingly absurd situations, the parody of genre conventions, and the action that's actually good underneath the comedy — all Sakamoto Days-adjacent.

---

#### 6. [The Way of the Househusband](/manga/way-of-the-househusband)

![Househusband manga panel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1542621334-a254cf47733d?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Kousuke Oono | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

The most direct Sakamoto Days parallel: a legendary yakuza who becomes a devoted househusband and applies his criminal-world intensity to grocery shopping and cooking. Pure comedy, minimal action — but the premise is identical in concept and the execution is hilarious.

---

#### 7. [Undead Unluck](/manga/undead-unluck)

**Author:** Yoshifumi Tozuka | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

The escalating "Negators vs. the system" conflict has Sakamoto Days' organizational structure and the duo at the center has that same "unlikely partnership becomes genuine affection" arc.

---

#### 8. [Black Clover](/manga/black-clover)

The comedic elements of Asta's character and the Magic Knight organizational structure have Sakamoto Days energy, though Black Clover takes itself more seriously.

---

#### 9. [Noblesse](/manga/noblesse) *(Manhwa)*

Already mentioned — the noble vampire navigating modern school life has the same "overwhelming power trying to live normally" comedy structure.

---

#### 10. [I Love Yoo](/manga/i-love-yoo) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Rachel Smythe | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Webcomic

Different genre (romance), but the comedy-action-sincerity balance and the way humor serves emotional honesty rather than deflecting from it has Sakamoto Days' tonal discipline.

---

#### 11. [Weak Hero](/manga/weak-hero) *(Manhwa)*

The tactical intelligence under physical pressure and the deadpan analytical protagonist are Sakamoto Days qualities applied to a school thriller.

---

#### 12. [Viral Hit (How to Fight)](/manga/viral-hit) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Taejun Pak | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A bullied student discovers a YouTube channel teaching self-defense and becomes a fighter by following its instructions. The "ordinary person learning extraordinary violence" comedy arc and the social dynamics of fighting ability in a school setting has Sakamoto Days' "violence as domestic life" quality in a more grounded register.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is Sakamoto Days getting an anime?**
Yes — the anime adaptation launched in early 2025 and has been well-received. The manga is substantially ahead.

**Q: Where does Gintama get good?**
The series finds its rhythm around chapter 50-100. The first major "serious arc" (Four Devas arc) is around chapter 300, but the comedic chapters before it establish the emotional investment that makes those arcs work.

**Q: Is The Way of the Househusband more comedy than action?**
Almost entirely comedy. If you want the action component, Sakamoto Days is the recommendation. Househusband is for the premise without the fights.

---

# If You Liked If You Liked Fire Force, Read These Supernatural Manga

![Cover: Flames rising from a city street at night — controlled and terrifying](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1518544866330-4e716499f800?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: Fire Force asked: what if firefighters fought fire that thought?*

**Category:** Modern Hits | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Fire Force: The Ōkubo Universe

Atsushi Ōkubo created Soul Eater before Fire Force, and reading both reveals a consistent creative vision: structured supernatural organizations, unique ability systems where the visual design of a power reflects the personality of its user, and an escalating mythology that moves from local to cosmic. Fire Force adds a new element — the religious organization as primary antagonist — that gives it a political texture Soul Eater didn't have.

Shinra Kusakabe's "devil's footprints" ability (flight via fire from his feet), the Company structure of the Special Fire Force, and the gradually revealed truth about spontaneous human combustion give Fire Force a strong mechanical foundation. The ending is ambitious if somewhat rushed.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Soul Eater](/manga/soul-eater)

Already covered — the direct predecessor by the same creator. Essential.

---

#### 2. [Blue Exorcist](/manga/blue-exorcist)

The supernatural organization fighting demonic threats, the protagonist with power from the "wrong" source, and the religious institutions as complex actors rather than simple good/evil.

---

#### 3. [D.Gray-man](/manga/d-gray-man)

The Exorcist organization, the religious aesthetics, and the gradual revelation that the institution has darker motives.

---

#### 4. [Noragami](/manga/noragami)

The divine bureaucracy and the human-divine interface.

---

#### 5. [Black Clover](/manga/black-clover)

The Magic Knight squad structure mirrors Fire Force's Company structure exactly.

---

#### 6. [Fullmetal Alchemist](/manga/fullmetal-alchemist)

The religious-state conspiracy, the "what the institution is actually for," and the alchemy system's visual elegance parallel Fire Force's power design.

---

#### 7. [Jujutsu Kaisen](/manga/jujutsu-kaisen)

The sorcerer organization, the cursed technique visual identities, and the escalating cosmic threat with religious overtones.

---

#### 8. [Tower of God](/manga/tower-of-god) *(Webtoon)*

The organizational hierarchy, the escalating ability tiers, and the divine-organization as controller of human fate.

---

#### 9. [Noblesse](/manga/noblesse) *(Manhwa)*

The hidden organization, the supernatural ability classification, and the protagonist's anomalous power within a formal structure.

---

#### 10. [God of Highschool](/manga/god-of-highschool) *(Manhwa)*

The Korean mythological divine power system and the escalating tournament-to-divine-war structure parallel Fire Force's religious mythology expansion.

---

#### 11. [Hardcore Leveling Warrior](/manga/hardcore-leveling-warrior) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Sehun Kim | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

The game-world ability structure and the escalating threats within a system governed by invisible higher powers.

---

#### 12. [The Breaker](/manga/the-breaker) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Jeon Geuk-jin (story), Park Jin-hwan (art) | **Volumes:** 10 (+ New Waves 20 vol) | **Status:** Complete + Sequel | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A high school student becomes involved with the world of murim (Korean martial arts underworld) through his mysterious teacher. The hidden-world reveal, the organizational hierarchy of martial arts schools, and the protagonist's anomalous power source have Fire Force's "ordinary person discovers the world has supernatural structure" quality.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Does Fire Force connect to Soul Eater?**
Yes — the ending of Fire Force reveals a canonical connection to the Soul Eater universe. It's best experienced without spoilers.

**Q: Is the Fire Force anime faithful to the manga?**
Largely yes, with some pacing differences. The manga's final act is more detailed.

---

# If You Liked If You Liked Kaguya-sama: Love Is War, Read These Romance Manga

![Cover: Two students on opposite sides of a library table, both pretending to read](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1524995997946-a1c2e315a42f?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: The longest distance between two people who like each other is pride*

**Category:** Romance | **Reading Time:** ~14 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Kaguya-sama: The Intelligence of Romantic Comedy

Aka Akasaka wrote one of the most precisely constructed romantic comedies in the history of the genre. Kaguya-sama: Love Is War treats the "who confesses first loses" premise with genuine strategic rigor — the battles between Kaguya and Miyuki are games of social chess where every move has a counter-move — while building a genuine emotional foundation underneath the comedy.

The series earns its finale because it took its characters seriously even when it was being absurd. Kaguya's arc from emotionally suppressed heir to someone who chooses her own feelings is the kind of growth that requires 22 volumes to feel real. The supporting cast — Chika, Ishigami, Iino — are written with the same care, and their arcs carry the later volumes after the central confession arc concludes.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Horimiya](/manga/horimiya)

![Horimiya manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1524995997946-a1c2e315a42f?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** HERO (story), Daisuke Hagiwara (art) | **Volumes:** 16 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Two students discover they have hidden sides to their personalities and fall into a relationship that's unexpectedly honest and direct. Horimiya's great quality is that the central couple actually *gets together* early and then spends the rest of the series being a couple — no artificial delay, just the actual difficulty of two people learning each other.

---

#### 2. [Nisekoi: False Love](/manga/nisekoi)

**Author:** Naoshi Komi | **Volumes:** 25 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

The yakuza's son and the gangster's daughter fake-date to keep their families from going to war. Classic romantic comedy structure with an ensemble of love interests, escalating ridiculous scenarios, and — controversial opinion — a genuinely satisfying ending for those who supported the right girl.

---

#### 3. [Oregairu (My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong as I Expected)](/manga/oregairu)

**Author:** Wataru Watari (story), Io Naomichi (art) | **Volumes:** 14 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Hachiman Hikigaya is the most honest deconstruction of the loner protagonist archetype in romantic comedy. The series is less comedic and more literary than Kaguya-sama — more interested in why people protect themselves with performance than in the games they play.

---

#### 4. [Takagi-san (Karakai Jouzu no Takagi-san)](/manga/takagi-san)

**Author:** Sōichirō Yamamoto | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A girl teases her classmate relentlessly with supernatural accuracy. The series is almost a micro-version of Kaguya-sama — the power dynamics of who notices what, who is ahead, who has admitted more to themselves — but quieter and gentler.

---

#### 5. [Teasing Master Takagi-san (continuation and spinoffs)](/manga/takagi-san-spinoffs)

The adult spinoff (Karakai Jouzu no (Moto) Takagi-san) showing Takagi and Nishikata as a married couple with a daughter is the best possible answer to anyone who wants to see how Kaguya and Miyuki turn out.

---

#### 6. [My Love Story (Ore Monogatari!!)](/manga/my-love-story)

![My Love Story cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1519681393784-d120267933ba?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Kazune Kawahara (story), Aruko (art) | **Volumes:** 13 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A giant, intimidating boy and a gentle girl fall in love immediately and actually say so — no games, no delay, no "who confesses first." My Love Story is Kaguya-sama's complete tonal opposite and a beautiful antidote to the "dragged out confession" format.

---

#### 7. [We Never Learn (Bokutachi wa Benkyou ga Dekinai)](/manga/we-never-learn)

**Author:** Taishi Tsutsui | **Volumes:** 21 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A tutor helps multiple genius girls who are terrible at their particular genius subjects. The harem structure is managed with more emotional seriousness than most series in the format, and each route's ending (the manga has multiple endings in a branching structure) is given genuine weight.

---

#### 8. [Love is War: The After Story](/manga/kaguya-sama-after-story)

Aka Akasaka's continuation following the confirmed couple navigating a long-distance relationship. For anyone who finished the main series and wanted more.

---

#### 9. [True Beauty](/manga/true-beauty) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Yaongyi | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Korean Manhwa (LINE Webtoon)

A girl who is insecure about her bare face becomes the school beauty through makeup skill. The love triangle, the hidden-identity structure, and the genuinely funny situational comedy make True Beauty one of the most popular manhwa romances globally. The ending is divisive but the journey is excellent.

---

#### 10. [Yumi's Cells](/manga/yumis-cells) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Lee Dong-gun | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

An office worker's romantic life told from the perspective of the cells running her brain — literally. The "inside the head of someone who is bad at feelings" structure is Kaguya-sama's premise from the inside rather than from the chess-game outside view. Utterly charming and emotionally devastating in equal measure.

---

#### 11. [I Love Yoo](/manga/i-love-yoo) *(Webcomic)*

**Author:** Rachel Smythe | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Webcomic (LINE Webtoon)

A girl who doesn't believe in romantic love encounters two brothers who complicate that position. The character writing is sophisticated and the slow-burn is genuinely well-managed.

---

#### 12. [My ID is Gangnam Beauty](/manga/my-id-is-gangnam-beauty) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Maengi | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A girl who had plastic surgery to escape bullying navigates college social life. The honest examination of appearance, self-worth, and romantic worthiness has Kaguya-sama's "what people will and won't say about how they feel" thematic territory in a completely realistic register.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Which Kaguya-sama arc is the best?**
The Culture Festival arc (volumes 13–17) is widely considered the series peak. The Confession arc's resolution is the emotional climax most readers built toward.

**Q: Is the Kaguya-sama anime faithful?**
Very — A-1 Pictures' adaptation is considered among the best romantic comedy anime productions. Watch after reading or alongside.

**Q: What's the reading order for Horimiya?**
The original webcomic (Hori-san to Miyamura-kun) → Horimiya manga (adaptation) → Horimiya: Piece (spinoff). The core manga is the recommended read.

---

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked Horimiya, Read These Romance Manga

![Cover: A school hallway in late afternoon light, two figures walking slightly closer than necessary](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1503454537195-1dcabb73ffb9?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: The best romances aren't about the confession — they're about everything after*

**Category:** Romance | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Horimiya: Romance That Respects Its Readers

The revolutionary thing about Horimiya isn't the art or the premise — it's the pacing decision. HERO and Hagiwara let Hori and Miyamura get together in volume 3 and then spent 13 more volumes figuring out what being together actually means. In a genre where artificial delay is the primary structural tool, Horimiya chose honesty over tension management.

That honesty extends to the characters themselves. Hori's possessiveness, Miyamura's self-doubt, the way they communicate badly and then figure out how to communicate better — these are adult relationship dynamics written into a high school romance with unusual maturity.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Kaguya-sama: Love Is War](/manga/kaguya-sama-love-is-war)

Already covered — the companion piece with opposite pacing philosophy.

---

#### 2. [My Love Story!!](/manga/my-love-story)

Already recommended — the "couple gets together immediately" cousin.

---

#### 3. [Takagi-san](/manga/takagi-san)

The small-scale everyday romance with genuine warmth.

---

#### 4. [A Silent Voice](/manga/a-silent-voice)

Not romance primarily — emotional drama — but the relationship at its center has Horimiya's "learning to actually see another person" quality.

---

#### 5. [Fruits Basket](/manga/fruits-basket)

The slow emotional opening of a closed-off person through genuine connection.

---

#### 6. [Tsubaki-chou Lonely Planet](/manga/tsubaki-chou-lonely-planet)

**Author:** Mika Yamamori | **Volumes:** 10 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A girl living alone becomes a housekeeper for a young novelist. The domestic intimacy and the gradual "seeing each other" arc has Horimiya's quiet emotional register.

---

#### 7. [Soredemo Sekai wa Utsukushii (Still Longing for You)](/manga/still-longing-for-you)

**Author:** Dai Shiina | **Volumes:** 16 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A princess summoned to marry a young conqueror king. The forced-proximity relationship that develops into genuine feeling has Horimiya's "circumstances brought us here, but choice keeps us" dynamic.

---

#### 8. [NANA](/manga/nana)

Already in the Emotional section — the most mature relationship manga, period.

---

#### 9. [I'll Be the Matriarch in This Life](/manga/ill-be-the-matriarch-in-this-life) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Aglae | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

Fantasy historical romance with a reincarnated protagonist. The relationship development — built on mutual respect before romantic feeling — has Horimiya's quality of two people genuinely choosing each other.

---

#### 10. [Under the Oak Tree](/manga/under-the-oak-tree) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Suji Kim | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A stuttering noble lady and her cold knight husband navigate a contracted marriage that becomes real. The healing of communication damage and the gradual intimacy building has Horimiya's "learning to say the things you actually mean" theme.

---

#### 11. [Cheese in the Trap](/manga/cheese-in-the-trap) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Soonkki | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A college girl navigates her complicated relationship with a charismatic senior who may not be what he appears. The realistic college romance setting, the psychological complexity of the leads, and the "what is this person actually thinking?" tension has Horimiya's character-interiority focus.

---

#### 12. [Yumi's Cells](/manga/yumis-cells) *(Manhwa)*

Already recommended — the internal experience of romantic relationship development.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is Horimiya: Piece worth reading?**
Piece is a collection of short chapters about side characters and alternate scenarios. Fun but not essential — read after the main series if you want more time in the world.

**Q: Is the Horimiya anime faithful?**
The 2021 anime is excellent but compresses significant content, particularly side character arcs. The manga has substantially more development for Ishigami, Yoshikawa, and others.

---

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked My Dress-Up Darling, Read These Romance Manga

![Cover: Colorful fabric swatches and a sewing kit — the tools of transformation](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1558769132-cb1aea458c5e?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: Cosplay is how some people finally become who they already were*

**Category:** Romance | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### My Dress-Up Darling: Passion as Romance Language

Shinichi Fukuda's My Dress-Up Darling (Sono Bisque Doll wa Koi wo Suru) works because both Wakana and Marin take their passions seriously and refuse to be embarrassed about them. Wakana's hina doll craftsmanship and Marin's cosplay enthusiasm are presented without condescension — the series treats hobby dedication as a form of emotional honesty, and the romance grows from two people respecting what each other loves.

The fanservice is present and deliberate, and that's worth acknowledging: Fukuda uses it as part of Wakana's characterization (his flustered, genuinely respectful responses to Marin) rather than as purely audience service. Whether that calculus works for individual readers is personal, but the emotional core is genuine regardless.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Kaguya-sama: Love Is War](/manga/kaguya-sama-love-is-war)

The honest-feeling-behind-the-game structure.

---

#### 2. [Horimiya](/manga/horimiya)

The hidden-side-of-personality reveal and the domestic warmth.

---

#### 3. [Wotakoi: Love is Hard for Otaku](/manga/wotakoi)

![Wotakoi manga cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1524995997946-a1c2e315a42f?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Fujita | **Volumes:** 10 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Adult otaku in workplace romance. The "two people whose passions are the basis for their connection" structure is exactly Dress-Up Darling in an office setting. Wotakoi also treats its characters' hobbies (gaming, BL manga, anime, cosplay) with the same respect Fukuda treats Marin's cosplay.

---

#### 4. [Genshiken](/manga/genshiken)

**Author:** Shimoku Kio | **Volumes:** 9 (+ Nidaime 11 vol) | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A university otaku club. Genshiken is the most realistic portrait of hobby communities in manga — the social dynamics, the internal culture, the relationships that form around shared enthusiasm. The romance is secondary to the community portrait but emerges naturally from it.

---

#### 5. [Gekkan Shoujo Nozaki-kun](/manga/gekkan-shoujo-nozaki-kun)

![Nozaki-kun manga panel](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1519681393784-d120267933ba?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Izumi Tsubaki | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A girl confesses to her crush and accidentally becomes his manga assistant. One of the funniest romance comedies in the medium — the manga-industry parody and the ensemble of comedic supporting characters are both exceptional. The central romance barely advances, which is either its greatest frustration or its greatest charm.

---

#### 6. [Takagi-san](/manga/takagi-san)

The quiet shared-hobby intimacy and the "knowing what the other person loves" romantic shorthand.

---

#### 7. [The Angel Next Door Spoils Me Rotten](/manga/the-angel-next-door-spoils-me-rotten)

**Author:** Saekisan (story), Wan Suwabe (art) | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A loner boy and the school's most beautiful girl are neighbors who gradually develop genuine friendship that tips into romance. The domestic intimacy and the "seeing beneath the public image" arc has Dress-Up Darling's quality.

---

#### 8. [My Hero Academia: Vigilantes](/manga/my-hero-academia-vigilantes)

Not romance — but Pop Step's character arc (hero-focused idol performer) has the "passion as identity" theme Dress-Up Darling develops with Marin.

---

#### 9. [True Beauty](/manga/true-beauty) *(Manhwa)*

The makeup-as-transformation and hidden-identity structure is Dress-Up Darling's cosplay premise in a contemporary Korean setting.

---

#### 10. [Let's Play](/manga/lets-play) *(Webcomic)*

**Author:** Mongie | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Webcomic (LINE Webtoon)

A girl who makes indie games has her debut overshadowed by a famous streamer who lives next door. The "passion project" romance and the creative-industry setting have Dress-Up Darling's "take what you love seriously" ethos.

---

#### 11. [I Love Yoo](/manga/i-love-yoo) *(Webcomic)*

The slow-burn between characters who gradually reveal more of themselves — the hidden-self-revealed-through-relationship arc.

---

#### 12. [Lore Olympus](/manga/lore-olympus) *(Webcomic)*

**Author:** Rachel Smythe | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Webcomic (LINE Webtoon)

Greek mythology retold as contemporary romance graphic novel. The visual style is unmistakable (pastel colors, anatomically stylized characters) and the Persephone/Hades relationship has the "powerful figure treated as object who finds genuine connection" arc that gives Dress-Up Darling its emotional core.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is My Dress-Up Darling manga complete?**
No — ongoing as of 2025. The romance has progressed meaningfully.

**Q: Is the anime faithful?**
Yes — the CloverWorks adaptation is excellent and widely considered among the best romance anime productions of recent years.

---

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked Komi Can't Communicate, Read These Slice of Life Manga

![Cover: A classroom window at sunset — the quiet hour between school and home](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1503454537195-1dcabb73ffb9?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: Some of the most important things that happen, happen quietly*

**Category:** Romance | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Komi Can't Communicate: Social Anxiety as Superpower

Tomohito Oda's Komi Can't Communicate treats its premise with the warmth it deserves: Komi Shouko is perceived as a goddess of beauty and composure, but she has debilitating social anxiety that makes communication nearly impossible. Tadano Hitohito notices what everyone else misses — that she's terrified — and becomes her first friend.

The series then does something remarkable: it spends 30 volumes watching Komi make 100 friends, one uncomfortable conversation at a time. Each new character is a comedic portrait of social eccentricity, and Oda's gift is that every one of them is treated as deserving of the connection they awkwardly reach for. It's the warmest manga running in Weekly Shonen Jump.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [Takagi-san](/manga/takagi-san)

The quiet, everyday warmth and the specific intimacy of two people paying close attention to each other.

---

#### 2. [Horimiya](/manga/horimiya)

The ensemble cast developed alongside the central relationship.

---

#### 3. [Monthly Girls' Nozaki-kun](/manga/gekkan-shoujo-nozaki-kun)

The comedic school social landscape and the ensemble of eccentric characters.

---

#### 4. [My Roommate is a Cat](/manga/my-roommate-is-a-cat)

**Author:** Minatsuki (story), Asu Futatsuya (art) | **Volumes:** 12 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A reclusive mystery author adopts a stray cat and gradually opens up to the world around him through the responsibility of caring for another creature. The social anxiety → gradual connection arc is Komi-san's emotional template in an adult register.

---

#### 5. [Wotakoi: Love is Hard for Otaku](/manga/wotakoi)

Adult social anxiety within a hobby community — same emotional territory, older characters.

---

#### 6. [The Helpful Fox Senko-san](/manga/helpful-fox-senko-san)

**Author:** Rimukoro | **Volumes:** 12 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

An overworked salaryman is visited by an ancient fox deity who wants to pamper him. Pure comfort — the slice of life warmth without any social anxiety or conflict.

---

#### 7. [Yotsuba&!](/manga/yotsuba)

![Yotsuba manga page](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1558769132-cb1aea458c5e?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Kiyohiko Azuma | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

A young girl and her father move to a new town, and Yotsuba discovers the ordinary world is full of extraordinary things. The most purely joyful manga in the medium. No conflict, no stakes, no romance — just a child experiencing the world with complete openness. Reading Yotsuba&! is one of the most calming experiences available in manga form.

---

#### 8. [Laid-Back Camp (Yuru Camp)](/manga/laid-back-camp)

**Author:** Afro | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Manga

Girls go solo and group camping. That's the entire premise, and it's perfect. The specificity of camping knowledge (gear, locations, weather, food), the quiet pleasure of being outdoors, and the warmth of the friendships formed around shared experience make Laid-Back Camp a masterclass in cozy manga.

---

#### 9. [Dungeon Meshi (for the warmth)](/manga/dungeon-meshi)

The found family around a shared meal — Dungeon Meshi's warmth is available even to readers who don't engage with its darker elements.

---

#### 10. [True Beauty](/manga/true-beauty) *(Manhwa)*

The social dynamics of high school appearance and the genuine friendships formed beneath the beauty-status hierarchy.

---

#### 11. [Webtoon: Let's Play](/manga/lets-play) *(Webcomic)*

The social anxiety protagonist navigating creative industry and neighborhood relationships.

---

#### 12. [Orange](/manga/orange)

The slice of life texture of teenage friendship and the small moments that constitute a life — covered more in the Emotional section below.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Does Komi Can't Communicate have an ending?**
The series concluded in 2024 — 34 volumes, fully complete. The 100-friends goal is achieved.

**Q: Is the Netflix anime faithful?**
The first two seasons cover the early arcs faithfully. Recommended as an entry point.

---

body:
# If You Liked If You Liked Nisekoi, Read These Romance Comedy Manga

![Cover: Two students surrounded by a confused tangle of lockets and keys](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1524995997946-a1c2e315a42f?w=1200&q=80)
*Image: Nisekoi proved that the journey matters even when everyone knows the destination*

**Category:** Romance | **Reading Time:** ~13 min | **Last Updated:** 2025

---

### Nisekoi: The Harem That Knew What It Was

Naoshi Komi's Nisekoi is the most self-aware harem manga in Weekly Shonen Jump's history. The childhood promise / locket mystery structure is deliberately drawn out, the love interests are deliberately archetypal (tsundere, kuudere, childhood friend), and the series periodically winks at its own conventions. What makes it work isn't originality — it's execution. Komi's art is beautiful, the character designs are distinctive, and each girl gets enough genuine development to make her route feel real.

The ending remains controversial in a way that actively misses the point — Nisekoi was always about the journey, and which girl "won" was always less important than which chapters made you feel most.

---

### Top Picks

---

#### 1. [We Never Learn](/manga/we-never-learn)

Already recommended — the multi-ending structure takes the "which girl?" question seriously.

---

#### 2. [The Quintessential Quintuplets](/manga/quintessential-quintuplets)

![Quintessential Quintuplets cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1519681393784-d120267933ba?w=800&q=80)

**Author:** Negi Haruba | **Volumes:** 14 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Five identical sisters hire a tutor. The mystery-romance structure (who is the girl from his past?) gives Quintessential Quintuplets Nisekoi's "childhood promise" hook while developing each sister with genuine depth. The ending is declared in the first chapter and still manages to feel earned.

---

#### 3. [Ranma ½](/manga/ranma-half)

The multiple love interests, the escalating situational comedy, and the central pairing that refuses to acknowledge itself.

---

#### 4. [To Love Ru](/manga/to-love-ru)

**Author:** Saki Hasemi (story), Kentaro Yabuki (art) | **Volumes:** 18 (+ Darkness 20 vol) | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

Alien princess lands in a boy's bathtub and declares herself his fiancée. The harem expands considerably. To Love Ru is the most unabashedly fanservice-focused recommendation on this list, but for readers who liked Nisekoi's comedy and love triangle energy and want more of the former with less of the latter restraint.

---

#### 5. [Yamada-kun and the Seven Witches](/manga/yamada-kun-and-the-seven-witches)

**Author:** Miki Yoshikawa | **Volumes:** 28 | **Status:** Complete | **Format:** Manga

A delinquent discovers he can exchange abilities with people by kissing them. The supernatural gimmick, the expanding cast of witches, and the central relationship built on repeated physical proximity has Nisekoi's comedic romantic escalation.

---

#### 6. [Takagi-san](/manga/takagi-san)

For readers who want the "who's winning?" tension in a two-person rather than multi-person format.

---

#### 7. [My Hero Academia: The Lighter Side](/manga/mha-smash)

Not romance — but the comedic shonen energy between arcs is the register Nisekoi operates in.

---

#### 8. [True Beauty](/manga/true-beauty) *(Manhwa)*

The love triangle with distinctly drawn love interests and the hidden-identity structure.

---

#### 9. [Sweet Home (not the horror)](/manga/sweet-home-romance) *(Manhwa)*

Romance manhwa with a similar "chaotic household" comedic setup.

---

#### 10. [My Love Tiger](/manga/my-love-tiger) *(Manhwa)*

**Author:** Park Sung-woo | **Status:** Ongoing | **Format:** Korean Manhwa

A boy who releases tiger spirits through his emotions navigates a harem of girls with supernatural connections. The supernatural harem comedy with Nisekoi-style love interest archetypes in a Korean manhwa format.

---

#### 11. [A Returner's Magic Should Be Special](/manga/a-returners-magic-should-be-special) *(Manhwa)*

The central relationship with romantic undertones develops alongside the main plot in a way that has Nisekoi's "we both know what this is" quality.

---

#### 12. [I'll Be the Matriarch in This Life](/manga/ill-be-the-matriarch-in-this-life) *(Manhwa)*

The multiple suitors and the protagonist's navigation of romantic pressure in a period setting.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Who does Raku end up with in Nisekoi?**
Onodera Kosaki fans are still typing angry forum posts. The answer is Kirisaki Chitoge. Komi signaled this early and consistently.

**Q: Is Quintessential Quintuplets better than Nisekoi?**
Different strengths. Quintessential Quintuplets has stronger individual character arcs and a cleaner structure. Nisekoi has better comedic timing and a more satisfying reading-in-real-time experience. Both are worth reading.

---
