# If You Like Slice of Life Comedy, Read These Manga

![Cover Image](https://via.placeholder.com/1200x600/1a472a/86efac?text=Slice+of+Life+Comedy+in+Webcomics+Manhua "Slice of Life Comedy")

*Genre: Comedy / Slice of Life | Format: Manhwa · Manhua · Webcomic · Manga | Reading Level: All levels*

---

### Slice of Life Comedy Is Harder Than It Looks — And These Pull It Off

Comedy that doesn't have a plot to lean on has nowhere to hide. Slice of life comedy succeeds or fails purely on whether the characters are interesting enough to generate humor from daily life situations — no dramatic stakes, no villains, no external pressure to justify the reader's attention. Just people being people, and finding the funny in that.

This is a genre where webcomics and manhua have genuinely excelled. The short-format serialization that platforms like Webtoon, LINE, and various Chinese comic apps favor is ideally suited to slice of life comedy — you need exactly as many pages as the moment requires.

---

### Slice of Life Comedy Done Right

#### 1. My Giant Nerd Boyfriend — fishball *(Webcomic)*
[![Giant Nerd Boyfriend SOL](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Giant+Nerd+Boyfriend+SOL "My Giant Nerd Boyfriend")](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/my-giant-nerd-boyfriend)

**[Read My Giant Nerd Boyfriend on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/my-giant-nerd-boyfriend)**

The gold standard for autobiographical slice of life webcomic comedy in Asian comics. Each episode is complete in itself and finds the funny in specific, recognizable moments of cohabitation, gaming, and navigating each other's quirks. The cumulative effect over hundreds of episodes is a genuinely warm portrait of a relationship.

---

#### 2. Yumi's Cells — Donggeon Lee *(Manhwa)*
[![Yumi's Cells SOL](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Yumis+Cells+SOL "Yumi's Cells")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/yumis-cells)

**[Read Yumi's Cells on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/yumis-cells)**

The anthropomorphized-cells concept transforms Yumi's daily life — office work, relationships, meals, decisions — into a comedy of internal governance. The comedy of watching Hunger Cell stage a coup to commandeer Yumi's lunch decision, or Love Cell slowly gaining power over an otherwise sensible person, is inventive and consistent.

---

#### 3. Tamen de Gushi (Their Story) — Tan Jiu *(Manhua)*
[![Tamen de Gushi SOL](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Tamen+de+Gushi+SOL "Tamen de Gushi")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/tamen-de-gushi)

**[Read Tamen de Gushi on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/tamen-de-gushi)**

Each episode is short — often just a few panels — and finds exactly one comedic or warm moment in the daily lives of its central couple. Tan Jiu's restraint is the skill: knowing what to leave out, knowing when the joke is in the setup rather than the punchline, knowing that simplicity is often the funnier choice.

---

#### 4. Café de Touji — Various *(Manhua / Webtoon)*
[![Café de Touji](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Cafe+de+Touji "Café de Touji")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/cafe-de-touji)

**[Read Café de Touji on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/cafe-de-touji)**

A Chinese webcomic set in a café staffed by historically significant figures who don't know they're famous. The comedy comes from the contrast between their genuine historical personalities and the mundane demands of café service. It's the kind of concept that sounds like it would run out of steam but keeps finding new angles.

---

#### 5. Dungeon Meshi (Delicious in Dungeon) — Ryoko Kui *(Manga)*
[![Dungeon Meshi SOL](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Dungeon+Meshi+SOL "Dungeon Meshi")](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/dungeon-meshi)

**[Read Dungeon Meshi on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/dungeon-meshi)**

The slice of life elements in Dungeon Meshi — the cooking, the eating, the camp life between dungeons — are where the series is funniest. Kui takes the mundane activity of preparing a meal and places it in an extraordinarily specific fantasy context, and the comedy of that collision is endlessly generative.

---

#### 6. Working!! — Karino Takatsu *(Manga)*
[![Working!!](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Working+Manga "Working!!")](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/working)

**[Read Working!! on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/working)**

A slice of life comedy about a family restaurant staffed entirely by dysfunctional people who somehow manage to keep the place running. Each character is built around a specific comedic neurosis, and the comedy comes from these neuroses colliding in the confined space of a workplace. Warm, funny, and more emotionally satisfying than its premise suggests.

---

#### 7. Penguin Gentlemen — Dojin Koh *(Manhwa / Webtoon)*
[![Penguin Gentlemen](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Penguin+Gentlemen "Penguin Gentlemen")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/penguin-gentlemen)

**[Read Penguin Gentlemen on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/penguin-gentlemen)**

Penguins living human lives in contemporary Korea. The comedy comes partly from the concept and partly from how seriously the penguins take their situations — penguin office politics, penguin dating anxiety, penguin career aspirations. It's absurdist and warm in equal measure.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is slice of life comedy suitable for all-ages reading?**
A: Generally yes — more than most other genres. Titles like Tamen de Gushi, My Giant Nerd Boyfriend, and Penguin Gentlemen are suitable for all ages. Working!! has mild adult humor but nothing inappropriate for teens.

**Q: Do slice of life series need to be read from the beginning?**
A: Most can be dipped into — episodic structure means individual chapters often work standalone. However, reading from the beginning builds character attachment that enhances the reading experience significantly.

---

*Jump to our [Workplace Comedy Manhwa guide](#) or browse [Slice of Life tag](https://yourwebsite.com/tag/slice-of-life).*

# If You Like Workplace Comedy, Read These Manhwa

![Cover Image](https://via.placeholder.com/1200x600/1a472a/86efac?text=Workplace+Comedy+Manhwa+and+Manhua "Workplace Comedy Manhwa")

*Genre: Comedy / Workplace | Format: Manhwa · Manhua · Webcomic | Reading Level: Adults / Young Adults*

---

### Workplace Comedy Hits Different Once You Actually Have a Job

There's a reason workplace comedy becomes funnier to adult readers than to teenagers: recognition. The absurdity of corporate hierarchy, the colleagues who should not be allowed to operate unsupervised, the gap between the official description of what your job is and the actual thing you spend most of your time doing — these are all funnier when you're inside them.

Manhwa and manhua have developed a rich tradition of workplace comedy, partly because Korean and Chinese working culture provides exceptional comedic material. The following series understand that the workplace isn't just a setting — it's a specific social world with its own rules, hierarchies, and absurdities.

---

### Workplace Comedy for Adult Readers

#### 1. The Office is Mine — Various *(Manhwa / Webtoon)*
[![The Office is Mine](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=The+Office+is+Mine "The Office is Mine")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-office-is-mine)

**[Read The Office is Mine on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-office-is-mine)**

A Korean workplace romance/comedy that uses a realistic corporate setting to generate comedy from the specific absurdities of Korean office culture — the hierarchy of coffee-fetching duties, the politics of which conference room you're allowed to book, the elaborate social choreography of who speaks to whom and in what register.

The romance is real but the comedy is in the office setting's ruthless accuracy.

---

#### 2. Yumi's Cells — Donggeon Lee *(Manhwa)*
[![Yumi's Cells Workplace](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Yumis+Cells+Work "Yumi's Cells Workplace")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/yumis-cells)

**[Read Yumi's Cells on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/yumis-cells)**

The workplace sections of Yumi's Cells — Yumi navigating office politics, deadlines, and the politics of work friendships using her cell team — are among the funniest in the entire run. The anthropomorphized-cell concept works especially well in professional settings, where the gap between your internal experience and required external presentation is widest.

---

#### 3. My Roommate is a Gumiho — Similar *(Manhwa)*
[![My Roommate is a Gumiho](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=My+Roommate+Gumiho "My Roommate is a Gumiho")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/my-roommate-is-a-gumiho)

**[Read My Roommate is a Gumiho on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/my-roommate-is-a-gumiho)**

A college student accidentally swallows the marble of a 999-year-old gumiho (fox spirit). The comedy isn't strictly workplace but the series uses adult life — university, part-time jobs, the chaos of early adulthood — with the specific comedic touch of someone who understands that adult life is mostly embarrassing situations navigated imperfectly.

---

#### 4. Unintentional Love Story — Pibi *(Manhwa)*
[![Unintentional Love Story](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Unintentional+Love+Story "Unintentional Love Story")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/unintentional-love-story)

**[Read Unintentional Love Story on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/unintentional-love-story)**

A PR employee is sent to win back a famous ceramic artist who withdrew their contract. The comedy comes from the collision of corporate tactics with someone who genuinely doesn't care about corporate logic — and from the protagonist's increasingly absurd situation as feelings complicate the mission.

---

#### 5. The Distinguished Gentleman's Office — Various *(Manhua)*
[![Distinguished Gentleman's Office](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Distinguished+Gentlemans+Office "The Distinguished Gentleman's Office")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/distinguished-gentlemans-office)

**[Read Distinguished Gentleman's Office on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/distinguished-gentlemans-office)**

A Chinese office comedy that targets specifically the absurdity of Chinese corporate culture — the reverence for the boss, the competition between colleagues that takes on the structure of martial arts rivalry, the elaborate formality of workplace relationships that coexists with genuine dysfunction. Very funny to anyone who's worked in a large organization.

---

#### 6. Office Wild Affairs — Various *(Manhwa)*
[![Office Wild Affairs](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Office+Wild+Affairs "Office Wild Affairs")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/office-wild-affairs)

**[Read Office Wild Affairs on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/office-wild-affairs)**

A workplace romance that's funnier than it is romantic. The comedy of navigating attraction in an environment with HR implications, performance reviews, and mutual professional stakes is handled with more self-awareness than most office romance fiction manages.

---

#### 7. Working!! — Karino Takatsu *(Manga)*
[![Working Workplace](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Working+Workplace+Comedy "Working!!")](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/working)

**[Read Working!! on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/working)**

Mentioned in slice of life, worth repeating here: the restaurant workplace in Working!! is one of manga's most lovingly observed workplace environments. It's specifically a restaurant rather than an office, which gives the series slightly different comedic material, but the fundamental comedy of colleagues who are all deeply weird trying to do a job together is universal.

---

### Why Workplace Comedy from Korea and China Hits Differently

Both cultures have intense working cultures that are also sources of genuine social pressure. Korean chaebol culture, Chinese corporate hierarchies, the specific social rituals of East Asian professional environments — these provide comedic material that's specific enough to be interesting and universal enough to be relatable.

The best workplace comedy from these traditions does what all good comedy does: it takes something real and slightly unbearable and makes it funny enough to survive.

---

### FAQ

**Q: Is workplace comedy in manhwa similar to shows like The Office?**
A: In structure, yes — ensemble cast, shared physical setting, comedy from personality clash. But the humor is culturally specific in ways that make it feel different. Less cringe-based, more socially stratified.

**Q: Do any of these deal with overwork or burnout themes?**
A: Several do — particularly the Korean series, which reflect genuine cultural conversations about working conditions. Yumi's Cells addresses burnout directly in several arcs.

---

*Explore our [Fantasy Comedy guide](#) or browse the [Workplace tag](https://yourwebsite.com/tag/workplace).*

# If You Like Fantasy Comedy, Read These Stories

![Cover Image](https://via.placeholder.com/1200x600/1a472a/86efac?text=Fantasy+Comedy+in+Manhwa+Manhua+Webcomics "Fantasy Comedy Stories")

*Genre: Comedy / Fantasy | Format: Manhwa · Manhua · Webcomic · Manga | Reading Level: All levels*

---

### Fantasy Comedy Is the Genre That Has the Most Fun Destroying Its Own Tropes

The isekai (transported to another world) and fantasy genres have generated enough tropes at this point that the best comedy in the space is comedic deconstruction — stories that know the genre deeply enough to make fun of it from the inside. But there's also a rich tradition of fantasy comedy that isn't primarily parody — comedy that uses magical settings to generate humor through character and situation rather than by winking at the camera.

This list covers both: the deconstructionist fantasies and the ones that are simply funny within their worlds.

---

### Fantasy Comedy Worth Your Time

#### 1. The Scum Villain's Self-Saving System — Mo Xiang Tong Xiu *(Manhua)*
[![Scum Villain Fantasy](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Scum+Villain+Fantasy+Comedy "Scum Villain's Self-Saving System")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/scum-villains-self-saving-system)

**[Read Scum Villain on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/scum-villains-self-saving-system)**

The fantasy world Shen Qingqiu is dropped into is a direct spoof of cultivation novel tropes — the chosen protagonist, the evil master, the righteous sect, the increasingly contrived power-ups. His internal monologue commentary on the clichés he's forced to inhabit is consistently hilarious. But the comedy is built on genuine affection for the genre it's ribbing.

---

#### 2. Who Made Me a Princess — Plutus *(Manhwa)*
[![Who Made Me a Princess Fantasy](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Who+Made+Me+a+Princess+Fantasy "Who Made Me a Princess")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/who-made-me-a-princess)

**[Read Who Made Me a Princess on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/who-made-me-a-princess)**

Meta-fantasy comedy at its most charming. Athanasia knows she's in a fantasy novel and knows how it ends, which makes her attempts to avoid the ending both comedic and genuinely tense. The comedy of someone trying to manipulate "plot" while developing real feelings that complicate the plan is executed with consistent wit.

---

#### 3. Punderworld — Linda Šejić *(Webcomic)*
[![Punderworld Fantasy](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Punderworld+Fantasy "Punderworld")](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/punderworld)

**[Read Punderworld on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/punderworld)**

Greek mythology as fantasy comedy, with an emphasis on the domestic comedy of divine life. The puns referenced in the title are genuinely good — mythology creates exceptional pun opportunities — and Šejić never misses the chance to point out the inherent absurdity of how Greek myths play out when treated as a coherent fictional world.

---

#### 4. Dungeon Meshi (Delicious in Dungeon) — Ryoko Kui *(Manga)*
[![Dungeon Meshi Fantasy](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Dungeon+Meshi+Fantasy "Dungeon Meshi")](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/dungeon-meshi)

**[Read Dungeon Meshi on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/dungeon-meshi)**

Fantasy comedy through the most unexpected angle: what if the ecology of a fantasy dungeon were treated with the same serious attention as real biology, and the comedy came from the gap between that seriousness and the characters' desperate attempt to eat slime jelly as part of a survival diet?

The worldbuilding is so thorough that the comedy lands harder — you believe in the world, which makes the application of its logic to mundane meal preparation funnier.

---

#### 5. The Abandoned Empress *(Comedy Moments)* — Inabaruma *(Manhwa)*
[![Abandoned Empress Comedy](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Abandoned+Empress+Comedy "The Abandoned Empress")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-abandoned-empress)

**[Read The Abandoned Empress on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-abandoned-empress)**

Primarily drama, but the fantasy comedy elements — especially Tia's exasperated internal commentary on court politics and the specific absurdity of being a time-traveler in a fantasy court who has to pretend not to know what's going to happen — provide genuine comedy alongside the drama.

---

#### 6. Sleepless Domain — Mary Cagle *(Webcomic)*
[![Sleepless Domain](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Sleepless+Domain "Sleepless Domain by Mary Cagle")](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/sleepless-domain)

**[Read Sleepless Domain on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/sleepless-domain)**

A magical girl webcomic that treats its premise with enough seriousness to generate real drama while also being genuinely funny about the specific absurdities of magical girl genre conventions. The comedy of magical girl costuming logistics, team dynamics, and the question of what happens during the school day after a late-night monster battle is handled with consistent wit.

---

#### 7. Heaven Official's Blessing — Mo Xiang Tong Xiu *(Manhua)*
[![TGCF Fantasy Comedy](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=TGCF+Fantasy+Comedy "Heaven Official's Blessing")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/heaven-officials-blessing)

**[Read Heaven Official's Blessing on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/heaven-officials-blessing)**

Listed in the tragic romance section, TGCF earns its fantasy comedy spot too. The heavenly bureaucracy is a consistent comedy goldmine — the politics of which gods have seniority, the indignity of a three-times-ascended prince being broke, the specific humiliation of divine politics conducted in the register of very passive-aggressive colleagues. It's funnier than its reputation suggests.

---

### The Meta-Fantasy Comedy Trend in Manhwa

The "I've been reincarnated into a novel/game/manhwa" subgenre that manhwa has developed extensively is particularly rich comedy territory because it allows characters to comment on genre conventions directly. The comedy is meta but the emotions are sincere — the transmigration is genuinely disorienting even when it's funny, and the worlds being deconstructed are treated with enough internal consistency to remain engaging.

---

### FAQ

**Q: What's the difference between isekai and transmigration stories?**
A: Isekai (Japanese term) typically involves being transported from the real world to a fantasy world. Transmigration (more common in Chinese manhua tradition) often involves being reborn into the body of a fictional character. In manhwa, both structures exist, often in combination.

**Q: Is Dungeon Meshi appropriate for all ages?**
A: Yes — it's one of the most all-ages appropriate series on this list despite being a dungeon fantasy. There are some serious emotional moments but nothing inappropriate for general audiences.

---

*Finish with our [Feel-Good Manga guide](#) or browse the [Fantasy Comedy tag](https://yourwebsite.com/tag/fantasy-comedy).*

# If You Like Feel-Good Manga, Read These Series

![Cover Image](https://via.placeholder.com/1200x600/1a472a/86efac?text=Feel+Good+Stories+in+Manhwa+Manhua+Webcomics "Feel-Good Series")

*Genre: Feel-Good / Wholesome | Format: Manhwa · Manhua · Webcomic · Manga | Reading Level: All levels*

---

### Sometimes You Just Need Something That Makes You Feel Like the World Is Okay

This is the guide for the days when you don't want to be challenged. When you don't want narrative tension or moral complexity or tragic reversals. When you want to open something and feel, reliably, like the world is warmer and kinder than your current circumstances suggest.

Feel-good comics are not simple. Creating something that generates consistent warmth without tipping into saccharine requires craft and emotional intelligence. The creators on this list understand exactly what their readers are there for and deliver it without condescension.

---

### Feel-Good Series for Every Kind of Tired

#### 1. My Giant Nerd Boyfriend — fishball *(Webcomic)*
[![Giant Nerd Feel-Good](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Giant+Nerd+Feel+Good "My Giant Nerd Boyfriend")](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/my-giant-nerd-boyfriend)

**[Read My Giant Nerd Boyfriend on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/my-giant-nerd-boyfriend)**

The gold standard for feel-good webcomics in this space. Every episode is a small, warm thing — the specific pleasure of two people enjoying being around each other, captured with humor and honesty. The autobiographical origin gives it an authenticity that manufactured warmth doesn't achieve.

**Feel-good type:** Warmth of an affectionate, functional relationship.

---

#### 2. Tamen de Gushi (Their Story) — Tan Jiu *(Manhua)*
[![Tamen Feel-Good](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Tamen+Feel+Good "Tamen de Gushi")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/tamen-de-gushi)

**[Read Tamen de Gushi on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhua/tamen-de-gushi)**

A love story told in small moments — the kind that feels so real you occasionally feel like you're intruding on something private. The warmth is cumulative. By the time you've read through the whole thing, you'll have seen a relationship develop from first meeting through genuine life partnership, one small moment at a time.

**Feel-good type:** Accumulative warmth of a real-feeling love story.

---

#### 3. Punderworld — Linda Šejić *(Webcomic)*
[![Punderworld Feel-Good](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Punderworld+Feel+Good "Punderworld")](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/punderworld)

**[Read Punderworld on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/webtoon/punderworld)**

The warm, laughing heart of Hades and Persephone's relationship in Punderworld is feel-good comics at their most confident. Šejić knows exactly what she's making and makes it with skill. Reading it is genuinely pleasant in a way that's harder to achieve than it looks.

**Feel-good type:** Warmth of an established loving relationship with humor.

---

#### 4. Something About Us — LEEHAMA *(Manhwa)*
[![Something About Us Feel-Good](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Something+About+Us+Feel+Good "Something About Us")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/something-about-us)

**[Read Something About Us on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/something-about-us)**

The slowest of slow-burns, and every page of it is comforting in the way that reading about two people who are clearly right for each other slowly figuring that out is comforting. LEEHAMA's art is warm and expressive, and the friendship-to-romance development is so natural it's essentially anxiety-free.

**Feel-good type:** The pleasure of knowing where a relationship is going before the characters do.

---

#### 5. Witch Hat Atelier — Kamome Shirahama *(Manga)*
[![Witch Hat Feel-Good](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Witch+Hat+Feel+Good "Witch Hat Atelier")](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/witch-hat-atelier)

**[Read Witch Hat Atelier on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/witch-hat-atelier)**

Feel-good through wonder rather than warmth, specifically. Reading Witch Hat Atelier evokes the sensation of discovering something extraordinary — the magic system based on drawing is a joy, the world is beautiful, and the central mentorship relationship is the kind that makes you wish you'd had a teacher like that.

**Feel-good type:** Sense of wonder and discovery.

---

#### 6. My Love Story!! (Ore Monogatari!!) — Kazune Kawahara *(Manga)*
[![My Love Story Feel-Good](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=My+Love+Story+Feel+Good "My Love Story!!")](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/my-love-story)

**[Read My Love Story!! on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/my-love-story)**

The single most reliably feel-good romance manga in existence. Takeo and Yamato's relationship is the antidote to every anxious, angst-ridden love story. They communicate. They're honest. They're happy. The manga doesn't manufacture obstacles — it just lets two good people be in love, and that simple premise is more satisfying than ten dramatic romances combined.

**Feel-good type:** Pure happiness at watching good people love each other well.

---

#### 7. Banana Fish *(alternative reading recommendation)* — [See Happy Alternatives Note Below]*

Actually, instead of Banana Fish (which would go in the opposite direction of feel-good): 

#### 7. The Makeup Remover — Ryu Ryang *(Manhwa)*
[![The Makeup Remover Feel-Good](https://via.placeholder.com/800x450/0d2b1a/86efac?text=Makeup+Remover+Feel+Good "The Makeup Remover")](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-makeup-remover)

**[Read The Makeup Remover on Our Site →](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-makeup-remover)**

Feel-good through self-discovery and found community. Watching the protagonist develop her own relationship with her appearance — separate from what anyone else thinks — generates a warm, sustained positive feeling that persists well beyond individual reading sessions. It's the kind of series that makes you want to do something kind for yourself.

**Feel-good type:** Self-acceptance warmth.

---

### The Difference Between Feel-Good and Just Easy

Feel-good comics are not necessarily unchallenging. They don't avoid difficulty — Witch Hat Atelier has genuine tension, Something About Us has real emotional stakes, My Giant Nerd Boyfriend has relatable frustrations. The difference is that the overall emotional atmosphere is one of warmth, the characters are people you want to spend time with, and the reading experience itself is pleasant rather than draining.

Shallow feel-good comics are instantly forgettable. Good feel-good comics are the ones you return to when you need to remember why you started reading in the first place.

### FAQ

**Q: Which series on this feel-good list is best for someone who's burned out?**
A: Start with My Giant Nerd Boyfriend for immediate warmth without investment requirements. Then, if you want to go longer-form, Something About Us provides sustained comfort across its full run.

**Q: Are any of these feel-good series also funny?**
A: All of them have comedic elements to varying degrees. Punderworld and My Giant Nerd Boyfriend are primarily comedic. My Love Story!! is frequently laugh-out-loud funny. Tamen de Gushi has consistent gentle humor.

**Q: How do I decide between manhwa, manhua, and manga?**
A: Format preference matters — manhwa/webtoons are vertical scroll, great for mobile reading. Manhua varies — some are vertical scroll, some traditional. Manga reads right-to-left in traditional format. Content-wise, your best bet is to use our genre tags and let the story quality guide you rather than the format.

**Q: Can I request a series be added to these guides?**
A: Yes — use the comment section on each blog's web page or contact us through our site's recommendation form. We update these guides as strong new series emerge.

---

### Final Note From the Editorial Team

Twenty-three guides. Hundreds of series. Manga, manhwa, manhua, webcomics from Korea, Japan, China, Malaysia, the US, Europe, and beyond.

The through line is this: great storytelling doesn't care where it comes from. If you've only been reading Japanese manga, you're missing some of the best comics being made right now. If you've only been reading Korean webtoons, the Chinese manhua tradition has decades of extraordinary work waiting for you. And if you haven't explored independent webcomics — fishball, Quimchee, Alice Oseman, Linda Šejić — you're missing a creative scene that's genuinely thriving.

Everything on every list in this collection has a detail page on our site. Click through, explore, and find your next obsession.

*Happy reading.*

excerpt: By HERO & Daisuke Hagiwara  Completed  16 Volumes If you only read one manga from this list, make it Horimiya. Popular girl Hori discovers that her reserved classmate Miyamura has tattoos and piercings outside of school — and what makes this series exceptional is how quickly it r
body: # 10 Romance Manga You Should Read ### 🌸 1. [Horimiya](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/horimiya) ![Horimiya](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By HERO & Daisuke Hagiwara | Completed | 16 Volumes* If you only read one manga from this list, make it *Horimiya*. Popular girl Hori discovers that her reserved classmate Miyamura has tattoos and piercings outside of school — and what makes this series exceptional is how quickly it refuses to be predictable. The leads get together early. The drama isn't about "will they or won't they" — it's about watching two people who genuinely like each other figure out how to actually be in a relationship. That's rare in manga, and it makes *Horimiya* feel refreshingly real. The supporting cast is developed enough to feel like full people, not props. Warm, funny, sometimes quietly heartbreaking. **Best for:** Readers tired of drawn-out confession arcs. --- ### 🌸 2. [Kimi ni Todoke](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/kimi-ni-todoke) ![Kimi ni Todoke](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1618556264157-b27a09f0f891?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Karuho Shiina | Completed | 30 Volumes* *Kimi ni Todoke* is the manga equivalent of a warm blanket. Sawako looks like the girl from *The Ring* (the series leans into this), but she's genuinely the sweetest person imaginable — someone who wants to connect with the world but keeps getting misread. Popular, easygoing Kazehaya is one of the few who actually sees her. The pacing is slow, but the emotional payoff for patient readers is enormous. Sawako's growth as a person is as central as the romance, and that's what gives it staying power across 30 volumes. **Best for:** Readers who want character development as much as romance. --- ### 🌸 3. [Ao Haru Ride (Blue Spring Ride)](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/ao-haru-ride) ![Ao Haru Ride](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Io Sakisaka | Completed | 13 Volumes* A first love that got cut short, years later, complicated. *Ao Haru Ride* deals with the messy middle ground between who you were and who you've become. Futaba deliberately made herself plain to survive middle school. Kou came back from years away as someone completely different. Watching them navigate that gap is where the manga lives. Sakisaka-sensei is great at not letting her leads be passive — characters make choices here, bad ones sometimes. That's what keeps you reading. **Best for:** Readers who appreciate complicated emotions and active protagonists. --- ### 🌸 4. [Ore Monogatari!! (My Love Story!!)](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/ore-monogatari) ![Ore Monogatari](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578301978693-85fa9c0320b9?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Kazune Kawahara & Aruko | Completed | 13 Volumes* A complete genre subversion disguised as a wholesome shojo manga. Takeo is enormous and intimidating-looking, perpetually overlooked by girls in favor of his handsome best friend Suna. Then he meets Yamato — and she actually likes *him*. No love triangles. No misunderstandings dragging for volumes. Just two people who like each other figuring out how to date. Revolutionary, honestly. **Best for:** Readers who want pure, drama-free feel-good romance. --- ### 🌸 5. [A Silent Voice (Koe no Katachi)](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/a-silent-voice) ![A Silent Voice](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yoshitoki Oima | Completed | 7 Volumes* Not a romance in the conventional sense — more like a story about guilt, forgiveness, disability, and slowly learning to hear the person in front of you. Shoya bullied Shoko, a deaf girl, in elementary school. Years later, struggling with his own isolation, he tries to make things right. The romantic thread is understated and restrained in exactly the right way. If you've seen the KyoAni film and haven't read the manga, you're missing significant character depth — especially the supporting cast. **Best for:** Readers who want romance woven into something emotionally complex. --- ### 🌸 6. [Skip Beat!](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/skip-beat) ![Skip Beat](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yoshiki Nakamura | Ongoing | 47+ Volumes* Kyoko discovers her childhood friend used her as a housekeeper while pursuing idol stardom, channels her heartbreak into entering the entertainment industry herself, and ends up in a complicated not-quite-rivalry with the industry's top star. The slow burn has been simmering for 47 volumes. The comedy is excellent. The entertainment industry world-building is detailed and genuinely interesting. If you can handle the wait, nothing in the genre matches the accumulated tension. **Best for:** Readers with patience and a high tolerance for exquisite suffering. --- ### 🌸 7. [Fruits Basket](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/fruits-basket) ![Fruits Basket](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Natsuki Takaya | Completed | 23 Volumes* The Sohma family is cursed to transform into zodiac animals. Tohru Honda, having lost her mother, ends up living with them. The romance takes time to develop — this is fundamentally a story about healing — but the payoff is one of the most cathartic conclusions in manga. The collector's edition includes a redrawn final arc that improves significantly on the original. A classic that deserves every word of its reputation. **Best for:** Readers who want romance wrapped in real emotional healing arcs. --- ### 🌸 8. [Lovely Complex](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/lovely-complex) ![Lovely Complex](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578662996442-48f60103fc96?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Aya Nakahara | Completed | 17 Volumes* A tall girl and a short boy constantly mistaken for a comedy duo slowly discover they might actually like each other. The Osaka dialect humor is a genuine part of the personality here — it has regional specificity that feels authentic. Risa is one of the most entertaining and relatable romance manga protagonists ever written. If you've only seen the anime adaptation, the manga goes further and hits harder. **Best for:** Readers who want comedy and romance in equal measure. --- ### 🌸 9. [Takane & Hana](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/takane-and-hana) ![Takane and Hana](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yuki Shiwasu | Completed | 18 Volumes* High school girl Hana fills in for her sister at an omiai (arranged meeting) and ends up sparring verbally with the arrogant, absurdly handsome heir Takane. He's fascinated by the first person who's ever talked back to him honestly. The banter is the entire appeal and it's genuinely funny. As the series progresses, both characters grow without losing what makes them interesting, and the romance earns its conclusion. **Best for:** Readers who love sharp banter between equally stubborn leads. --- ### 🌸 10. [We Never Learn (Bokutachi wa Benkyou ga Dekinai)](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/we-never-learn) ![We Never Learn](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Taishi Tsutsui | Completed | 21 Volumes* A tutor is assigned to help three academically gifted girls improve in their weak subjects. What sounds like a standard harem setup is elevated by genuinely well-developed female leads and a clever structure where the manga published multiple alternate endings — each following a different girl's route. It's one of the more creative structural experiments in the genre, and each ending is legitimately satisfying on its own terms. **Best for:** Readers who want multiple satisfying romance routes in one manga. --- ## Quick Reference Table | Title | Volumes | Status | Best Quality | |---|---|---|---| | [Horimiya](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/horimiya) | 16 | Complete | Early relationship focus | | [Kimi ni Todoke](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/kimi-ni-todoke) | 30 | Complete | Character growth | | [Ao Haru Ride](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/ao-haru-ride) | 13 | Complete | Emotional complexity | | [Ore Monogatari!!](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/ore-monogatari) | 13 | Complete | Wholesome + subversive | | [A Silent Voice](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/a-silent-voice) | 7 | Complete | Depth and restraint | | [Skip Beat!](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/skip-beat) | 47+ | Ongoing | Supreme slow burn | | [Fruits Basket](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/fruits-basket) | 23 | Complete | Healing + romance | | [Lovely Complex](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/lovely-complex) | 17 | Complete | Comedy + warmth | | [Takane & Hana](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/takane-and-hana) | 18 | Complete | Banter-driven romance | | [We Never Learn](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/we-never-learn) | 21 | Complete | Multiple route endings | --- ## FAQ **What's the difference between shojo and josei romance?** Shojo targets teenage girls — protagonists are usually in high school and stories center on first love and identity. Josei targets adult women and features more mature dynamics, adult workplaces, and more complex relationship conflicts. **What's a good romance manga for someone who's never read manga before?** [Horimiya](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/horimiya) or [Ore Monogatari!!](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/ore-monogatari) — both are accessible, not too long, and don't require genre familiarity. **Do I need to read romance manga in publication order?** Most romance manga are single ongoing stories — start from volume 1. --- --- # 2. If You Like Romance Manhwa, Read These Stories ![Romance Manhwa Cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=1200&h=400&fit=crop&q=80) *Cover image: The lush, full-color world of romance manhwa — stylized and deeply expressive.* Here's the thing nobody tells you when you first discover manhwa: the full color format genuinely changes how romance lands. Those soft blushes, the way light falls across a character's face in a critical moment, the ability to use color temperature to set emotional tone — manhwa has tools that black-and-white manga simply doesn't. And South Korean romance webtoons have developed their own narrative DNA. Female protagonists are often sharper and more goal-oriented. The isekai-romance hybrid — someone reincarnated into a romance novel world — is essentially a manhwa invention. If you've been living in manga world and haven't crossed over, this guide is where you start. ---

body: # 10 Romance Manhwa You Need to Read ### 💎 1. [True Beauty (Yesin Gangrim)](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/true-beauty) ![True Beauty](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yaongyi | Ongoing | WEBTOON* Started as a relatable story about a girl who transforms herself with makeup and ended up becoming one of the most-read webtoons in the world. *True Beauty* works because Jugyeong feels like a real person — insecure, funny, a horror movie obsessive — not just a narrative device. The love triangle between Suho and Seojun is genuinely contested, and the series handles unexpectedly serious themes underneath its school comedy surface. Yes, it got a K-drama. The webtoon is better. --- ### 💎 2. [The Remarried Empress](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-remarried-empress) ![The Remarried Empress](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578662996442-48f60103fc96?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Alphatart & Sumpul | Ongoing* One of the smartest romance manhwa being published right now. Empress Navier gets cheated on by her emperor husband, decides to divorce him and marry another king — and the execution is ice-cold, precise, and utterly captivating. Navier doesn't fall apart. She doesn't beg. She makes moves. The romance with the neighboring king Heinrey feels earned because both characters feel credible. Reads equally well as political drama and slow-burn romance. --- ### 💎 3. [I Love Yoo](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/i-love-yoo) ![I Love Yoo](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Quimchee | Ongoing | WEBTOON* The art alone is worth reading this for — Quimchee's style is distinctive in ways that feel genuinely intentional rather than conventionally pretty. But *I Love Yoo* earns its following through Shin-Ae: a protagonist who starts openly difficult — guarded, blunt, not interested in people — and earns reader affection through gradual, credible thawing. The romance is slow. The family dynamics are complicated. It asks you to sit with ambiguity, and rewards you for it. --- ### 💎 4. [Cheese in the Trap](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/cheese-in-the-trap) ![Cheese in the Trap](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1618556264157-b27a09f0f891?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Soonkki | Completed* A manhwa that genuinely challenges you. Yoo Jung is handsome, charming, popular — and Hong Seol cannot shake the feeling that something underneath that surface is deeply off. *Cheese in the Trap* is a romance that keeps you genuinely uncertain whether the male lead is safe. The psychological tension is the point. It raised some of the most interesting reader debates in webtoon history when it ended. Not for everyone, but if you want a romance that makes you think, this is unmatched. --- ### 💎 5. [Let Dai](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/let-dai) ![Let Dai](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Won Soo-Yeon | Completed* One of the most emotionally intense manhwa ever published. Dai is beautiful, violent, and dangerous. Jaehee is drawn into his orbit against every reasonable instinct. *Let Dai* deals with love that is genuinely destructive and asks real questions about what we're willing to accept in the name of connection. Mature, dark, and quietly devastating. Not a comfortable read — that's exactly why it stays with you. --- ### 💎 6. [My ID is Gangnam Beauty](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/my-id-is-gangnam-beauty) ![My ID is Gangnam Beauty](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Maenggi | Completed* A girl who had plastic surgery to escape bullying enters university and faces new forms of scrutiny. *My ID is Gangnam Beauty* is sharp about beauty standards and social cruelty in ways that feel genuinely observed. The romance with a taciturn classmate who actually sees her is secondary to Mirae's own growth — which makes it more satisfying, not less. --- ### 💎 7. [Bastard](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/bastard) ![Bastard](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Carnby Kim & Youngchan Hwang | Completed* Thriller-romance hybrid that most people don't expect to have real romantic tension — and yet it absolutely does. Jin is the son of a serial killer forced to assist in his father's crimes. The relationship that develops with a classmate while he tries to protect her is charged in a completely unique way. If you want romance with genuine life-or-death stakes, nothing in manhwa delivers it quite like this. --- ### 💎 8. [It's Mine](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/its-mine) ![It's Mine](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Ongoing* A refreshing manhwa where the female lead is the one making the first moves consistently and unapologetically. The role reversals feel natural rather than gimmicky because the character has a defined personality behind them. The romance develops at a good pace and the art is clean and expressive. --- ### 💎 9. [I Became the Wife of the Male Lead](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/i-became-wife-of-male-lead) ![I Became the Wife of the Male Lead](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578301978693-85fa9c0320b9?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Ongoing* A reader reincarnates as a minor character in a fantasy novel and ends up married to the male lead she always rooted for. The twist: the male lead in the book was manipulative and cruel. Now she has to figure out whether the person she's living with is the monster from the pages or someone different. The romantic tension lives in that uncertainty. --- ### 💎 10. [Unholy Blood](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/unholy-blood) ![Unholy Blood](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Lina Im | Completed* Action-romance hybrid that goes hard on both ends. Hayan is a half-vampire in a world being torn apart by full vampires. A detective needs to figure out what she actually is. The romance subplot develops organically and doesn't undercut the main story. An excellent entry point for readers who want some adrenaline with their love story, and a strong female protagonist who can genuinely fight. --- ## Quick Reference Table | Title | Format | Status | Tone | |---|---|---|---| | [True Beauty](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/true-beauty) | Webtoon | Ongoing | Warm, funny, real | | [The Remarried Empress](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-remarried-empress) | Webtoon | Ongoing | Political + elegant | | [I Love Yoo](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/i-love-yoo) | Webtoon | Ongoing | Slow-burn, complex | | [Cheese in the Trap](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/cheese-in-the-trap) | Webtoon | Complete | Psychological tension | | [Let Dai](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/let-dai) | Print | Complete | Dark, intense | | [My ID is Gangnam Beauty](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/my-id-is-gangnam-beauty) | Webtoon | Complete | Social commentary | | [Bastard](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/bastard) | Webtoon | Complete | Thriller-romance | | [It's Mine](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/its-mine) | Webtoon | Ongoing | Role reversal | | [I Became the Wife of the Male Lead](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/i-became-wife-of-male-lead) | Webtoon | Ongoing | Isekai romance | | [Unholy Blood](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/unholy-blood) | Webtoon | Complete | Action-romance | --- ## FAQ **Is manhwa always in color?** Most webtoon-format manhwa is in full color. Older print manhwa may be black-and-white like manga. **Where can I legally read these?** LINE WEBTOON, Tapas, and Lezhin Comics are the main legal platforms. **Do romance manhwa get anime adaptations?** A few — *True Beauty* got a K-drama. Anime adaptations of manhwa are still relatively rare but increasing. --- --- # 3. If You Like Slow Burn Romance, Read These Manga & Manhwa ![Slow Burn Romance Cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=1200&h=400&fit=crop&q=80) *Cover image: Slow burn romance — everything lives in the distance between two people.* Slow burn romance is a patience test and a trust fall. You commit to a series knowing the payoff is chapters, volumes, maybe years away. The best slow burn stories do something specific: they make the *not yet* feel meaningful. The moments that almost happened. The conversations that nearly crossed a line. The looks that get noticed by everyone except the person they're directed at. Done right, it's some of the most emotionally effective storytelling in the medium. Done wrong, it's a reader screaming at their screen at 1 a.m. The series below earn their pacing. The tension accumulates rather than resets. ---

title: 10 Best Slow Burn Manga & Manhwa
excerpt: By Aka Akasaka  Completed  28 Volumes Two geniuses in love, both too proud to confess first, treating romantic encounters like psychological warfare. Kaguya-sama built this gimmick into one of the best slow burn experiences in manga. The comedy is genuinely funny — not just panel
body: # 10 Best Slow Burn Manga & Manhwa ### 🔥 1. [Kaguya-sama: Love Is War](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/kaguya-sama-love-is-war) ![Kaguya-sama](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Aka Akasaka | Completed | 28 Volumes* Two geniuses in love, both too proud to confess first, treating romantic encounters like psychological warfare. *Kaguya-sama* built this gimmick into one of the best slow burn experiences in manga. The comedy is genuinely funny — not just panel-filler. Underneath the battles, Kaguya's arc from isolated, emotionally stunted heiress to someone capable of vulnerability is quietly devastating. The final third goes places the early chapters couldn't have predicted. If you dropped it thinking "it's just a gag manga," go back. You're missing the good part. --- ### 🔥 2. [My Love Story with Yamada-kun at Lv999](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/yamada-kun-lv999) ![Yamada-kun Lv999](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Mashiro | Completed* Akane, fresh off a breakup, starts playing an online RPG and keeps running into a cold, impossibly handsome high schooler named Yamada. The burn comes not from dramatic obstacles but from two emotionally defensive people learning to let their guards down in small, believable increments. The game-world setting adds texture without overwhelming the romance, and Yamada's arc — going from unavailable to genuinely present — is handled with real care. --- ### 🔥 3. [Komi Can't Communicate](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/komi-cant-communicate) ![Komi-san](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578662996442-48f60103fc96?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Tomohito Oda | Completed | 28 Volumes* Komi looks perfect. But she has severe social anxiety and can barely speak. The school thinks she's an aloof goddess. Only Tadano actually notices her discomfort. Their friendship builds across 28 volumes at a pace that mirrors Komi's gradual growth. Every step forward is a real step forward for Komi as a person, not just a narrative beat. If you read it right, the final volumes hit harder than almost anything in contemporary rom-com manga. --- ### 🔥 4. [Lore Olympus](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/lore-olympus) ![Lore Olympus](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Rachel Smythe | Completed | WEBTOON* A Greek mythology retelling with art so distinctive it became one of the most recognizable webtoons on the platform. Persephone is pink. Hades is blue. The color-coded world creates visual shorthand for emotional states used brilliantly across hundreds of chapters. Their relationship develops in a way complicated by trauma, divine politics, and both characters' damage — and when it resolves, it earns every chapter it took to get there. --- ### 🔥 5. [The Dangers in My Heart](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/dangers-in-my-heart) ![The Dangers in My Heart](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1618556264157-b27a09f0f891?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Norio Sakurai | Ongoing* Started as a dark comedy about a boy who fantasizes about the popular girl in disturbing ways, and slowly became one of the most earnest romance manga currently running. The transformation of Kyotaro from edgelord to a person who can actually express feelings is the whole arc. Anna is tall, kind, and a great character in her own right. The anime adaptation (both seasons) handles the slow burn well, but the manga goes further. --- ### 🔥 6. [Skip Beat!](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/skip-beat) ![Skip Beat](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yoshiki Nakamura | Ongoing | 47+ Volumes* The slow burn of all slow burns. 47 volumes. Still ongoing. Kyoko and Ren's relationship has been circling each other for years across entertainment industry storylines, and somehow Nakamura-sensei keeps adding layers rather than treading water. If you're the kind of reader who finds enormous satisfaction in the almost — the near-confession, the touch held a second too long — *Skip Beat!* is the endurance test that pays off every chapter. --- ### 🔥 7. [Takagi-san (Karakai Jouzu no Takagi-san)](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/takagi-san) ![Takagi-san](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Soichiro Yamamoto | Ongoing* Every chapter is a small, self-contained tease. Takagi teases her flustered classmate Nishikata relentlessly — and it's obvious to everyone, including the reader, that the teasing is affection. The genius is watching him slowly, slowly figure that out. The sweetness accumulates without ever being cloying. Perfect reading when you only have a few minutes and want to smile. --- ### 🔥 8. [Chihayafuru](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/chihayafuru) ![Chihayafuru](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yuki Suetsugu | Completed | 50 Volumes* Technically a sports manga about karuta, but the romantic triangle running through all 50 volumes is one of the genre's most debated and emotionally complex. Chihaya, Taichi, and Arata have loved each other in different configurations since childhood. The resolution took 50 volumes and split readers. Both sides of the debate are passionate. That's how you know it worked. --- ### 🔥 9. [I Love Yoo](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/i-love-yoo) ![I Love Yoo](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578301978693-85fa9c0320b9?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Quimchee | Ongoing | WEBTOON* Shin-Ae's walls don't come down in convenient dramatic moments. They erode, slowly, in small genuine interactions. That's what makes *I Love Yoo* an exemplary slow burn — the progress is microscopic but always real. The art style amplifies the emotional restraint. Every small moment carries weight precisely because the series never rushes. --- ### 🔥 10. [Orange](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/orange) ![Orange](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Ichigo Takano | Completed | 6 Volumes* A high school girl receives letters from her future self urging her to pay attention to the new transfer student and prevent his suicide. *Orange* uses the time travel premise to make every small choice carry the full weight of what it means to reach out to someone. The romance is tender and painful simultaneously, and the series addresses mental health with genuine care. Six volumes. Go slowly. --- ## Quick Reference Table | Title | Medium | Burn Length | Why It Works | |---|---|---|---| | [Kaguya-sama](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/kaguya-sama-love-is-war) | Manga | 28 volumes | Comedy masking vulnerability | | [Yamada-kun Lv999](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/yamada-kun-lv999) | Manga | Medium | No manufactured drama | | [Komi Can't Communicate](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/komi-cant-communicate) | Manga | 28 volumes | Mirrors character growth | | [Lore Olympus](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/lore-olympus) | Manhwa | Long | Visual + emotional depth | | [Dangers in My Heart](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/dangers-in-my-heart) | Manga | Ongoing | Protagonist transformation | | [Skip Beat!](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/skip-beat) | Manga | 47+ volumes | Supreme tension | | [Takagi-san](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/takagi-san) | Manga | Ongoing | Quiet accumulated sweetness | | [Chihayafuru](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/chihayafuru) | Manga | 50 volumes | Triangle complexity | | [I Love Yoo](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/i-love-yoo) | Manhwa | Ongoing | Microscopic, real progress | | [Orange](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/orange) | Manga | 6 volumes | Stakes make every moment matter | --- ## FAQ **How many chapters should I wait before a slow burn starts paying off?** Generally give it 20–30 chapters. Series like *Kaguya-sama* lay groundwork early that pays off much later. **What if I hate slow burn?** Try [Horimiya](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/horimiya) or [Ore Monogatari!!](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/ore-monogatari) — both get the couple together quickly. **Which slow burn has the most satisfying payoff?** [Kaguya-sama](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/kaguya-sama-love-is-war) — the conclusion delivers on every volume of buildup, and then some. --- --- # 4. If You Like Fantasy Romance, Read These Series ![Fantasy Romance Cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578301978693-85fa9c0320b9?w=1200&h=400&fit=crop&q=80) *Cover image: Fantasy romance — worlds built for falling in love in impossible places.* Fantasy romance is where the medium gets to go completely unhinged in the best way. Magic systems, political intrigue, ancient bloodlines, demon lords with surprisingly complicated feelings — all of it's on the table. When a fantasy world is built well, the romance carries stakes that feel genuinely different from contemporary settings. Here, love between the wrong people might start a war. The villainess reincarnation subgenre — a reader wakes up inside a romance novel as a side character destined to die — has produced some of the cleverest, most self-aware fantasy romance in the medium. ---

excerpt: By Yuna & INA  Manhwa  Completed One of the titles that helped define the "noble lady with tragic past gets a second chance" subgenre. Aristia was discarded and died — then wakes up as a child to make different choices. The romance here is genuinely complicated: can you love the
body: # 10 Fantasy Romance Series Worth Reading ### ⚔️ 1. [The Abandoned Empress](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-abandoned-empress) ![The Abandoned Empress](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yuna & INA | Manhwa | Completed* One of the titles that helped define the "noble lady with tragic past gets a second chance" subgenre. Aristia was discarded and died — then wakes up as a child to make different choices. The romance here is genuinely complicated: can you love the person who once hurt you simply because the timeline changed? The manhwa actually engages with that question rather than dismissing it. The art is beautiful and the court politics are well-constructed. --- ### ⚔️ 2. [The Remarried Empress](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-remarried-empress) ![The Remarried Empress](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Alphatart & Sumpul | Manhwa | Ongoing* Already featured in romance manhwa, but it belongs here too. The imperial fantasy world is richly constructed, and the political dimensions of Navier's second marriage carry genuine weight. The way two kingdoms negotiate around two people choosing each other is more interesting than most pure fantasy plots. --- ### ⚔️ 3. [Sugar Apple Fairy Tale](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/sugar-apple-fairy-tale) ![Sugar Apple Fairy Tale](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Miri Mikawa & Aki | Manga | Completed | 6 Volumes* Set in a world where humans and fairies coexist in an uneasy hierarchy. Anne wants to be a master candy artisan; Challe is a fairy she purchases as a guard. The romance that develops across that power imbalance — complicated by broader social structures — is handled with more nuance than you'd expect. The art is delicate and genuinely beautiful. A quiet, thoughtful fantasy romance. --- ### ⚔️ 4. [Bride of the Water God](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/bride-of-the-water-god) ![Bride of the Water God](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578662996442-48f60103fc96?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Mi-Kyung Yun | Manhwa | Completed* A village girl offered to the Water God as a sacrifice ends up in the realm of the gods instead of dying. The Water God, Habaek, only appears as a child in the human world — which creates an immediately strange dynamic that the series navigates cleverly. The art is intricate, the mythological world-building is rich, and it's one of the classic Korean fantasy manhwa everyone in the genre knows. --- ### ⚔️ 5. [Frieren: Beyond Journey's End](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/frieren-beyond-journeys-end) ![Frieren](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Kanehito Yamada & Tsukasa Abe | Manga | Ongoing* Not a romance in the conventional sense, but the longing in *Frieren* — an elven mage slowly awakening to emotion across a thousand-year lifespan — is more moving than most explicit love stories. The manga won the Manga Taisho Award. The anime by Madhouse is one of the best of the decade. If you want fantasy with deep, quiet emotional resonance, nothing else feels quite like this. --- ### ⚔️ 6. [I Was Reincarnated as the Villainess](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/villainess-reincarnation) ![Villainess Reincarnation](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1618556264157-b27a09f0f891?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Ongoing* The villainess isekai genre has many entries, and this is one of the stronger ones because the protagonist has an actual plan rather than just reacting. She's working to change her fate with intelligence and agency, and the romance develops with the male lead through mutual respect building into something more. The period-appropriate art is lush and the court politics keep things moving. --- ### ⚔️ 7. [I'll Be the Matriarch in This Life](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/ill-be-the-matriarch) ![I'll Be the Matriarch](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Ongoing* A woman reincarnates with memories of her past life and decides to build her family into a great house this time around. The romance is secondary to the ambition — which paradoxically makes both more interesting. The family-building strategy is detailed and satisfying, and the romantic interest is someone who respects her goals rather than undermining them. --- ### ⚔️ 8. [My Next Life as a Villainess](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/my-next-life-as-villainess) ![My Next Life as a Villainess](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578301978693-85fa9c0320b9?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Satoru Yamaguchi & Nami Hidaka | Manga | Ongoing* Catarina Claes reincarnates as the villainess of an otome game and knows all her routes end in exile or death. Her solution is to befriend everyone, cultivate her vegetable garden, and avoid all bad ends. The comedy comes from everyone around her falling for her earnest sincerity while she's obliviously planning agricultural backup careers. One of the most charming fantasy romance manga running. --- ### ⚔️ 9. [Black Clover](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/black-clover) ![Black Clover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yuki Tabata | Manga | Ongoing* Primarily action, but the romance threads woven through — particularly around Asta and Noelle — follow classic fantasy romance beats in a well-constructed magic world. Included here for readers who want their romance served inside a substantial fantasy action series. --- ### ⚔️ 10. [The Lady and the Beast](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-lady-and-the-beast) ![The Lady and the Beast](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Ongoing* A woman ends up bound to a cursed beast-man in a gorgeously rendered fantasy world. The romance develops across genuine mutual wariness — neither party trusts the other initially, and watching that shift is the pleasure of the series. Strong art and a fantasy world that feels textured rather than generic. --- ## Quick Reference Table | Title | Medium | Setting | Romance Style | |---|---|---|---| | [The Abandoned Empress](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-abandoned-empress) | Manhwa | Imperial court | Second chance, complex | | [The Remarried Empress](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-remarried-empress) | Manhwa | Imperial court | Political + slow burn | | [Sugar Apple Fairy Tale](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/sugar-apple-fairy-tale) | Manga | Fairy world | Quiet, nuanced | | [Bride of the Water God](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/bride-of-the-water-god) | Manhwa | Divine realm | Mythological | | [Frieren](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/frieren-beyond-journeys-end) | Manga | Post-quest world | Quiet longing | | [Villainess Reincarnation](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/villainess-reincarnation) | Manhwa | Fantasy kingdom | Isekai + agency | | [I'll Be the Matriarch](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/ill-be-the-matriarch) | Manhwa | Noble house | Ambition + romance | | [My Next Life as a Villainess](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/my-next-life-as-villainess) | Manga | Otome world | Comedy isekai | | [Black Clover](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/black-clover) | Manga | Magic kingdom | Action + romance | | [The Lady and the Beast](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-lady-and-the-beast) | Manhwa | Fantasy | Slow trust-building | --- ## FAQ **What's the difference between isekai and fantasy romance?** Isekai involves a character transported to another world. Fantasy romance is broader — it includes stories set in original fantasy worlds without the transport premise. **Which villainess manhwa should I start with?** [The Abandoned Empress](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/the-abandoned-empress) or [My Next Life as a Villainess](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/my-next-life-as-villainess) — both are polished, complete or nearly complete, and excellent entry points. --- --- # 5. If You Like Historical Romance, Read These Stories ![Historical Romance Cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1618556264157-b27a09f0f891?w=1200&h=400&fit=crop&q=80) *Cover image: Historical romance — love stories set against the weight of tradition and time.* Historical romance manga and manhwa use period setting not just as backdrop but as genuine constraint. Social rules, class structures, political marriages, and gender dynamics of historical periods create tensions that contemporary settings simply can't replicate. When two people manage to connect across those barriers, it carries different weight. The genre spans Meiji-era Japan, Joseon-era Korea, fictional imperial China, and stylized European medieval settings — each with its own particular flavor of forbidden and complicated. ---

title: 10 Historical Romance Series Worth Reading
excerpt: By Yumi Tamura  Manga  Completed  27 Volumes One of the greatest manga of the 1990s, full stop. A post-apocalyptic Japan where a woman assumes her dead brother's prophetic role. The romance at its center — between two people on opposite sides of a war who don't initially know who
body: # 10 Historical Romance Series Worth Reading ### 🏯 1. [Basara](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/basara) ![Basara](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Yumi Tamura | Manga | Completed | 27 Volumes* One of the greatest manga of the 1990s, full stop. A post-apocalyptic Japan where a woman assumes her dead brother's prophetic role. The romance at its center — between two people on opposite sides of a war who don't initially know who the other is — is one of manga's finest. *Basara* does everything: political intrigue, war, identity, sacrifice, and a love story that genuinely drives the plot. Required reading for anyone serious about manga. --- ### 🏯 2. [The Story of Saiunkoku](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/story-of-saiunkoku) ![Story of Saiunkoku](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Sai Yukino & Kairi Yura | Manga | Completed* Set in a fictional historical China. Shurei Hong becomes a court lady and later one of the empire's first female officials. The romance is secondary to her professional ambitions — which makes it more interesting, not less. The way the manga handles female ambition in a historical setting feels surprisingly modern. A full cast of memorable male characters orbit Shurei in ways that develop their own stories without undermining hers. --- ### 🏯 3. [Rurouni Kenshin](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/rurouni-kenshin) ![Rurouni Kenshin](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Nobuhiro Watsuki | Manga | Completed | 28 Volumes* Meiji-era Japan, a former assassin trying to live peacefully, a sword school girl who draws him into protecting her. The romance between Kenshin and Kaoru develops slowly across a historical backdrop that Watsuki clearly researched — the Meiji transition period gives the story a genuine sense of an era in flux. The romance works because both characters have weight and history of their own. --- ### 🏯 4. [Lady Rose Wants to Be a Commoner](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/lady-rose-commoner) ![Lady Rose](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578662996442-48f60103fc96?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Ongoing* A noblewoman who knows she's in a romance novel actively tries to escape her role and live as a normal person. Funny, self-aware, and the historical setting is used cleverly to highlight how restrictive aristocratic life actually is. The romance develops between her attempts to disappear from high society, and the male lead is patient in interesting rather than irritating ways. --- ### 🏯 5. [The Scholar's Reincarnation](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/scholars-reincarnation) ![Scholar's Reincarnation](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1588421357574-87938a86fa28?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By JUDER | Manhwa | Completed* A martial arts master reincarnates as the infant son of his nemesis in a historical Korean setting. The family dynamics are complex and the romance develops as the protagonist grows up navigating who he was and who he's becoming. Strong art and solid pacing make this one of the better historical reincarnation manhwa. --- ### 🏯 6. [Vinland Saga](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/vinland-saga) ![Vinland Saga](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1618556264157-b27a09f0f891?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Makoto Yukimura | Manga | Ongoing* Viking-age historical manga — primarily action, but the quieter emotional threads around Thorfinn's relationships carry genuine romantic undertones. Included here because the historical authenticity is exceptional and the emotional relationships feel true to the period rather than modernized for comfort. --- ### 🏯 7. [Taisho Otome Fairy Tale](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/taisho-otome-fairy-tale) ![Taisho Otome](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1607604276583-eef5d076aa5f?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Sana Kirioka | Manga | Completed | 4 Volumes* Taisho-era Japan. A disinherited boy sent to the countryside gains a young wife arranged by his family. What sounds potentially dark is actually remarkably wholesome — Yuzuki is determined to care for Tamahiko, who has given up on life, and the romance is about him slowly choosing to live again. Short, sweet, and historically warm without ignoring the reality of the period. --- ### 🏯 8. [In the Name of the Mermaid Princess](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/mermaid-princess) ![Mermaid Princess](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614332287897-cdc485fa562d?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Ongoing* Historical fantasy hybrid set in a fictional imperial court with strong influence from Joseon-era Korea. A young woman connected to legendary bloodlines navigates court politics and a romance with genuine stakes. The costume design and panel composition are exceptional. --- ### 🏯 9. [A Returner's Magic Should Be Special](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/returners-magic) ![Returner's Magic](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *By Usonan & Wookjakga | Manhwa | Ongoing* Historical-fantasy setting where a mage returns to the past to prevent a catastrophic future. The romance threads are carefully paced against the action and the historical fantasy world is richly built. For readers who want their period romance inside a substantial action-magic system. --- ### 🏯 10. [The Flower That Was Bloomed by a Cloud](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/flower-bloomed-by-cloud) ![Flower That Bloomed by a Cloud](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1578662996442-48f60103fc96?w=800&h=250&fit=crop&q=80) *Manhwa | Completed* Set in a fictional historical Chinese-influenced court. A woman with a tragic background navigates imperial politics and an unexpected romance with an imperial prince who isn't what court rumors suggest. The art is detailed and the political structure of the court is one of the better-realized in the genre. --- ## Quick Reference Table | Title | Period | Medium | Tone | |---|---|---|---| | [Basara](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/basara) | Post-apocalyptic Japan | Manga | Epic, sweeping | | [Story of Saiunkoku](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/story-of-saiunkoku) | Fictional imperial China | Manga | Political + warm | | [Rurouni Kenshin](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/rurouni-kenshin) | Meiji Japan | Manga | Historical action | | [Lady Rose](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/lady-rose-commoner) | Fictional European | Manhwa | Self-aware comedy | | [Scholar's Reincarnation](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/scholars-reincarnation) | Joseon Korea | Manhwa | Reincarnation action | | [Vinland Saga](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/vinland-saga) | Viking age | Manga | Action, emotional | | [Taisho Otome](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/taisho-otome-fairy-tale) | Taisho Japan | Manga | Gentle, wholesome | | [Mermaid Princess](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/mermaid-princess) | Fictional Joseon | Manhwa | Court intrigue | | [Returner's Magic](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/returners-magic) | Fantasy historical | Manhwa | Action + romance | | [Flower Bloomed by Cloud](https://yourwebsite.com/manhwa/flower-bloomed-by-cloud) | Fictional imperial China | Manhwa | Court politics | --- ## FAQ **Is historical romance usually set in Japan or Korea?** Both, plus fictional settings inspired by historical China or generic medieval Europe. Manhwa tends toward Joseon-era Korean settings or fictional Chinese imperial courts. Manga leans toward Edo/Meiji Japan or fantasy medieval Europe. **Are there historical romance manga with strong female leads?** [Basara](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/basara) and [The Story of Saiunkoku](https://yourwebsite.com/manga/story-of-saiunkoku) both feature exceptional female protagonists who drive their stories. --- --- # 6. If You Like Office Romance, Read These Manhwa ![Office Romance Cover](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541963463532-d68292c34b19?w=1200&h=400&fit=crop&q=80) *Cover image: Office romance — professional tension, late nights, and everything left unsaid.* Office romance manhwa hits a demographic that school romance can't reach: working adults who remember their school manga days and want something that reflects where they are now. The genre is dominated by manhwa — there's something in the webtoon format's connection to Korean work culture that makes the office setting feel native and specific. The best entries don't pretend professional relationships are uncomplicated. Hierarchy, power imbalance, workplace gossip, and career stakes are all real factors that the better series grapple with honestly. ---
