# Upcoming Manga to Watch in 2026

![Cover Image](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1587502537104-aac10f5fb6f7?w=1200&q=80&alt=Upcoming+Manga+to+Watch+2026)
*The manga landscape in 2026 is rich with continuations, new launches, and adaptations generating major attention. Here's what to track.*

**Category:** Reading Guide | **Updated:** 2026 | **Read Time:** ~11 min

---

## The Manga Scene in 2026

The post-pandemic manga boom normalized reading habits that have fundamentally changed the market. Digital consumption is dominant, simultaneous global releases are standard, and the gap between manga publication and English-language availability has effectively closed for major titles.

For 2026, the stories driving most of the conversation fall into three categories: major ongoing series in crucial arcs, returning series after hiatuses, and new launches that industry observers flagged during late 2025 preview season.

---

## Major Ongoing Series in Critical 2026 Arcs

### Berserk — The Fantasia Arc

**[→ Follow Berserk on our site](/manga/berserk)**

The manga world has watched Berserk's continuation with a mix of hope and careful attention since Kentaro Miura's death in 2021. Kouji Mori, Miura's closest friend and a manga author himself, committed to continuing the series using Miura's notes and discussions. Studio Gaga (Miura's team) continues the art.

2026 sees the Fantasia arc — Elfheim, Guts's struggle with the Berserker Armor, and the larger mythological confrontation — continuing at a careful pace. Whether this is the ending Miura envisioned remains unanswerable, but the care being taken is evident.

**Why to watch:** This is one of manga's most significant ongoing stories. However it ends, the ending will be discussed for decades.

---

### Chainsaw Man Part 2

**[→ Follow Chainsaw Man on our site](/manga/chainsaw-man)**

Fujimoto's school arc in Part 2 is doing something genuinely interesting with Denji's character in a context that looks different from Part 1 on the surface but is exploring similar questions about identity, love, and what people sacrifice for connection.

2026 brings what appears to be Part 2's escalation into its larger threat — and Fujimoto's tendency to recontextualize everything the reader thought they knew is fully intact.

**Why to watch:** Fujimoto is one of manga's most interesting active authors. Whatever he's building toward in Part 2 will not be what you expect.

---

### Vinland Saga — Baltic Arc

**[→ Follow Vinland Saga on our site](/manga/vinland-saga)**

The current arc explores territory north of England and the Viking slave trade with the same meticulous historical research Yukimura brings to every arc. Thorfinn's pacifist mission is being tested in increasingly direct ways.

**Why to watch:** Each Vinland Saga arc is better than the last. The Baltic material is no exception.

---

## New Launches to Watch (2026)

### Ghost Cat Anzu (English Release)

**[→ Read Ghost Cat Anzu on our site](/manga/ghost-cat-anzu)**

The film adaptation from 2024 introduced Western audiences to this heartwarming supernatural slice-of-life. 2026 sees wider English availability of the source manga, which has a warmth and visual specificity worth experiencing in its original form.

---

### Goodbye, Eri — Standalone Watch

**[→ Read Goodbye Eri on our site](/manga/goodbye-eri)**

Fujimoto's one-shot from 2022 continues to circulate as essential reading for anyone interested in what manga can do with the form itself. If you somehow haven't read it yet, 2026 is as good a time as any — it takes 20 minutes and will stay with you for much longer.

---

### New Shonen Jump Launches (Q1-Q2 2026)

Weekly Shonen Jump's 2025-2026 launch window included several series worth tracking:

- Series addressing post-apocalyptic themes with school-setting twists
- The continued rise of "system" manga (inspired by manhwa's RPG-mechanics crossover)
- Historical action series drawing from Tokugawa-era Japan

**[→ Check our New Releases page for 2026 Shonen Jump series](/new-releases)**

---

## 2026 Manga Adaptations Worth Knowing

Major anime adaptations of manga source material arriving in 2026 will drive new readership to their source:

Several 2026 adaptation announcements incentivize reading the manga first, as adaptation audiences typically find the source richer in detail and nuance.

**[→ Check our Anime Adaptation Tracker](/anime-adaptations)**

---

## FAQs

**Q: How do I keep up with new manga releases in 2026?**
Our [New Releases page](/new-releases) tracks weekly Shonen Jump, Shonen Magazine, and major digital releases. Enable notifications for the series you follow via your [account settings](/account).

**Q: Is Berserk's continuation by Mori/Studio Gaga faithful to Miura's vision?**
This is genuinely unknown and perhaps unknowable. Mori has been explicit that he's using Miura's notes and their years of conversations as his guide. What's been published since 2022 has generally been received as respectful to the source material, though naturally without the certainty that comes from Miura's own hand.

---

# Upcoming Manhwa to Watch in 2026

![Cover Image](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1560169897-fc0cdbdfa4d5?w=1200&q=80&alt=Upcoming+Manhwa+to+Watch+2026)
*The Korean webtoon industry shows no signs of slowing. Here's where the action is in 2026.*

**Category:** Reading Guide | **Updated:** 2026 | **Read Time:** ~10 min

---

## Manhwa in 2026: A Market Ascending

Korean webtoons have become a genuinely global industry. The Webtoon platform's expansion, LINE Manga's growth in Japan, and Tapas and Tappytoon serving English-language markets have created an infrastructure where successful Korean webtoons reach millions of international readers within days of publication.

The industry is generating more content than ever — which means more to sort through, but also more genuine innovation as creators experiment with format, genre, and tone.

---

## Ongoing Series in Crucial 2026 Chapters

### Tower of God — Final Chapters?

**[→ Follow Tower of God on our site](/manhwa/tower-of-god)**

SIU has been building toward what appears to be the story's final major confrontation between Bam and the King of the Tower for years. 2026 may bring the beginning of that end, though SIU's health hiatus history means pacing is never guaranteed.

**Why it matters:** Tower of God is one of the longest-running and most beloved webtoons ever published. Whatever the ending looks like, it will be a cultural event for manhwa fandom.

---

### Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint — Post-Completion Expansion?

**[→ Follow Omniscient Reader on our site](/manhwa/omniscient-readers-viewpoint)**

ORV completed its main story. The question in 2026 is whether the IP — which has expanded into a novel, audio drama, and major film/drama projects — will generate supplementary manhwa content. Watch for announcements.

---

### The Beginning After the End — Adaptation Tracking

**[→ Follow TBATE on our site](/manhwa/beginning-after-end)**

The completed manhwa's IP has been explored for adaptation across multiple formats. 2026 is expected to bring significant adaptation news for TBATE. Follow our [Adaptation News](/adaptations) page for updates.

- New titles from authors with strong track records in action manhwa

# Most Anticipated New Manga Series in 2026

![Cover Image](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1614065097520-4f2ae7bc3e82?w=1200&q=80&alt=Most+Anticipated+New+Manga+Series+2026)
*New manga that's earned genuine anticipation in 2026 — from promising debuts to major industry launches.*

**Category:** Reading Guide | **Updated:** 2026 | **Read Time:** ~10 min

---

## How "Anticipated" Gets Earned

Not every new series generates legitimate anticipation — most of it is marketing. Real anticipation in manga fandom comes from: an author with a strong prior track record launching something new, serialization in a high-prestige magazine that signals editorial backing, preview chapters that show unusual ambition, or word-of-mouth from early readers in Japan that's traveled to international communities.

This list only covers series where at least two of those factors are present.

---

## 1. New Works From Established Authors

### The Next Project From Tatsuki Fujimoto

**[→ Follow Fujimoto's new works on our site](/manga/tatsuki-fujimoto)**

After Look Back (2021), Goodbye Eri (2022), and Chainsaw Man Part 2, Fujimoto has demonstrated consistent willingness to experiment with form, length, and tone. Any new serialization or one-shot announcement from him generates significant legitimate anticipation.

Industry tracking in late 2025 suggested a new standalone project was in development. Details have been carefully managed — which is itself a signal of how seriously Shueisha is treating the release.

---

### Post-Blue Period Work From Tsubasa Yamaguchi

**[→ Follow Yamaguchi's upcoming works on our site](/manga/tsubasa-yamaguchi)**

Blue Period concluded in 2025 as one of the decade's most celebrated slice-of-life manga. The art community that the series cultivated is deeply invested in what Yamaguchi does next. Early 2026 has seen hints of a new project in a different genre — potentially historical.

---

## 2. Major Magazine New Launches (2026)

### Shonen Jump — New Genre Experiments

WSJ's editorial team has been deliberately seeking manga that addresses the system/RPG-mechanics genre from a Japan-native perspective, responding to the influence manhwa has had on Japanese reader tastes. Several 2025 launches are evolving into significant 2026 series.

**[→ Track all current Shonen Jump series on our site](/shonen-jump-tracker)**

---

### Shonen Magazine — Historical and Sports Expansion

Shonen Magazine's historical action tradition (Fairy Tail, Akame ga Kill, Vinland Saga) continues with new launches in 2026 addressing Edo-era Japan and World War II-adjacent historical settings.

---

## 3. Adaptation-Generating Manga to Read Now

Several manga will receive major anime adaptations in 2026-2027, meaning reading them now puts you ahead of the conversation that's coming:

- **Dungeon Meshi (Season 2):** Read ahead of the second season currently airing
- **Chainsaw Man Part 2:** The adaptation timeline is expected to catch up to the current manga in 2026-2027
- **Frieren: Beyond Journey's End:** Season 2 is coming; the manga is substantially ahead

**[→ Full Anime Adaptation Calendar](/anime-adaptations/2026)**

---

## 4. Debut Authors Worth Following

The manga industry's talent pipeline remains strong. 2026 sees several debut authors who earned significant attention during their serialization trials (Shonen Jump's JUMP START system and equivalents) or who built audiences through web serialization before print publication.

Keep an eye on:

- Authors making the jump from web serialization to magazine publication
- Winners of the 2025 Gold Future Cup and equivalent talent competitions
- Creators who built significant social media followings on shorter work

**[→ New Author Spotlight on our site](/new-authors)**

---

# Most Anticipated New Manhwa Series in 2026

![Cover Image](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1541701494587-cb58502866ab?w=1200&q=80&alt=Most+Anticipated+New+Manhwa+Series+2026)
*Korean webtoon creators are pushing the format into new territory in 2026. Here's what's generating real buzz.*

**Category:** Reading Guide | **Updated:** 2026 | **Read Time:** ~10 min

---

## The Korean Webtoon Industry's 2026 Moment

The Korean webtoon industry has become sophisticated enough that anticipation cycles — the pre-launch discourse, the first-chapter reaction, the early reviews — now closely resemble those of mainstream publishing. Platform exclusives, author announcements, and preview chapter drops generate genuine community excitement in ways that were rare even five years ago.

2026's most anticipated new manhwa share a few common threads: they're being created by authors with established track records, they're launching on premium platforms with significant promotional investment, or they're representing genre experiments that fill clear gaps in what's currently available.

---

## 1. Returns From Hiatus — High-Anticipation Comebacks

### Tower of God Author SIU

**[→ Follow Tower of God on our site](/manhwa/tower-of-god)**

SIU's health has forced multiple Tower of God hiatuses over the years. Each return generates enormous fandom response. 2026 continuation chapters are expected with cautious optimism.

---

### True Beauty Creator Yaongyi's New Project

**[→ Follow Yaongyi's new works on our site](/manhwa/yaongyi-new-work)**

Yaongyi's next project after True Beauty's completion has been announced in broad strokes. The genre appears to be different from True Beauty — darker and more dramatically complex. Given True Beauty's enormous readership, whatever comes next will be closely watched.

---

## 2. Platform-Exclusive Launch Announcements

Naver, Kakao, and LINE have all significantly increased investment in exclusive content for 2026, including:

- Multi-volume guarantees for authors with proven track records
- Animation-first development deals that start as manhwa
- Cross-format projects where the manhwa and a drama develop simultaneously

The cross-media model is particularly interesting — it means some of 2026's most anticipated manhwa launches are also simultaneously in development as streaming dramas.

**[→ Cross-Media Manhwa Tracker](/manhwa/adaptations)**

---

## 3. Genre Spaces to Watch

### Post-ORV Literary Fantasy

Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint created an audience for manhwa that functions as literary fantasy — emotionally complex, thematically rich, formally aware. 2026 has at least two new series attempting to occupy this space.

**[→ Literary Fantasy Manhwa Recommendations](/recommendations/literary-manhwa)**

---

### Second-Generation Villainess Isekai

The first wave of villainess isekai (Villainess Reverses the Hourglass, Remarried Empress, Beware the Villainess) created a template. 2026's new entries in the genre are notable for subverting the template: protagonists who are genuinely morally grey, villainess scenarios that engage with systemic rather than personal antagonism, and romance that takes longer to materialize and is more complicated when it does.

**[→ Villainess Manhwa Reading Guide](/reading-guides/villainess-manhwa)**

---

### Action-Romance Hybrid

The genre intersection that's generated the most reader interest in late 2025 and early 2026 is action-romance: series where a romantic central relationship and genuinely excellent fight sequences share equal narrative weight. Neither element is subordinate to the other.

**[→ Action Romance Manhwa Recommendations](/recommendations/action-romance-manhwa)**

---

## How to Stay Updated on New Manhwa in 2026

1. **Follow our [New Releases](/new-releases) page** — updated weekly with new chapter releases and series launches
2. **Enable notifications** for specific series via your [account page](/account)
3. **Check our [Platform Guides](/platforms)** for where to read specific manhwa legally in English
4. **Subscribe to our newsletter** for curated monthly roundups of new and notable launches

---

## FAQs

**Q: Where is the best place to discover new manhwa series in 2026?**
Platform-native discovery on Webtoon and Kakao has improved significantly. Our [New Releases tracker](/new-releases) curates across platforms so you don't have to monitor each one separately.

**Q: Are there manhwa series that started in 2025 worth picking up now?**
Yes — several 2025 launches are now into their story-establishing arcs (typically chapters 20-50) where you can assess whether the premise pays off. Check our [2025-2026 Series Spotlight](/series-spotlight) for recommendations.

**Q: How long does it typically take for a Korean manhwa to be translated to English?**
Major platform titles (Webtoon, Tapas) release simultaneously in Korean and English. Premium titles on Tappytoon may have 1-2 episode delays. Unofficial translations appear faster but reading on licensed platforms supports the creators.
